lsj_entry_text: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο, gen. τούτου, ταύτης, τούτου, etc.: the dual fem. never in Att. , v. ὁ, ἡ, τό, init.:—demonstr. Pron., this, common from Hom. downwds. ORIGIN and FORMS: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο prob. arose from a reduplication of the demonstr. ὁ, ἡ , τό with insertion of -υ- (= Skt. Particle u), e.g. ταῦτα fr. τα-υ-τα: Dor. gen. sg. fem. τούτας Philol. 11 ; nom. pl. τοῦτοι, ταῦται A.D. Synt. 111.23 : the former occurs Sophr. 24 , GDI 3045 B 6 (Selinus), SIG 339.16 (Rhodes, iii B. C.), etc., the latter is dub. in Sophr. 97 , certain in SIG 241 B 117 (Delph., iv B. C.): in Boeot. all forms begin with οὑτ-, as gen. sg. neut. οὕτω Supp.Epigr. 3.359.11 (iii B. C.); acc. sg. fem. οὕταν Corinn. Supp. 2.80 ; acc. pl. neut. οὗτα SIG 1185.20 (Tanagra, iii B. C.), etc.: gen. pl. fem. Att. τούτων, Cret. ταυτᾶν Leg.Gort. 5.19 ; neut. ταύτων Michel 1334.10 (Elis, iv B. C.).—In Ion. sts. written ταότην, ταο ͂τα, SIG 283.19 (Chios, iv B. C.), 46.7 (Halic., v B. C.), al.—In Att. οὗτος was freq. strengthd. by the demonstr. -ί, οὑτοσί, αὑτηί, τουτί, gen. τουτουί, dat. τουτῳί, acc. τουτονί; pl. nom. οὑτοιί, neut. ταυτί, etc., this man here: sts. a Particle is inserted between the Pron. and -ί, as αὑτηγί for αὑτηί γε, Ar. Ach. 784 ; τουτογί for τουτί γε, Id. V. 781 , Av. 894 , al.; ταυταγί for ταυτί γε, Id. Eq. 492 , Pax 1057 , al.; τουτοδί for τουτὶ δέ, Id. Pl. 227 ; τουτουμενί for τουτουὶ μέν, Id. Ra. 965 .—In codd. the ν ἐφελκυστικόν is sts. added in the forms οὑτοσίν, οὑτωσίν, and οὑτοσίν is said to be Att. by A.D. Pron. 59.24 , 82.11 . [This ι is always long, and a long vowel or diphthong before it becomes short, as αὑτηί, τουτῳί, οὑτοιί, Ar. Nu. 201 , Pl. 44 , Ach. 40 , etc.] USAGE in regard to CONCOR D. οὗτος is freq. used as a Pron. Subst.: hence neut. is folld. by gen., κατὰ τοῦτο τῆς ἀκροπόλιος Hdt. 1.84 ; εἰς τοῦθ' ὕβρεως ἐλήλυθεν D. 4.37 ; εἰς τοῦθ' ἥκεις μανίας Id. 36.48 ; ταῦτα τῶν μαθημάτων Pl. Euthd. 278b : but quite as freq. as Adj., in which case its Subst. commonly takes the Art., οὗτος ὁ ἀνήρ or ὁ ἀνὴρ οὗτος.—But the Art. is absent, always in Ep. Poets (exc. Od. 18.114 ), οὗτος ἀνήρ Il. 14.471 , Od. 1.406 , etc.: sts. also in Trag., A. Pers. 122 (lyr.), 495 , S. Ph. 406 , OC 471 , 1177 : once in an Inscr., τοπεῖα: τούτων τὰ ἡμίσεα τοπείων IG 22.1622.135 (iv B. C.). sts. when the Noun is so specified that the Art. is not needed, ἐς γῆν ταύτην . . , ἥντινα νῦν Σκύθαι νέμονται Hdt. 4.8 ; ταύτας ἃς οἱ πατέρες παρέδοσαν μελέτας Th. 1.85 , cf. Pl. R. 449d , etc.; πατὴρ σὸς οὗτος, ὃν θρηνεῖς ἀεί S. El. 530 . when οὗτος is used in local sense, here, v. infr. c. 1.5 . when the Noun with which οὗτος agrees stands as its Predicate, αὕτη γὰρ ἦν σοι πρόφασις S. Ph. 1034 ; δικαστοῦ αὕτη ἀρετή [ἐστι] Pl. Ap. 18a : this exception extends to cases in which the Predicate is not so distinctly separated from the Subject, αἰτίαι μὲν αὗται προυγεγένηντο these were the grievances which already existed, Th. 1.66 ; ταύτην φήμην παρέδοσαν this was the report which . . , Pl. Phlb. 16c : freq. with a Sup. , κίνησις αὕτη μεγίστη δὴ . . ἐγένετο this was notably the greatest movement which . . , Th. 1.1 , cf. 3.113 : with πρῶτος Id. 1.55 , 98 , 6.31 , Ev.Luc. 2.2 . when 3rd pers. is used for 2nd to express contempt, οὗτος ἀνήρ, οὑτοσὶ ἀνήρ, Pl. Grg. 467b , 489b , etc. though οὗτος usu. agrees with the Noun that serves as Predicate, it is not rare to find it in the neut., μανία δὲ καὶ τοῦτ' ἐστί E. Ba. 305 ; τοῦτο γάρ εἰσι . . εὔθυναι D. 19.82 , etc.: and in pl., οὐκ ἔστι ταῦτα ἀρχή Aeschin. 3.13 ; ταῦτ' ἐστὶν ὁ προδότης Id. 2.166 : so with an explanatory clause added, τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν ὁ συκοφάντης, αἰτιᾶσθαι μὲν πάντα ἐξελέγξαι δὲ μηδέν D. 57.34 . so also with a Noun in apposition, τούτοισιν μὲν ταῦτα μέλει, κίθαρις καὶ ἀοιδή Od. 1.159 ; τούτου τιμῶμαι, ἐν πρυτανείῳ σιτήσεως Pl. Ap. 36e , cf. E. Fr. 323.3 , etc. the neut. also may refer to a masc. or fem. Noun, καρπὸν φορέει κυάμῳ ἴσον: τοῦτο ἐπεὰν γένηται πέπον κτλ. Hdt. 4.23 , cf. X. An. 1.5.10 , etc. the neut. is also used of classes of persons, μελιτοπῶλαι καὶ τυροπῶλαι: τοῦτο δ' εἰς ἕν ἐστι συγκεκυφός Ar. Eq. 854 , cf. Pl. Lg. 711a ; or of an abstract fact, οὐκ Ἰοφῶν ζῇ;—τοῦτο γάρ τοι καὶ μόνον ἔτ' ἐστὶ λοιπὸν ἀγαθόν Ar. Ra. 73 . with Prons., personal, οὗτος σύ, in local sense, v. infr. c. 1.5 . interrog., τί τοῦτ' ἔλεξας; what is this that . . ? S. Ph. 1173 (lyr.), cf. Ant. 7 ; ποίοισι τούτοις; for ποῖά ἐστι ταῦτα οἷς [ἔχεις ἐλπίδα]; Id. OC 388 , cf. Ant. 1049 ; Νέστορ' ἔρειο ὅν τινα τοῦτον ἄγει whom he brings here, Il. 11.612 . with οἷος, Od. 20.377 , Pl. Phd. 61c . possess., πατὴρ σὸς οὗτος this father of thine, S. El. 530 , cf. X. An. 7.3.30 . demonstr., οὗτος ἐκεῖνος, τὸν σὺ ζητέεις, where ἐκεῖνος is the Predicate, Hdt. 1.32 ; τοῦτ' ἔστ' ἐκεῖνο E. Hel. 622 , cf. Or. 804 ; αὐτὸ τοῦτο, v. αὐτός 1.7; τοῦτον τὸν αὐτὸν ἄνδρα this same man, S. Ph. 128 . exceptionally, Διφίλου οὗτος ὅδ' ἐστὶ τύπος IG 12(5).300 (Paros). ἄλλος τις οὗτος ἀνέστη another man here, Od. 20.380 . with Numerals, τέθνηκε ταῦτα τρία ἔτη these three years, Lys. 7.10c odd.; [στρατείαν] ἑνδέκατον μῆνα τουτονὶ ποιεῖται for these eleven months, D. 8.2 , cf. 3.4 ; τριακοστὴν ταύτην ἡμέραν Men. Epit. 27 ; ταύτας τριάκοντα μνᾶς D. 27.23 , cf. Pl. Grg. 463b , etc. SIGNIFICATION AND SPECIAL IDIOMS: this, to designate the nearer, opp. ἐκεῖνος, that, the more remote, ταῦτα, like τὰ ἐνταῦθα , things round and about us, earthly things, Pl. Phd. 75e (v. l.); cf. ὅδε init.: but οὗτος sts. indicates that which is not really nearest, but most important, δεῖ . . τὸ βέλτιστον ἀεί, μὴ τὸ ῥᾷστον λέγειν: ἐπὶ ἐκεῖνο μὲν γὰρ ἡ φύσις αὐτὴ βαδιεῖται, ἐπὶ τοῦτο δὲ κτλ. D. 8.72 , cf. 51.3 and 18 . when, of two things, one precedes and the other follows, ὅδε prop. refers to what follows, οὗτος to what precedes, οὐκ ἔστι σοι ταῦτ', ἀλλά σοι τάδ' ἔστι S. OC 787 , cf. ὅδε III. 2 : freq., however, where there are not two things, οὗτος refers to what follows, Il. 13.377 , Od. 2.306 , etc.; οὔκουν . . τοῦτο γιγνώσκεις, ὅτι . . ; A. Pr. 379 , etc. οὗτος is used emphat., generally in contempt, while ἐκεῖνος denotes praise, ὁ πάντ' ἄναλκις οὗτος, i.e. Aegisthus, S. El. 301 ; τούτους τοὺς συκοφάντας Pl. Cri. 45a ; so D. de Coron. uses οὗτος of Aeschines, ἐκεῖνος of Philip; but οὗτος is used of Philip, D. 2.15 , 4.3 . of what is familiar, τούτους τοὺς πολυτελεῖς χιτῶνας, of the Persians, X. An. 1.5.8 ; οἱ τὰς τελετὰς . . οὗτοι καταστήσαντες Pl. Phd. 69c , cf. Men. 80a ; τὸ θυλακῶδες τοῦτο the familiar bag-like thing, Thphr. HP 3.7.3 , cf. 3.18.11 , 4.7.1 ; οἱ τὰς κόρας ταύτας ὠνούμενοι τοῖς παισίν D.Chr. 31.153 . in Att. law-language, οὗτος is commonly applied to the opponent, whether plaintiff (as in Aeschin. 2.130 ) or defendant (as in Id. 1.1 ); so, in the political speeches of D. , οὗτοι are the opposite party, 4.1 , 8.7 , etc.; but in the forensic speeches, οὗτοι freq. means the judges, the court, 21.134 , 36.47 . much like an Adv., in local sense (cf. ὅδε init.), τίς δ' οὗτος κατὰ νῆας . . ἔρχεαι; who art thou here that comest . . ? Il. 10.82 ; freq. in Att. , τίς οὑτοσί; who's this here? Ar. Ach. 1048 ; πολλὰ ὁρῶ ταῦτα πρόβατα I see many sheep here, X. An. 3.5.9 (as v.l.): with Pron. of 2 pers., οὗτος σύ ho you! you there! S. OT 532 , 1121 , E. Hec. 1280 , etc.: and then οὗτος alone like a voc., οὗτος, τί ποιεῖς; A. Supp. 911 ,cf. S. Aj. 71 , E. Alc. 773 , Ar. Eq. 240 , Nu. 220 , al.: with a pr. n., ὦ οὗτος, Αἴας S. Aj. 89 ; ὦ οὗτος οὗτος, Οἰδίπους Id. OC 1627 , cf. Ar. V. 1364 : with voc., βέντισθ' οὗτος Theoc. 5.76 :—the fem. is rarer, αὕτη E. Med. 922 ; αὕτη σύ Ar. Th. 610 .—This phrase mostly implies anger, impatience, or scorn. simply as antec. to ὅς, Od. 2.40 , S. OT 1180 , etc.: freq. following relat. clause, ἅ γ' ἔλαβες, . . μεθεῖναι ταῦτα Id. Ph. 1247 , cf. 1319 , Ant. 183 , 203 , Pl. Grg. 469c . = τοιοῦτος, οὗτος ἐγὼ ταχυτᾶτι Pi. O. 4.26 ; σὺ τοίνυν οὗτος εὑρέθης D. 18.282 , cf. 173 . after a parenthesis, the Subject, though already named, is freq. emphat. repeated by οὗτος, οὐδὲ γὰρ οὐδὲ Ἀριστέης . . , οὐδὲ οὗτος προσωτέρω . . ἔφησε ἀπικέσθαι Hdt. 4.16 , cf. 81 (s. v. l.), 1.146 , Pl. Phd. 107d , etc. καὶ οὗτος is added to heighten the force of a previous word, ξυνεστῶτες . . ναυτικῷ ἀγῶνι, καὶ τούτῳ πρὸς Ἀθηναίους Th. 4.55 , cf. Hdt. 1.147 , 6.11 , etc.; so οὐδὲ τούτου Aeschin. 2.100 ; v. infr. VIII. 2 . repeated, where for the second we should merely say he or it, τοῖσιν τούτου τοῦτον μέλεσιν . . κελαδοῦντες Ar. Ra. 1526 , cf. Pl. La. 200d . ταῦτα is used in some special phrases, ταῦτ', ὦ δέσποτα yes Sir (i. e. ἔστι ταῦτα, ταῦτα δράσω, etc.), Ar. V. 142 , Pax 275 , cf. Eq.III; so ταῦτα δή Id. Ach. 815 ; ταῦτά νυν Id. V. 1008 ; so also ἦν ταῦτα even so, true, E. Ph. 417 . ταῦτα μὲν δὴ ὑπάρξει so it shall be, Pl. Phd. 78a . καὶ ταῦτα μὲν δὴ ταῦτα so much for that, freq. in Att. , as Pl. Smp. 220c . ταῦτα at end of a formula in epitaphs, etc., prob. short for ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχει or ὁ βίος ταῦτά ἐστιν, e.g. οὐδὶς ( = -εὶς ) ἀθάνατος: ταῦτα IG 14.420 ; Προκόπι ταῦτα ib. 1824 ; χαίρεται ( = -τε ) ταῦτα ib. 1479 , etc.: similarly perh. in a letter, ἂμ μὴ πέμψῃς, οὐ μὴ φάγω, οὐ μὴ πείνω. ταῦτα POxy. 119.15 (ii/iii A. D.). Adverbial usages: ταῦταabs., therefore, that is why . . , Il. 11.694 ; ταῦτ' ἄρα Ar. Ach. 90 , Nu. 319 , 335 , 394 , al., X. Smp. 4.55 ; ταῦτα δή A. Pers. 159 , Pl. Smp. 174a ; ταῦτ' οὖν S. Tr. 550 , Ar. V. 1358 , etc.; αὐτὰ ταῦτα ἥκω, ἵνα . . Pl. Prt. 310e : τοῦτο is rare in this sense, τοῦτ' ἀφικόμην, ὅπως . . εὖ πράξαιμί τι S. OT 1005 ; αὐτὸ γὰρ τοῦτο just because of this, Pl. Smp. 204a . πρὸς ταῦτα so then, therefore, prop. used in indignant defiance, A. Pr. 992 , 1043 , S. Aj. 971 , 1115 , 1313 , OT 426 , OC 455 , etc. καὶ ταῦτα, adding a circumstance heightening the force of what has been said, and that, ἄνδρα γενναῖον θανεῖν, καὶ ταῦτα πρὸς γυναικός A. Eu. 627 : but mostly with a part., ὅς γ' ἐξέλυσας ἄστυ . . , καὶ ταῦθ' ὑφ' ἡμῶν οὐδὲν ἐξειδὼς πλέον S. OT 37 , cf. Ar. Ra. 704 , Pl. Phdr. 241e , etc.; or with a part. omitted, ἥτις . . τὴν τεκοῦσαν ὕβρισεν, καὶ ταῦτα τηλικοῦτος (sc. οὖσα) S. El. 614 ; so καὶ ταῦτα μέντοι Pl. Erx. 400b . καὶ ταῦτα anyhow, no matter what happens (or happened), ἐπεχείρησας, οὐδὲν ὢν καὶ ταῦτα you tried, but were no good anyhow, i.e. try as you might, Id. R. 341c , cf. Diod.Com. 3.5 . τοῦτο μέν . . , τοῦτο δέ . . on the one hand . . , on the other . . , partly . . , partly . . , very freq. in Hdt. , as 1.161 , al.; τοῦτο μέν is sts. answered by δέ only, 4.76 , S. Aj. 670 , OC 440 ; by δὲ αὖ, Hdt. 7.176 ; by ἔπειτα δέ, S. Ant. 61 ; by ἀλλά, D. 22.13 ; by εἶτα, S. Ph. 1345 ; by τοῦτ' αὖθις, Id. Ant. 165 . dat. fem. ταύτῃ, on this spot, here, ταύτῃ μὲν . . , τῇδε δ' αὖ . . Id. Ph. 1331 ; ἀλλ' ἐὰν ταύτῃ γε νικᾷ, ταυτῃὶ πεπλήξεται Ar. Eq. 271 , cf. Th. 1221 . in this point, herein, μηδὲν ταύτῃ γε κομήσῃς Id. Pl. 572 , cf. X. Hier. 7.12 , etc. in this way, thus, A. Pr. 191 , S. OC 1300 , etc.; οὐ . . ταῦτ' ἐστί πω ταύτῃ Ar. english_sentence_A: But reflecting again that cold has truly been said by Hippocrates to be hostile to the nerves, I recognised that the best drug for those wounded in the nerves would be whatever dries and is intermediate between heating and cooling, or has not departed far from the mean in the direction of heating.

english_sentence_A: For where one applies the drug to the bare nerve, there the aforesaid indication of the drugs that will be of benefit ought to be taken over in its pure form; but when the parts lying in front are unaffected, one must find a more fine-particled drug, so that its power is not exhausted beforehand by the bodies in between, but reaches into the depth.
english_sentence_B: For where one applies the drug to the bare nerve, there it was proper to adopt the indication already stated for the drugs that had been of benefit in its unmixed form.

Pass. οἴκημαι, as pres., οἱ ἐν τῇ ἠπείρῳ οἰκημένοι Ἕλληνες those who have been settled, i.e. those who dwell . . , Hdt. 1.27 ; οἱ ἐντὸς Ἅλυος ποταμοῦ οἰ. ib. 28 , cf. 8.115 ; also of cities, to be situated, lie, παρ' ὃν [ποταμὸν] Νίνος πόλις οἴκητο Id. 1.193 . manage, direct a household or a state, S. greek_sentence: ἐκ ταὐτοῦ δὲ γένους ὑπάρχει τοῖσδε καὶ ὁ τοῦ εὐφορβίου κατὰ τὰ δυτικὰ μέρη τῆς οἰκουμένης γεννώμενος, εἴτ’ ὀπὸν αὐτὸν εἴτ’ ἄλλο τι καλεῖν ἐθέλοι τις.
english_sentence_A: Of the same kind as these is also that of euphorbium, which is produced in the western parts of the inhabited world, whether one wishes to call it a juice or something else.
english_sentence_B: Of the same kind as these is also the sap of euphorbium produced in the western parts of the inhabited world, whether one wishes to call it a sap or something else.

greek_sentence: ἡμῖν δ’ ἀρκέσει καθ’ ὅλον τὸν λόγον εὐφόρβιον ὀνομάζειν τὸ φάρμακον τοῦτο, καθάπερ ἔθος ἤδη πᾶσίν ἐστιν.
english_sentence_A: For us it will suffice throughout the whole discourse to name this drug euphorbium, as is already the custom for everyone.
english_sentence_B: For our part it will suffice throughout the whole discussion to call this drug euphorbium, as is now the custom with everyone.

english_sentence_A: Chrysocolla too is fairly fine-particled.
english_sentence_B: Chrysocolla too is quite fine-particled.

english_sentence_A: For the recognition of perceptible things is perfected through continuous viewing, and the greatest proof of this is the case of twins, who seem to us to be indistinguishable but are not indistinguishable to those familiar with them, so that they do not pass unnoticed (παραδραμεῖν).

english_sentence_A: Now the material from herbs, shrubs and trees it is best to examine, before it is taken up out of the earth, at the stages of fruiting—impending, beginning, advancing and at full maturity.

english_sentence_A: For this continuous viewing of them will teach you at what season above all one would do well to gather them and, placing them in dry rooms, to preserve them, neither baked by the rays of the sun nor moistened by damp from the roof or the walls.

greek_sentence: γιγνώσκετε γὰρ, ὅπως ἐξ ἑκάστου τῶν ἐθνῶν τὰ κάλλιστά μοι διακομίζεται καθ’ ἕκαστον ἔτος φάρμακα διὰ τὸ τοὺς ἐπιτρίπτους ῥωποπώλας, παντοίως αὐτοῖς λυμαίνεσθαι.
english_sentence_A: For you know how the finest drugs are conveyed to me from each of the nations every year, because the wretched sellers of petty wares (ῥωποπῶλαι) corrupt them in every possible way.

greek_sentence: ὅστις οὖν βούλεται πανταχόθεν βοηθημάτων εὐπορεῖν, ἔμπειρος γενέσθω πάσης μὲν τῆς ἀπὸ τῶν φυτῶν ὕλης, πάσης δὲ τῆς ἀπὸ τῶν ζώων τε καὶ μετάλλων, ὅσα τε γεώδη σώματα χωρὶς μεταλλείας εἰς ἰατρικὴν χρῆσιν ἄγομεν, ὡς διαγινώσκειν αὐτῶν τά τε ἀκριβῆ καὶ τὰ νόθα, καὶ μετὰ τοῦτο γυμνασάσθω κατὰ τὴν ἐμὴν πραγματείαν, ἐν ᾗ περὶ τῆς δυνάμεως ἔγραψα τῶν ἁπλῶν φαρμάκων.

Epict. 1.1.1 ; δ. σκεπτική the doctrine of the Sceptics, S.E. M. 7.1 . a medicine, Timostr. 7 , etc.; δ. ἁπλαῖ Hp. Decent. 9 , Aret. CD 1.4 , etc.; δ. πολυφάρμακοι Plu. 2.403c , Gal. 13.365 : in pl., collection of formulae or prescriptions, Orib. 10.33 . action of medicines, περὶ τῆς ἁπλῶν φαρμάκων δ., title of work by Galen; also, potency, δυνάμει θερμά, ψυχρά, Id. 1.672 , al. magically potent substance or object, PMag.Leid.V. 8.12 : in pl., magical powers, Hld. 4.7 . force or meaning of a word, Lys. 10.7 , Pl. Cra. 394b , Diog.Oen. 12 , Phld. Sign. 31 , etc. phonetic value of sounds or letters, Plb. 10.47.8 , D.H. Comp. 12 , Luc. Jud.Voc. 5 , etc. worth or value of money, Th. 6.46 , 2.97 , Plu. Lyc. 9 , Sol. 15 . capability of existing or acting, potentiality, opp. actuality (ἐνέργεια), Arist. Metaph. 1047b31 , 1051a5 , etc.: hence δυνάμει as Adv., virtually, ὕστερον ὂν τῇ τάξει, πρότερον τῇ δυνάμει . . ἐστί D. 3.15 ; opp. ἐνεργείᾳ, Arist. APo. 86a28 , al.; opp. ἐντελεχείᾳ, Id. Ph. 193b8 , al. Math., power, κατὰ μεταφορὰν ἡ ἐν γεωμετρίᾳ λέγεται δ. Id. Metaph. 1019b33 ; usu. second power, square, κατὰ δύναμιν in square, Pl. Ti. 54b , cf. Theol.Ar. 11 , etc.: chiefly in dat., [εὐθεῖα] δυνάμει ἴση a line the square on which is equal to an area, ἡ BA ἐλάσσων ἐστὶν ἢ διπλασίων δυνάμει τῆς AK the square on BA is less than double of the square on AK, Archim. Sph.Cyl. 2.9 : εὐθεῖαι δ. σύμμετροι commensurable in square, Euc. 10 Def. 2 ; ἡ δυνάμει δεκάς the series 12 + 22 . . . + 102 , Theol.Ar. 64 . square number, Pl. Ti. 32a . square of an unknown quantity ( x2 ), Dioph. Def. 2 , al. square root of a number which is not a perfect square, surd, opp. μῆκος, Pl. Tht. 147d . product of two numbers, ἡ ἀμφοῖν (sc. τριάδος καὶ δυάδος) δ. ἑξάς Ph. 1.3 , cf. Iamb. in Nic. p.108 P.; δυνάμει in product, Hero Metr. 1.15 , Theol.Ar. 33 . concrete, powers, esp. of divine beings, αἱ δ. τῶν οὐρανῶν LXX Is. 34.4 , cf. 1 Ep.Pet. 3.22 , al., Ph. 1.587 , Corp.Herm. 1.26 , Porph. Abst. 2.34 : sg., Act.Ap. 8.10 , PMag.Par. 1.1275 ; πολυώνυμος δ., of God, Secund. Sent. 3 . manifestation of divine power, miracle, Ev.Matt. 11.21 , al., Buresch Aus Lydien 113 , etc.

english_sentence_A: For merely knowing is to recognize whether the drug is of such a nature as to dry or moisten or cool or heat us; but knowing accurately is, in addition to this, also to have come to know the quantity of the power.

greek_sentence: τινὰ μὲν γὰρ φάρμακα δύναμιν ἔχει χλιαρᾶς θερμασίας γεννητικὴν, ὅταν ὁμιλήσῃ τοῖς σώμασιν ἡμῶν, ἔνια δὲ συμμέτρου, καθάπερ ἄλλα βραχὺ ταύτης ἰσχυρότερα, ἕτερα δ’ ἤδη ζεούσης οὕτως ἰσχυρῶς, ὡς καίειν δύνασθαι.
english_sentence_A: For some drugs have a power generative of lukewarm heat when they come into contact with our bodies, some of a moderate heat, just as others are a little stronger than this, and others still of a heat already so strongly boiling that it is able to burn.
english_sentence_B: For some drugs have a faculty productive of lukewarm heat when they come into contact with our bodies, some of moderate heat, just as others have a faculty of heat a little stronger than this, and others again of heat already seething so strongly that it is able to burn.

english_sentence_A: And so extensive is the use of things said in this way that they already possess the force of a proper term, much as with 'box' (pyxis), 'coppersmith' (chalkeus), 'painter' (zōgraphos) and 'woodcutter' (dryotomos), and, to put it in a word, with those terms that began from what the grammarians call catachresis but later came to be accepted as being said in the proper sense.

greek_sentence: καί μοι δειχθέντος τινὸς νεανίσκου, κατὰ τὸ πρῶτον ἄρθρον τοῦ μέσου δακτύλου τῆς δεξιᾶς χειρὸς, ἐκ περιθλάσεως ὑγρὸν οὕτως ἐσχηκότος ἅπαν τὸ κατ’ αὐτὴν περὶ τῷ νεύρῳ χωρίον, ὡς ἤδη σήπεσθαι, τὸ μὲν σηπόμενον αὐτὸ κατέπλασα διὰ κονίας στακτῆς καὶ ὠμῆς λύσεως, οὕτω δ’ ἴσθι με καλοῦντα τὸ κρίθινον ἄλευρον, ἐλαίῳ δὲ πολλῷ θερμῷ καταντλήσας τὸ μὴ σηπόμενον μὲν, τεταμένον δὲ καὶ ὀδυνώμενον, εἶτα ἐκμάξας ἐρίῳ ξηρῷ περιέχρισα κηρωτὴν οὕτως ὑγρὰν, ὡς ἐπὶ τῶν καταγμάτων χρώμεθα, μεμιγμένον ἔχουσαν εὐφόρβιον.
english_sentence_A: And when a certain young man was shown to me who, at the first joint of the middle finger of the right hand, as a result of a contusion had the whole region around the nerve at that place so moist that it was already putrefying, the putrefying part itself I plastered with a poultice of dripped lye and raw lysis—know that it is barley meal that I call by this name—while the part that was not putrefying but was tense and painful I fomented by pouring over it plenty of warm oil, and then, having wiped it off with dry wool, I smeared around it a cerate as moist as we use in the case of fractures, having euphorbium mixed into it.
english_sentence_B: And when a certain young man was shown to me who, at the first joint of the middle finger of the right hand, had as a result of a contusion the whole region at it, around the nerve, so moist that it was already putrefying, I poulticed the putrefying part itself with percolated lye and raw lysis (know that this is what I call barley meal); and having bathed with plenty of warm oil the part that was not putrefying but was tense and painful, and then wiped it with dry wool, I smeared around it a cerate as moist as the one we use for fractures, having euphorbium mixed into it.

english_sentence_A: I for my part am not unaware that it would be clearer and more proper for them to be named 'wounded in the tendons'; but since all men customarily call them 'wounded in the nerves', in order that no one may say that I am innovating in the appellations, I preferred the customary term to the true one.
english_sentence_B: For my part, I am not unaware that it would be clearer and more proper for them to be named 'tendon-wounded'. But since all men customarily call them 'nerve-wounded', I preferred the customary name to the true one, so that no one might say that I am innovating in names.

english_sentence_A: But whether you wish to call them [576] those wounded in the nerves or those wounded in the tendons, they will neither be saved on account of these words nor be convulsed, just as they will neither be maimed nor die.

greek_sentence: ὁ γοῦν ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὁ σηπόμενος μὲν ἤδη τὰ περὶ τὸ πρῶτον ἄρθρον τοῦ μέσου δακτύλου, τεινόμενός τε καὶ ὀδυνώμενος τὰ ὑπερκείμενα, πολὺ βελτίων ἑαυτοῦ κατὰ τὴν ὑστεραίαν ἐγένετο, καθ’ ἣν ἀντὶ τῆς ὠμῆς λύσεως ἔμιξα τὸ τῶν ὀρόβων ἄλευρον τῇ στακτῇ κονίᾳ, καὶ τῇ γε τρίτῃ τῶν ἡμερῶν ὁμοίως ἔτι θεραπευόμενος ἦν μὲν ἤδη τελέως ἀνώδυνος τὰ ἄλλα, κατὰ δὲ τὸ θλάσμα, νευρῶδές τι σῶμα ﻿ [577] παραπλήσιον ὑμένι παχεῖ προὔκυψεν, ὃ μετρίως διακινήσαντός μου ῥᾳδίως ὅλον ἐξέπεσεν ἡμισαπὲς ὄν.
english_sentence_A: At any rate, that man, who was already putrefying in the parts around the first joint of the middle finger, and was suffering tension and pain in the parts lying above, became much better than he had been on the following day, on which, in place of the raw lysis (ὠμὴ λύσις), I mixed the flour of bitter vetch with dripped lye; and on the third day, while still being treated in the same way, he was already completely free of pain in the other parts, but at the contusion a certain sinewy body [577] resembling a thick membrane protruded, which, when I moved it moderately, easily fell out whole, being half-rotten.
english_sentence_B: That man, at any rate, who was already putrefying in the region of the first joint of the middle finger, and was suffering tension and pain in the parts lying above, became much better than he had been on the following day, on which, instead of the raw solution, I mixed the meal of bitter vetch with strained lye; and on the third day, while still being treated in the same way, he was by now entirely free of pain in other respects, but at the contusion a nerve-like body [577] resembling a thick membrane protruded, which, when I moved it moderately, came away easily and whole, being half-putrefied.

greek_sentence: ἀνιεὶς οὖν ἕνα τῶν τροχίσκων ἢ κυκλίσκων ἢ ὅπως ἂν ὀνομάζειν ἐθέλοι τις, ὧν εἶς ἐστι καὶ ὁ τοῦ Πολυείδου, δι’ ἑψήματος ἢ σιραίου· καὶ γὰρ καὶ τοῦτο καλεῖν ὡς ἂν αὐτὸς βουληθῇς ἐξέστω σοι· καὶ προκαταχρίσας τὸ φαινόμενον τοῦ νεύρου, τῷ τε καταπλάσματι πάλιν ἐχρησάμην ὡσαύτως καὶ τῷ δι’ εὐφορβίου χρίσματι κατὰ τῶν αὐτῶν τόπων, ὡς ἔμπροσθεν ἑκατέρῳ.

greek_sentence: καὶ μᾶλλόν γε ποιῶ τοῦτο δακνομένου τοῦ ἕλκους ὑπὸ τῶν φαρμάκων, ὡς ὅταν γε ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς χρωμένῳ μοι τοιούτῳ φαρμάκῳ, μήτε δάκνεσθαι λέγῃ μήτε ὀδυνᾶσθαι μήτε τάσεως ὁ κάμνων αἴσθηται, δὶς τῆς ἡμέρας ἐπιλύω τε καὶ καταντλῶ, περὶ μὲν τὴν ἕω τὸ πρῶτον, εἰς ἑσπέραν δὲ τὸ δεύτερον.
english_sentence_A: And I do this the more when the wound is being bitten by the drugs, inasmuch as whenever, when I am using such a drug from the beginning, the patient says he is neither bitten nor in pain, nor perceives any tension, I undo the dressing and foment twice a day, the first time around dawn, the second toward evening.
english_sentence_B: I do this all the more when the wound is being bitten by the drugs. For when I have used such a drug from the beginning and the patient says he feels neither biting nor pain, and perceives no tension, I unbind and pour oil over the part twice a day, the first time around dawn and the second towards evening.

english_sentence_A: But I guard against the use of water throughout the whole treatment, to the point that it does not even touch the wound, so that, when right at the beginning it is necessary to wash the blood off the wounded part, one does this with oil; and when the patients, already in a moderate condition, take a bath, not even then does one permit them to put the affected place into the water—for in most cases those with wounded nerves receive the wound in the hands themselves. [581] And I remember one of those wounded in this way who, when he was on his fourth day and was completely free of pain and saw that the affected part was free of inflammation, went out of the house in great cold for some necessary business, and having spent a longer time at it, came home with the whole limb strained with tension as far as the neck and feeling great pain.

greek_sentence: ὡς δ’ ἀφικομένου τινὸς ἐπ’ ἐμὲ παραγενόμενος ὡς αὐτὸν ἐθεασάμην ἐν οἷς ἦν, ἀποῤῥῖψαι μὲν ἐκέλευσα τὸ κατὰ τὸ μόριον ἔλαιον ψυχρὸν ἐκ τῆς προόδου γεγονὸς, ἐλαίῳ δὲ θερμῷ καταντλήσας ὅλον τὸ κῶλον, εἶτα καὶ τοῦ τραχήλου τὸ κατ’ εὐθὺ μέρος, ἐλαιοβρεχέσιν ἐρίοις πυριάσας ἐπιθείς τε τὸ διὰ τοῦ εὐφορβίου φάρμακον ὑγρὸν ἅμα καστορίῳ, παρηγόρησα τὸν ἄνθρωπον αὐτίκα καὶ ὕπνου ἐπιγενομένου μέχρι τῆς ἑσπέρας ἐπέπαυτο πάντα τὰ συμπτώματα.
english_sentence_A: When someone came to me and I arrived at his side and saw the state he was in, I ordered the oil on the part, which had become cold from his going out, to be wiped off, and having bathed the whole limb with hot oil, and then also the part of the neck directly in line with it, and having fomented it with oil-soaked wool and applied the liquid drug made with euphorbium together with castoreum, I soothed the man at once, and when sleep supervened, by evening all the symptoms had ceased.

greek_sentence: ὁποῖον δέ τι πρᾶγμά ἐστιν ἔνδειξις λογικὴ καὶ ὅσον πλουσιώτερον ἐμπειρίας ψιλῆς ἄνευ μεθόδου, κᾀκ τῶνδε μαθήσῃ νευροτρώτων τε πολλοῖς πολλάκις ἐν ὁδοῖς τε καὶ κατὰ πλοῦν καὶ κατ’ ἀγρὸν, ἢ ἐν πόλει μὲν, ἀλλὰ πόῤῥω τῆς ἐμῆς οἰκίας παραγενόμενος, οὔτε τοῦ δι’ εὐφορβίου φαρμάκου παρόντος οὔτε τοῦ δι’ ὄξους, ἀλλ’ οὔτε ἄλλου τῶν ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ χωρίῳ κατὰ τύχην εὐπορηθέντων φαρμάκων ἐπιθεὶς τῷ τραύματι, διὰ παντὸς [583] ἔτυχον τοῦ σκοποῦ.
english_sentence_A: What sort of thing rational indication is, and how much richer it is than bare experience without method, you will learn also from the following. Having come to many persons wounded in the nerves, often on journeys and on a voyage and in the country, or in a city but far from my own house, when neither the drug made with euphorbium was at hand nor the one made with vinegar, nor any other, but applying to the wound one of the drugs that happened to be available in that place, I always [583] hit the mark.
english_sentence_B: What sort of thing rational indication is, and how much richer it is than bare experience without method, you will learn from these cases too. Often, when I came upon many nerve-wounded people on roads, on voyages, in the countryside, or in the city but far from my house, and neither the drug made with euphorbium nor the one made with vinegar was at hand, I applied to the wound some other of the drugs that chanced to be available in that place (the text reads 'nor any other'), and I always [583] attained my aim.

english_sentence_A: [Also those] made with oxymel and the meal of beans or of bitter vetch or of darnel or of chickpeas or of bitter lupins or the fine dust of barley groats or barley meal, which I have used in the cities as cataplasms not only on parts already inflamed, but also straightaway at the beginning.
english_sentence_B: Then there are the poultices made with oxymel and flour of beans, or of bitter vetch, or of darnel, or of chickpeas, or of bitter lupins, or with fine meal of barley-groats, or with barley flour. These are the poultices I have used in the cities, not only on parts already inflamed but also immediately at the outset.

greek_sentence: ἐν ἀγρῷ δὲ καὶ πίτταν εὑρὼν ὑγρὰν παρὰ τέκτονι, [584] τῇ ζύμῃ μίξας ἐπέθηκα, καὶ παρ’ ἄλλῳ τὸ τῶν ὀρόβων ἄλευρον ἀναδεύσας αὐτῇ.
english_sentence_A: And in the country, having also found liquid pitch at a carpenter's, [584] I mixed it with leaven and applied it; and at another man's I applied bitter-vetch flour, having kneaded it up with the leaven.
english_sentence_B: In the country, too, having found liquid pitch at a carpenter's, [584] I mixed it with the leaven and applied it; and with another patient I kneaded the meal of bitter vetch into it.

greek_sentence: καὶ ὀξέλαιον δὲ μόνον ἀναλαβὼν ἐρίῳ θερμὸν ἐπέβαλον εὐθέως, ἄλλου μὴ παρόντος.
english_sentence_A: And I have also applied immediately oxelaeum alone, hot, taken up in wool, when nothing else was available; for I had confidence in the vinegar, which was sufficiently sharp and old.
english_sentence_B: I have also taken up oxelaeum (vinegar-and-oil) alone in wool and applied it warm at once, when nothing else was at hand; for I had confidence in the vinegar, since it was both sufficiently sharp and old.

lsj_entry_text: ἄμφω, τώ, τά, τώ, also οἱ, αἱ , τά; gen. ἀμφοῖν S. Ph. 25 , etc., dat. ἀμφοῖν Aj. 1264 , etc.:—both, of individuals, Il. 1.363 ; of armies or nations, 2.124 :— Hom. uses only nom. and acc.: from Hom. downwards freq. with pl. Noun or Verb, Il. 2.767 , 7.255 , etc.; ἐξ ἀμφοῖν, = ἐξ ἀλλήλοιν , S. OC 1425 : sts. indecl., h.Cer. 15 , Arist. Top. 118a28 , Theoc. 17.26 , A.R. 1.165 . (For the root cf. ἀμφί.)
greek_sentence: καὶ τότε προμίξας ὄξος, ἐπειδὴ τὸ περιέχον θερμότατον ἦν ὥρᾳ θέρους τὸ μικτὸν ἐξ ἀμφοῖν ἄχρι πλείστου κατήντλουν, ἕως τῶν ἄλλων ἐκομίσθη τι φαρμάκων.
english_sentence_A: In the case of another man who had already been chilled beforehand, because the nerve had been bruised an hour or even a still longer time earlier, I waited until one of the suitable things should be brought to me, having ordered that the part be bathed with oil; and then, having first mixed in vinegar, since the surrounding air was very hot, it being the season of summer, I kept bathing it with the mixture of both for as long as possible, until one of the other drugs was brought.
english_sentence_B: And then, having first mixed in vinegar, since the ambient air was very hot, it being the summer season, I kept pouring the mixture of both over it for a very long time, until some one of the other drugs was brought.

lsj_entry_text: στακ-τή, ἡ, (στάζω) oil of myrrh, Antiph. 223 , LXX Ge. 37.25 , Plb. 13.9.5 , Dsc. 1.60 : metaph., ἡ τῶν φρενῶν ς. Men. Per. 16 .
greek_sentence: ἕκαστον δὲ τῶν εἰρημένων ἀλεύρων καὶ τῆς στακτῆς διαμίξας πολλάκις, ἐπέπλασα καὶ κατ’ ἀρχὰς εὐθέως καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα φθάσαντος ἀνθρώπου τῶν ἐναίμων τινὶ φαρμάκων οὐ καλῶς κεχρῆσθαι.
english_sentence_A: And often, having mixed each of the flours mentioned with stacte, I applied it as a plaster both right at the beginning and afterwards, when the person had previously made bad use of one of the drugs for bleeding wounds.
english_sentence_B: Having often mixed each of the aforesaid meals with the percolated lye, I applied it as a poultice, both right at the beginning and afterwards, when the person had already made improper use of one of the 'bloody' (enaimos) drugs.

lsj_entry_text: ποιότης, ητος, ἡ, quality, Pl. Tht. 182a (where he apologizes for the use of the word as ἀλλόκοτον ὄνομα), Arist. Cat. 8b26 , EN 1173a15 (pl.), Gal. Nat.Fac. 1.2 , POxy. 2113.16 (iv A.D.), etc.; of size, Babr. 28.10 , Aesop. 84 .
greek_sentence: πάντα δ’ οὖν ταῦτα τὰ ὁπωσοῦν ἐπιτιθέμενα φάρμακα θερμὰ ταῖς ποιότησι προσφερέσθω.
english_sentence_A: All these drugs, then, applied in whatever way, should be administered warm in their qualities.
english_sentence_B: At any rate, let all these drugs, in whatever way they are applied, be administered hot in their qualities.

lsj_entry_text: συντίθημι, used by Hom. only in Med. , v. infr.:— Pass. (v. infr.), but σύγκειμαι is more freq. as Pass. :— place or put together, τὴν οὐρὴν καὶ τὸν σπλῆνα . . συνθεὶς ὁμοῦ Hdt. 2.47 , cf. 4.67 ; ὅπλα ἐν τῷ ναῷ X. HG 2.3.20 ; ἅπαντα εἰς ἕν E. IT 1016 ; ἐν ὀλίγῳ πάντα Id. Supp. 1126 (lyr.); ὁ πρῶτος συνθεὶς εἰς ταὐτὸν τὰ δύο ταῦτα βιβλίδια Gal. 15.109 ; ς. ἱμάτια, opp. ἀνασείειν, fold them together, X. Oec. 10.11 ; ς. σκέλη, opp. ἐκτείνειν, Id. Cyn. 5.10 ; opp. διαιρεῖσθαι, Pl. Sph. 252b ; ς. ἄρθρα στόματος close the lips, E. Cyc. 625 ; εἰς τὸ οὖλον (αυλον cod.) ς. τὴν κόμην, = calamistrat, Gloss. :— Pass. , τὸ συντίθεσθαι καθ' ὁντινοῦν τρόπον ῥῖγος οὐκ ἀγαθόν ἐστι any sort of combination of shivering (with other symptoms), Gal. 16.746 . technical uses, Math., add together, of numbers, Hdt. 3.95 ( Pass. ); τό τε ἀρχαῖον καὶ τὸ ἔργον principal and interest, D. 27.17 , cf. 29.30 : Geom., of lines and figures, Archim. Spir.Praef. , Papp. 70.4 . Math. also, of the transformation of a ratio componendo, Arist. EN 1131b8 ( Pass. ), Euc. 5.18 , 24 ( Pass. ). Logic, combine the terms of a proposition, Arist. Metaph. 1012a4 , 1024b19 ( Pass. ); also, use the fallacy of composition (cf. σύνθεσις 1.2e ), Id. Rh. 1401a24 . Rhet., accumulate, joined with ἐποικοδομεῖν (to form a climax), ib. 1365a16 . ς. λόγον make up an account, PHib. 1.48.15 (iii B.C.). put together constructively, so as to make a whole, πεντηκοντέρους καὶ τριήρεας (as a bridge) Hdt. 7.36 ; λίθους, of builders, Th. 4.4 , IG 42(1).103.59 (Epid., iv B.C.); πλίνθους, ξύλα, X. Mem. 3.1.7 , etc.; τὰ ὄστρακα IG 42(1).121.82 (Epid., iv B.C.); τὰ κομισθέντα Sor. 2.64 ; ἐκ τούτων τὰ μέγιστα . . συνθεὶς τοῦτον . . τὸν λόγον ποιήσομαι Hippias Eleus 6 D. ; συλλαβάς Pl. Cra. 424e . construct, frame, τὸ θνητὸν γένος Pl. Ti. 69d ; ὁ συνθείς the creator, ib. 33d :— Pass. , to be constructed, of the material universe, opp. διαλύεσθαι, Arist. Cael. 304b30 . ς. τι ἀπό τινος compose or make one thing of or from another, Hdt. 4.23 ; τὸ ἐκ τῶν νεῶν καὶ τοῦ πεζοῦ πλῆθος συντιθέμενον Id. 7.184 ; ἐξ ὧν [συλλαβῶν] τὰ ὀνόματα συντίθενται Pl. Cra. 425a , cf. 434a ; συνθεὶς πρᾶγμα πράξει δι' ὀνόματος καὶ ῥήματος Id. Sph. 262e ; εἴδωλον οὐρανοῦ ξυνθεῖσ' ἄπο (Reiske for ὕπο) E. Hel. 34 : metaph., συντιθεὶς γέλων πολύν S. Aj. 303 ; δυοῖν ἅμιλλαν ξ. strive for two things at once, E. El. 95 . construct or frame a story, συνθέντες λόγον Id. Ba. 297 , cf. Ar. Ra. 1052 (anap.), Pl. Phdr. 260b ; οἱ τὰς τέχνας τῶν λόγων συντιθέντες Arist. Rh. 1354a12 ; narrate in writing, τὰ Ἑλληνικά Th. 1.97 , cf. 21 ; compose, ς. μύθους, ποίησιν, μελῳδίαν, ὄρχησιν, Pl. R. 377d , Phdr. 278c , Lg. 812d , 816c ; αἴνιγμα Id. Ap. 27a ; ὁ τὴν ἐνθάδε συνθεὶς ἀνατομήν Gal. 15.147 :— Pass. , pf. συντέθειται ib. 797 ; περὶ ὀλίγας οἰκίας αἱ . . τραγῳδίαι συντίθενται Arist. Po. 1453a19 . Math., of the synthesis of a geometrical problem, opp. ἀναλύω, Id. SE 175a28 , Papp. 648.13 ; συντεθήσεται τὸ πρόβλημα οὕτως the synthesis of the problem will proceed thus, Archim. Sph.Cyl. 2.1 , cf. Apollon. Perg. Con. 1 Praef., 2.44 , al. frame, devise, contrive, ὁ συνθεὶς τάδε the framer of this plot, S. OT 401 , cf. Th. 8.68 ; ἐξ ἐπιβουλῆς ς. ταῦτα Antipho 5.25 ; ς. λόγους ψευδεῖς Id. 6.9 ; ψευδεῖς αἰτίας D. 25.28 ; τὴν κατηγορίαν And. 1.6 , etc.; rarely in good sense, εὖ πρᾶγμα συντεθὲν ὄψεσθε D. 18.144 . put together, take in, comprehend, παιδὸς μόρον A. Supp. 65 (lyr.); ὄμνυ . . θεῶν συντιθεὶς ἅπαν γένος E. Med. 747 ; πάσας συντιθεὶς ψέγει γυναῖκας Id. Fr. 657 , cf. Hec. 1184 : ἐν βραχεῖ ξυνθεὶς λέγω putting things shortly together, speaking briefly, S. El. 673 . commit to a person's care, deliver to him for his own use or that of others, PMich.Zen. 2.3 , 14 (iii B.C.), PCair.Zen. 4.23 , 6.11 , 64 , 299.9 , al. (iii B.C.); γνώριζε οὐχ ὑπάρχον παρ' ἡμῖν ἀργύριον τοσοῦτο ὥστε ἱκανὸν συνθεῖναι Πυρρίχῳ PMich.Zen. 28.18 , cf. 32.7 , PSI 4.392.7 , 5.524.3 , 6.613.8 , 7.862.1 , PLille 15.3 (all iii B.C.); τινὶ ὀστᾶ, ἐπιστολάς, πλῆθος χρυσίου, etc., Plb. 5.10.4 , 8.17.4 , 15.25.16 , cf. 27.7.1 , 28.22.3 , IG 12(5).590.12 (Ceos, ii B.C.), 11(4).1056.4 (Delos, ii B.C., cf. Jahresh. 24.171 ), OGI 345.11 (Delph., i B.C.). αὐτοὶ δ' ἔνοχοι εἴημεν τῷ ὅρκῳ ὁπηνίκ' ἂν εὖ συνθῶμεν perh. as soon as we have duly delivered (or executed) this declaration, BGU 1738.32 (i B.C.); συνθεὶς τούτους μου τοὺς λιβέλλους ἐπιδίδωμι τῇ σῇ λαμπρότητι PLond. 3.1000.7 (vi A.D.). collect, conclude, infer, Plb. 28.17.14 , Arr. Ind. 34 . Med. συντίθεμαι, used by Hom. only in aor. 2 and in signf. 1 : put together for oneself, i.e. observe, give heed to, σύνθετο θυμῷ βουλήν Il. 7.44 ; φρεσὶ σύνθετο θέσπιν ἀοιδήν Od. 1.328 ; ἐμεῖο δὲ σύνθεο μῦθον 17.153 ; συνθέμενος ῥῆμα Pi. P. 4.277 ; and, simply, perceive, hear, κλαιούσης ὄπα σύνθετο Od. 20.92 : in Hom. mostly abs., σὺ δὲ σύνθεο do thou take heed, Il. 1.76 , Od. 15.318 , etc.; σὺ δὲ σύνθεο θυμῷ ib. 27 . set in order organize, δύναμιν X. HG 4.8.20 ; τὰ τῆς πόλεως ib. 6.1.17 . agree on, conclude (cf. συνθήκη) , ἄνδρεσσι κακοῖς συνθέμενοι φιλίην Thgn. 306 ; συντίθεσθαι συμμαχίην, ὁμαιχμίην τισί, Hdt. 2.181 , 8.140 .á; τὰς ξυνθήκας ἂς ξυνέθεντο IG 12.117.4 , cf. 116.27 , al.; εἰρήνην Isoc. 15.109 ; ς. ναῦλον agree upon the fare, X. An. 5.1.12 ; ταῦτα συνθέμενοι having agreed on these points, Th. 3.114 , cf. Ar. Lys. 178 , Plu. Alc. 31 ; ξυνέθεσθε κοινῇ τάδε E. Ba. 807 , cf. 808 ; so τάπερ τῷ Δαρείῳ συνεθήκατο with D. , Hdt. 3.157 ; ς. Ἴωσι ξεινίην Id. 1.27 ; μισθόν τινι Pl. Grg. 520c ; ς. τι πρός τινα Hdt. 7.145 , etc.:— Pass. , τοῦ συντεθέντος χρόνου agreed upon, Pl. Phdr. 254d . c. inf., covenant, agree to do, συνέθευ παρέχειν φωνάν Pi. P. 11.41 (dub. l.); ς. ἀλλήλοις μήτ' ἀδικεῖν μήτ' ἀδικεῖσθαι Pl. R. 359a , cf. And. 4.18 , Arist. Pol. 1257a35 : c. inf. fut., ξυνέθεντο ἥξειν Th. 6.65 ; ς. τινί folld. by inf. fut., συνθέμενοι ἡμῖν . . ἀντιώσεσθαι Hdt. 9.7 .β ́, cf. And. 1.42 : an inf. must be supplied in the phrases, κατὰ (i.e. καθ' ἃ) συνεθήκαντο, καθ' ὅτι ἂν συνθῶνται, etc., Hdt. 3.86 , Foed. ap. Th. 5.18 : also ς. ὡς . . Hdt. 6.84 ; ὡς δεῖ ἕκαστα γίγνεσθαι X. HG 5.4.2 . abs., make a covenant, ἔβαν συνθέμενος Pi. N. 4.75 (constr. uncertain in Alc. Supp. 5.11 ): c. dat., Hdt. 6.115 , X. An. 1.9.7 , POxy. 1668.12 (iii A.D.); αὐτὸς σαυτῷ συνέθου Pl. Cra. 435a ; συνθέσθαι πρός τινα come to terms with him, Decr. ap. D. 18.187 , POxy. 908.18 (ii/iii A.D.); περί τινος πρὸς ἀλλήλους D.S. 1.98 ; also, bet, wager, Thphr. HP 9.17.2 , Men. Epit. 288 ; πρός τινας Plu. Alc. 8 . vote with, support, τούτοις Lys. Fr. 68 , cf. Call. Epigr. 1.14 , D.H. Phdr. 274a :—in political sense, aristocrats, esp. in the phrase καλοὶ κἀγαθοί (v. sub καλοκἀγαθός). brave, valiant, since courage was attributed to Chiefs and Nobles, Il. 1.131 , al.; τῷ κ' ἀγαθὸς μὲν ἔπεφν', ἀγαθὸν δέ κεν ἐξενάριξεν 21.280 ; cf. greek_sentence: ὥσπερ δὲ τὴν πρόπολιν ἐν ἀγρῷ ποτε ἐπέθηκα τῶν τότε παρόντων ὡς βέλτιον φάρμακον ἐκλεξάμενος, οὕτως καὶ τὴν ζύμην αὖθις [593] ἐφ’ ἑτέρου, φαρμάκου μὴ παρόντος, ἐπειδὴ καὶ ταύτην τὰ ἐκ τοῦ βάθους ἠπιστάμην ἕλκουσάν τε καὶ διαφοροῦσαν.
english_sentence_A: And just as I once, in the country, applied propolis, having selected it as the better drug among those then available, so too I applied leaven on another occasion [593] in the case of another patient, when no drug was at hand, since I knew that this too draws out what lies in the depth and disperses it.
english_sentence_B: Just as I once, in the country, applied propolis, having selected it as the better drug among those then at hand, so too on another occasion [593] I applied leaven to another patient, when no drug was at hand, since I knew that this too both draws out and disperses what lies in the depth.

C.), found in codd. of Th. 1.143 , 8.1 , (ἐπεσ-) Id. 4.13 , (συνεκ-) Lys. 13.25 , (ἀπο-) Pl. Cyr. 6.1.16 , D. 56.12 : Hom. uses only pres., impf., and fut. πλεύσομαι (v. supr.).—Of the Ion. πλώω, Hom. uses opt. πλώοιεν Od. 5.240 , part. ἐπι-πλώων ib. 284 , πλώων h.Hom. 22.7 : impf. πλῶον Il. 21.302 ; also shortd. aor. ἔπλων, ως, ω, part. πλώς, in the compds. ἀπ-έπλω, ἐπ-έπλως, part. ἐπιπλώς, παρέπλω; and Hes. has ἐπ-έπλων; the pres., impf., and fut. forms occur as vv.ll. in Hdt. , inf. πλώειν 4.156 , part. πλωούσας 8.10 , 22 , 42 : impf. ἔπλωον ib. 41 ; Iterat. πλώεσκον Q.S. 14.656 : fut. πλώσομαι (ἀπο-) Hdt. 8.5 ( πλώσω Lyc. 1044 ); but the aor. 1 forms are read in Hdt. , ἔπλωσα 4.148 ; inf. πλῶσαι 1.24 ; part. πλώσας 4.156 , 8.49 (also once in Hom. in compd. ἐπι-πλώσας Il. 3.47 ): pf. παρα-πέπλωκα Hdt. 4.99 ; πέπλωκα occurs E. Hel. 532 , Ar. Th. 878 (paratrag.).—Only εε and εει are contracted in Att. (πλέει is f.l. in Th. 4.28 , and πλέετε v.l. in X. An. 7.6.37 ). [ Hom. uses πλέων as monosyll., πλέων ἐπὶ οἴνοπα πόντον Od. 1.183 ]:—sail, go by sea, Λακεδαίμονος ἐξ ἐρατεινῆς Il. 3.444 ; Ἰλιόθεν 14.251 ; ἐπὶ Κέρκυραν Th. 1.53 ; εὐθὺ Λέσβου X. lsj_entry_text: ἀγροικ-ία, ἡ, rusticity, boorishness, Pl. Grg. 461c , R. 560d , al.; cf. Arist. EN 1108a26 . the country, Herod. 1.2 , Inscr.Magn. 8 , SIG 344.100 (Teos), Muson. Fr. 11p.60H. , Plu. 2.519a , Longus 1.13 , Aristid. Or. 47(23).45 ; pl., Plu. 2.311b . in pl., countryhouses, D.S. 20.8 , Nymphod. 12 , M.Ant. 4.3 .
greek_sentence: οὐ μόνον δὲ τὰ τοιαῦτα κατὰ τὰς ἀγροικίας εὑρίσκεται ῥᾳδίως, ἀλλὰ καὶ θεῖον ἄπυρον, ᾧ ποτε καὶ αὐτῷ ἐχρησάμην μίξας τῇ τετραφαρμάκῳ.
english_sentence_A: Not only are such things readily found in country districts, but also unburnt sulphur, which I myself also once used, mixing it with the tetrapharmakon.
english_sentence_B: Not only are such things easily found in country places, but also unfired sulphur, which I myself once used as well, mixing it with the tetrapharmacum.

lsj_entry_text: ἀφρόνιτρον, Att. ἀφρόλιτρον (the two distd. by Gal.l.c., cf. Gp. 2.28 ), τό, a form of native sodium carbonate (cf.νίτρον), distd. by Gal. 12.212 from the finer ἄνθος νίτρου, cf. Herod.Med. ap. Orib. 6.20.5 : in Hp. and correct Greek divisim ἀφρὸς νίτρου: hence ἀφρόνιτρον is condemned by Phryn. 272 .
greek_sentence: ταύτῃ μὲν οὖν καὶ ἀφρόνιτρον καὶ Βερενίκιον λίτρον καὶ ἀφρόλιτρον τὸ μὴ λιθῶδες, ἀλλ’ ὄντως ἀφρόλιτρον, ὅπερ ἀφρώδη τὴν σύστασιν ἔχει, μίξας ἐχρησάμην πολλάκις, οὐ μόνον ἐπ’ ἀγροικίας ἀπορίᾳ τῶν ἄλλων, ἀλλὰ καὶ παρόντων τῶν εἰρημένων φαρμάκων, ἕνεκα τοῦ τῇ πείρᾳ βασανίσαι μου τὴν ἐπίνοιαν καὶ διὰ μόνης τῆς τοιαύτης χρήσεως ὁ τετρωμένος ἐθεραπεύθη, καταντλώμενος δηλονότι τῷ ἐλαίῳ.
english_sentence_A: With this, then, I also often used, having mixed them in, aphronitron and Berenician nitron and aphrolitron—not the stony kind, but genuine aphrolitron, which has a foamy consistency—not only in the country for lack of the others, but also when the aforementioned drugs were available, for the sake of testing my devising by experience; and through such use alone the wounded man was cured, being, of course, fomented with the oil.
english_sentence_B: With this, then, I often mixed and used aphronitre, and Berenician litron, and aphrolitre (not the stony kind, but true aphrolitre, which has a frothy consistency), not only in the country for want of other things, but even when the aforementioned drugs were at hand, in order to test my devising by experience; and through this use alone the wounded man was cured, being of course bathed with the oil.

greek_sentence: ἐπεὶ δέ τινα τούτων ἐζευγμένας ἔχει θερμότητας ἀμετροτέρας ἢ δακνώδεις ἰσχυρῶς δριμύτητας ἢ ὀξύτητας, εὔλογόν ἐστι μιγνύειν αὐτοῖς [595] ἕτερα φάρμακα δυνάμενα τὰς εἰρημένας ὑπεροχὰς μετριωτέρας ἐργάζεσθαι χωρὶς τοῦ μὴ βλάπτειν τὴν δύναμιν.
english_sentence_A: But since some of these have, coupled with them, heats that are rather immoderate, or strongly biting acridities or sharpnesses, it is reasonable to mix with them [595] other drugs capable of rendering the aforesaid excesses more moderate without harming the power.
english_sentence_B: But since some of these have joined to them heats that are rather immoderate, or strongly biting pungencies or acidities, it is reasonable to mix with them [595] other drugs that are able to make the said excesses more moderate without harming the potency.

greek_sentence: τινὰ μὲν γὰρ, ὡς ἐδείκνυμεν ἐν τῇ περὶ τῶν ἁπλῶν φαρμάκων πραγματείᾳ, τῆς πρώτης τάξεώς ἐστι τῶν θερμαινόντων, ἀποκεχωρηκότα βραχύ τι τῶν εὐκράτων, ἕτερα δ’ ἐπ’ αὐτῆς τῆς δευτέρας ἐπὶ πλέον ἀφεστηκότα, καὶ τινὰ τῆς τρίτης καὶ τετάρτης, ἄλλ’ ἄττα καίειν ἤδη δυνάμενα.
english_sentence_A: For some, as we showed in the treatise On Simple Drugs, are of the first order of heating things, having departed a little from the well-tempered; others are in the second itself, standing further away; and some are of the third and fourth, certain others being already able to burn.
english_sentence_B: For some, as we showed in the treatise on simple drugs, belong to the first order of heating drugs, having departed only a little from the well-tempered; others lie in the second order itself, standing further off; and some belong to the third and the fourth, certain others being already able to burn.

english_sentence_A: Accordingly, in proportion to the vehemence of each drug in respect of its power, the power of the things mixed together is discovered, if one knows the temperaments of all the simple drugs.

english_sentence_A: But the method of the Empiricists, which mixes only things of the same kind, comes about both through ignorance of the nature of each drug and, for those who do know this, through the quantity of the excess not being securely known.

english_sentence_A: For once the wool has been removed, having only such a drug itself lying upon them, they bathe with less disturbance.

lsj_entry_text: ὕδωρ [υ, v. fin.], τό, gen. ὕδατος: an Ep. dat. ὕδει in Hes. Op. 61 , Thgn. 961 ; later nom. ὕδος Call. Fr. 475 ; Boeot. οὕδωρ prob. in IG 7.3169 (Orchom.):—water, of any kind, but in Hom. rarely of seawater without an epith., ἄνεμός τε καὶ ὕ. Od. 3.300 , 7.277 ; but ἁλμυρὸν ὕ. 9.227 , al., cf. Th. 4.26 ; of rivers, ὕ. Αἰσήποιο, Στυγός, Il. 2.825 , 8.369 , al.; so in Lyr. and Trag., ὕ, Ἀσώπιον Pi. N. 3.3 ; ὕ. τὸ Νείλου A. Supp. 561 (lyr.): freq. in pl. (but only once in Hom. , ὕδατ' ἀενάοντα Od. 13.109 ), Καφίσια ὕδατα the waters of Cephisus, Pi. O. 14.1 ; ῥυτῶν ὑδάτων S. OC 1599 ; ὕδασιν τοίς Ἀχελῴου Id. Fr. 271 (anap.): spring-water, drinking-water, οἶνον ἔμισγον καὶ ὕ. Od. 1.110 ; ἀφυσσάμεθ' ὕδωρ 9.85 ; ὕδατα καὶ . . δῖτοι Pl. R. 404a ; πότιμον ὕ. X. HG 3.2.19 ; ὕ. πίνων a water-drinker, D. 6.30 , cf. 19.46 , Ar. Eq. 349 ; ὕ. δὲ πίνων οὐδὲν ἂν τέκοι σοφόν Cratin. 199 , cf. Aristopho 10.3 , Bato 2.9 , al.: ὕδωρ κατὰ χειρός water for washing the hands, v. χείρ; φέρτε χερσὶν ὕ. Il. 9.171 ; ὕ. ἐπὶ χεῖρας ἔχευαν 3.270 , Od. 1.146 , al.; λοέσσας ὕδατι λευκῷ Il. 23.282 :—on γῆν καὶ ὕδωρ αἰτεῖν and διδόναι, v. γῆ 1.2b :—a curse was invoked upon those who refused fire (i.e. the right to borrow burning embers) or water or to direct a traveller on his way, Diph. 62 , cf. X. Oec. 2.15 :—prov., ὅρκους ἐγὼ γυναικὸς εἰς ὕ. γράφω S. Fr. 811 , cf. Men. Mon. 25 ; ἐν ὕδατι γράφειν Pl. Phdr. 276c ; ὅταν τὸ ὕδωρ πνίγῃ, τί δεῖ ἐπιπίνειν; if water chokes, what more can be done ? of a desperate case, Arist. EN 1146a35 , cf. ἐπιρροφέω 1 . rain-water, rain, ὅτε λαβρότατον χέει ὕ. Ζεύς Il. 16.385 ; ὗσαι ὕδατι λαβροτάτῳ Hdt. 1.87 ; ἐγίνετο ὕ. ἄπλετον Id. 8.12 ; πολύ Th. 6.70 , D. 59.99 ; ὕ. ἐπιγενόμενον πολύ X. HG 1.6.28 ; τὸ ὕ. τὸ γενόμενον τῆς νυκτός Th. 2.5 , cf. Hdt. 8.13 : more definitely, ὕδωρ ἐζ οὐρανοῦ X. An. 4.2.2 , Aristid. Or. 50(26).35 (but ἐζ οὐρανοῦ is a gloss in Th. 2.77 ): pl., ὕ. ὄμβρια Pi. O. 11(10).2 ; τὰ Διὸς, or παρὰ τοῦ Δ., ὕ. Pl. Lg. 761a , 761b ; τὸ ἐκ Διὸς ὕ. Thphr. HP 2.6.5 ; καινὸν ἀεὶ τὸν Δία ὕειν ὕδωρ, ὕδωρ τὸν θεὸν ποιῆσαι, Ar. Nu. 1280 , V. 261 (lyr.), cf. Thphr. Char. 3.4 : abs., ἐὰν πλείω ποιῇ ὕ. Id. CP 1.19.3 : κεραύνια ὕ. thunder-showers, Plu. 2.664f ; ὕ. πολλά, συνεχέα μαλθακῶς Hp. Epid. 1.1 . for ἐν ὕδατι βρέχεσθαι, Hdt. 3.104 , v. βρέχω. in the law-courts, τὸ ὕδωρ was the water of the water-clock (κλεψύδρ), and hence the time it took in running out, ἂν ἐγχωρῇ τὸ ὕδωρ D. 44.45 ; οὐχ ἱκανόν μοι τὸὕ. Id. 45.47 ; ἐν τῷ ἐμῷ ὕ., ἐπὶ τοῦ ἐμοῦ ὕ., in the time allowed me, Id. 18.139 , 57.61 ; οὐκ ἐνδέχεται πρὸς ταὐτὸ ὕ. εἰπεῖν one cannot say (all) in one speech, Id. 27.12 ; τὸ ὕ. ἀναλῶσαι Din. 2.6 ; πρὸς ὕ. σμικρὸν διδάζαι Pl. Tht. 201b ; ἐν μικρῷ μέρει τοῦ παντὸς ὕ. D. 29.9 ; ἐπίλαβε τὸ ὕ. stop the water (which was done while the speech was interrupted by the calling of evidence and reading of documents), Id. 45.8 ; ἐγχεῖται τὸ μὲν πρῶτον ὕ. τῷ κατηγόρῳ . . , τὸ δὲ δεύτερον ὕ. τῷ φεύγοντι Aeschin. 3.197 ; ἀποδιδόναι, παραδιδόναι τινὶ τὸ ὕ., to give him the turn of speaking, Id. 1.162 , Din. 1.114 . generally, liquid, ὕδατος εἴδη τὰ τοιάδε· οἶνος, οὖρον, ὀρός Arist. Mete. 382b13 , cf. Hp. Cord. 12 . part of the constellation Aquarius, Arat. 399 . a name for the winter solstice, Paul.Al. A. 4 . Ὕδατα, τά, as the name of places with hot or mineral waters, Ὕ. Σέζτια, Lat. Aquae Sextiae, Ὕ. Νεαπολιτανά, etc., Ptol. Geog. 2.10.8 , 3.3.7 , etc. [υ by nature, ὕδωρ Il. 18.347 , al. greek_sentence: προείρηται γὰρ ὅτι μηδὲ τότε προσήκει βρέχειν ὕδασι τὸ τετρωμένον, ἐάν γε ἐν χειρὶ ᾖ.
english_sentence_A: For it has been said before that not even then is it fitting to wet the wounded part with water, at least if it is in the hand.
english_sentence_B: For it has been said before that not even then is it proper to wet the wounded part with water, at least if it is on the hand.

lsj_entry_text: τρῶσις, εως, ἡ, (τρώω) wounding, mostly pl., Hp. VC 2 , Arist. Po. 1452b13 , Plu. 2.20e , Sammelb. 6003.13 (iv A. D.): sg., Phld. Herc. 1251.6 ; injury to a tree, Thphr. HP 4.16.1 .
greek_sentence: κατὰ μέντοι τὸν πόδα τῆς τρώσεως ἐπιγενομένης ἀδύνατον μέν ἐστι μὴ βρέχειν τὸ μόριον, ἀπέχεσθαι δὲ χρὴ τηνικαῦτα βαλανείου τὰς πρώτας τέτταρας ἡμέρας.
english_sentence_A: When, however, the wound has occurred in the foot, it is impossible not to wet the part, but one must at that time abstain from the bath for the first four days.
english_sentence_B: When, however, the wound has occurred in the foot, it is impossible not to wet the part, but in that case one must abstain from the bath for the first four days.

lsj_entry_text: ἀγρός, οῦ, ὁ, field, mostly in pl., fields, lands, Il. 23.832 , Od. 4.757 , Pi. P. 4.149 , etc.; opp. κῆποι, Theopomp. Hist. 89 ; sg., farm, Od. 24.205 ; also in pl., X. HG 2.4.1 :—tilled land, opp. fallow, ἀγρὸς καὶ ἀργός, Ἀθηνᾶ 20.167 (Erythrae). country, opp. town, Od. 17.182 , E. Supp. 884 , etc.; ἀγρὸν τὰν πόλιν ποιεῖς Epich. 169 ; ἀγρῷ in the country, Od. 11.188 ; ἐπ' ἀγροῦ in the country, 1.190 , 22.47 ; ἐπ' ἀγρὸῦ νόσφι πόληος 1.185 ; in pl., κατὰ πτόλιν ἠὲ κατ' ἀγρούς 17.18 ; ἐν οἴκοις ἢ 'ν ἀγροῖς S. Av. 579 , Philem. 116 ; αγρόθεν in Alc. Com. 19 is paratrag.] (Cf. Skt. ájras 'plain', prob. fr. aj 'drive' (cf. ἄγω), i.e. pasture.)
greek_sentence: ἐπεὶ δὲ ἀπόλωλεν ἐν τῷ νῦν βίῳ ἡ καρτερία πάντων ἀνθρώπων, ἤδη μέχρι καὶ τῶν ἐν τοῖς ἀγροῖς καθ’ ἡμέραν εἰωθότων λούεσθαι, τοὺς μὲν μὴ πάνυ τρυφῶντας, εἶεν δ’ ἂν οἱ πένητες οὗτοι, πειθομένους ἔχομεν ὡς τὸ πολὺ, τοὺς πλουσίους δὲ καὶ μάλιστα αὐτῶν ὅσοι πολὺ δύνανται ἢ δυσπειθοῦντας ἢ τελείως ἀπειθοῦντας.
english_sentence_A: But since in present-day life endurance has perished among all men, so that by now even those in the fields have become accustomed to bathe every day, we have those who are not very luxurious—and these would be the poor—obedient for the most part, but the rich, and especially those of them who have great power, either hard to persuade or entirely disobedient.
english_sentence_B: But since in present-day life the endurance of all men has perished, now reaching even to those in the countryside, accustomed as they are to bathe every day, we find those who are not very given to luxury (and these would be the poor) for the most part compliant, but the rich, and above all those of them who wield great power, either hard to persuade or wholly disobedient.

english_sentence_A: But since, I know not how, each for a different reason, some of us unwillingly and others willingly are compelled to put up with their softness, [598] I am accustomed to do something of this sort.

english_sentence_A: Placing one of the plaster-like drugs upon the wounded part, I apply over it on the outside in turn several many-folded linen cloths soaked in oil, and over these again, on the outside, I apply a bandage of linen cloth; and after this, once more, in the bath itself I first pour the oil over the bandage, when the person wounded in the nerves is about to step into the tub; and obviously, when he has bathed, I remove everything that lies upon the part and employ the previously described regimen of the whole treatment.
english_sentence_B: Placing one of the plaster-like drugs on the wounded part, I again lay over it on the outside several many-folded linen cloths soaked through with oil, and over these in turn, on the outside, I put a bandage of linen cloth. After this, again in the bath itself, I first pour the oil over the bandage when the nerve-wounded patient is about to step into the tub [reading πύελον for πτύελον]; and when he has, of course, bathed, I take off everything that was laid on and follow the previously described course of the whole treatment.

greek_sentence: εἴρηται γὰρ ἔμπροσθεν ὅτι καὶ οἱ τένοντες, εἰς οὓς οἱ πλεῖστοι τῶν μυῶν τελευτῶσι, συμπαθείας οὐ μικρὰς ἐπιφέρουσι, πρῶτον μὲν τοὺς σπασμοὺς γεννῶντες, ὕστερον δὲ σηπόμενοί τε αὐτοὶ καὶ τὰ πλησιάζοντα πάντα συνδιαφθείροντες.
english_sentence_A: For it was said earlier that the tendons too, in which most of the muscles terminate, bring about no small sympathetic affections, first generating spasms, and later both putrefying themselves and destroying along with themselves all the neighbouring parts.

greek_sentence: ἐπεὶ δ’ ἕκαστον ὧν ἐπενόησα φαρμάκων ἔδωκα τοῖς φίλοις ἰατροῖς, οὐ μόνον τοῖς πολίταις, ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς ἀστυγείτοσιν ἕνεκεν τοῦ βεβαιωθῆναι πάντα τῇ πείρᾳ· δόξαν δ’ οὐκ οἶδ’ ὅπως τῷ κατὰ τὴν πόλιν ἡμῶν ἀρχιερεῖ, τὴν θεραπείαν ἐγχειρῆσαί μοι μόνῳ τῶν μονομάχων καίτοι νέῳ τὴν ἡλικίαν ὄντι.
english_sentence_A: And since I gave each of the drugs I had devised to my physician friends, not only to my fellow citizens but also to those of the neighbouring cities, in order that everything might be confirmed by experience; and since it seemed good, I know not how, to the high priest in our city to entrust the treatment of the gladiators to me alone, although I was young in age—for I was beginning my twenty-ninth year—at that time I treated those wounded in the front and lower part of the thigh by means of the regimen I had devised, myself cutting through the remainder of the tendon in those whose wound was transverse, so that the treatment was free of danger for me, while in those whose wound was small or straight I conducted the whole regimen with safety and at the same time with fear.
english_sentence_B: And since I gave each of the drugs I had devised to physicians who were my friends, not only to my fellow citizens but also to those of the neighbouring cities, so that everything might be confirmed by experience; and it seemed good, I know not how, to the high priest of our city to entrust the treatment of the gladiators to me alone, although I was young in age.

lsj_entry_text: ἐγκάρσιος, α , ον (ος, ον Gal. UP 5.12 codd.), athwart, oblique, Th. 2.76 , 6.99 , Ach.Tat. 3.2 , Hld. 3.2 ; of the ecliptic, Arist. Mu. 392a12 (v.l. -ίως).
greek_sentence: τοῦ γὰρ ἐνάτου καὶ εἰκοστοῦ ἔτους ἠρχόμην, τηνικαῦτα τοὺς τρωθέντας κατὰ τὸ πρόσω τε καὶ κάτω μέρος τοῦ μηροῦ διὰ τῆς ἐπινενοημένης ἀγωγῆς ἐθεράπευσα, τῶν μὲν ἐγκαρσίαν ἐχόντων τὴν πληγὴν τὸ τοῦ τένοντος ὑπόλοιπον ἐντέμνων αὐτὸς, ὡς ἀκίνδυνον εἶναί μοι τὴν θεραπείαν, τῶν δὲ τὸ μικρὸν ἢ ὄρθιον ἐχόντων τὸ τραῦμα, σὺν ἀσφαλείᾳ τε ἅμα καὶ δέει τὴν ὅλην ἀγωγὴν ποιούμενος.
english_sentence_A: And since I gave each of the drugs I had devised to my physician friends, not only to my fellow citizens but also to those of the neighbouring cities, in order that everything might be confirmed by experience; and since it seemed good, I know not how, to the high priest in our city to entrust the treatment of the gladiators to me alone, although I was young in age—for I was beginning my twenty-ninth year—at that time I treated those wounded in the front and lower part of the thigh by means of the regimen I had devised, myself cutting through the remainder of the tendon in those whose wound was transverse, so that the treatment was free of danger for me, while in those whose wound was small or straight I conducted the whole regimen with safety and at the same time with fear.
english_sentence_B: For I was beginning my twenty-ninth year. greek_sentence: τοῦ γὰρ ἐνάτου καὶ εἰκοστοῦ ἔτους ἠρχόμην, τηνικαῦτα τοὺς τρωθέντας κατὰ τὸ πρόσω τε καὶ κάτω μέρος τοῦ μηροῦ διὰ τῆς ἐπινενοημένης ἀγωγῆς ἐθεράπευσα, τῶν μὲν ἐγκαρσίαν ἐχόντων τὴν πληγὴν τὸ τοῦ τένοντος ὑπόλοιπον ἐντέμνων αὐτὸς, ὡς ἀκίνδυνον εἶναί μοι τὴν θεραπείαν, τῶν δὲ τὸ μικρὸν ἢ ὄρθιον ἐχόντων τὸ τραῦμα, σὺν ἀσφαλείᾳ τε ἅμα καὶ δέει τὴν ὅλην ἀγωγὴν ποιούμενος.
english_sentence_A: And since I gave each of the drugs I had devised to my physician friends, not only to my fellow citizens but also to those of the neighbouring cities, in order that everything might be confirmed by experience; and since it seemed good, I know not how, to the high priest in our city to entrust the treatment of the gladiators to me alone, although I was young in age—for I was beginning my twenty-ninth year—at that time I treated those wounded in the front and lower part of the thigh by means of the regimen I had devised, myself cutting through the remainder of the tendon in those whose wound was transverse, so that the treatment was free of danger for me, while in those whose wound was small or straight I conducted the whole regimen with safety and at the same time with fear.
english_sentence_B: For I was beginning my twenty-ninth year. At that time I treated those wounded in the front and lower part of the thigh by means of the treatment I had devised: in those who had the wound transverse, I myself cut through what remained of the tendon, so that the treatment might be without danger for me; and in those who had the wound small or longitudinal, I carried out the whole treatment with both safety and apprehension at once.

greek_sentence: τῶν γὰρ πρὸ ἐμοῦ πάντων [600] ἰατρῶν, ἐπὶ πλεῖστόν τε καταντλούντων αὐτοὺς ὕδατι θερμῷ καὶ καταπλαττόντων ἀλεύρῳ πυρίνῳ, δι’ ὑδρελαίου συμμέτρως ἑψημένῳ, τὸ μὲν ὕδωρ οὐδ’ ὅλως προσήνεγκα, τῷ δὲ ἐλαίῳ πολλάκις καταιονῶν ἅμα τοῖς εἰρημένοις φαρμάκοις, ὑγιεῖς πάντας ἐν τάχει εἰργασάμην.
english_sentence_A: For whereas all the physicians before me [600] both fomented them for a very long time with hot water and applied poultices of wheaten flour moderately boiled in water-and-oil (hydrelaion), I did not apply the water at all, but, bathing them frequently with the oil together with the drugs mentioned, I quickly rendered them all healthy.
english_sentence_B: For whereas all the physicians before me [600] bathed them very extensively with hot water and applied a poultice of wheaten flour boiled to a moderate degree in hydrelaeum (water and oil), I did not apply water at all. Instead, by frequently pouring oil over them together with the drugs already mentioned, I quickly made them all healthy.

greek_sentence: πάλιν δ’ ἐπὶ τούτῳ σωθέντων ἁπάντων ὁ τρίτος καὶ ὁ τέταρτος καὶ πέμπτος ὡσαύτως ἐνεχείρισάν μοι τὴν θεραπείαν τῶν μονομάχων, ὥστε πολλὴν βάσανον ἔχειν τῆς ἀγωγῆς.
english_sentence_A: And when again under this one all were saved, the third and the fourth and the fifth likewise entrusted to me the treatment of the gladiators, so that I have had an extensive testing of the method of treatment.
english_sentence_B: And again, since under him all were saved, the third, the fourth and the fifth in the same way entrusted me with the treatment of the gladiators, so that I had extensive testing of the method of treatment.

greek_sentence: ἐν δὲ δὴ χρόνῳ τούτῳ καὶ τοιοῦτον ἐπενοήθη μοί τι, καὶ μάλιστα αὐτῷ προσέχειν χρὴ τὸν νοῦν ἐκείνους τῶν ἰατρῶν, ὅσοι τραυμάτων θεραπείαν ὀρθῶς βούλονται μεταχειρίζεσθαι.
english_sentence_A: And indeed in this period something of the following kind was also devised by me, and those physicians who wish to handle the treatment of wounds correctly must pay particular attention to it.
english_sentence_B: During this time something of the following kind also occurred to me, and those physicians who wish to undertake the treatment of wounds correctly must above all pay attention to it.

greek_sentence: θεασάμενος [601] γάρ τινα μονομάχων τῶν καλουμένων ἱππέων ἐγκαρσίαν ἔχοντα διαίρεσιν, ἄχρι βάθους πολλοῦ κατὰ τὰ πρόσω τε καὶ κάτω τοῦ μηροῦ καὶ τὸ χεῖλος ἰδὼν τοῦ τραύματος, ἄνωθεν μὲν τὸ ἕτερον ἀνεσπασμένον, κάτω δὲ θάτερον, ὡς ἐπὶ τὴν μύλην κατεσπασμένον, ἐτόλμησα τῆς κατὰ πλάτος ὀνομαζομένης ἀγωγῆς ἀποστὰς, συναγαγεῖν ῥαφαῖς πρὸς ἄλληλα τὰ διεστῶτα μέρη τῶν μυῶν.
english_sentence_A: For having observed [601] one of the gladiators called horsemen (hippeis) who had a transverse division, extending to a great depth, in the front and lower part of the thigh, and having seen the lip of the wound—the one drawn up above, the other drawn down below, as if toward the kneecap (mylē)—I ventured, departing from the treatment named 'according to breadth' (kata platos), to bring together with sutures the separated parts of the muscles toward one another.
english_sentence_B: For having observed [601] one of the gladiators called 'horsemen' with a transverse division, reaching to a great depth at the front and lower part of the thigh, and having seen the lips of the wound, the one drawn up above and the other drawn down below, as if towards the kneecap, I ventured, departing from what is named the 'broad' method, to bring the separated parts of the muscles together to one another with sutures.

Th. 367 ; ἕτερον τοσοῦτον as much again, Hdt. 2.149 ; ἑτέρου τοσούτου χρόνου for as long again, Isoc. 4.153 ; ἕ. τοιαῦτα other things of like kind, Hdt. 1.120 , 191 ; ἑτέρων τοιῶνδε (sc. ἀνθρώπων) ἄρχεις ib. 207 ; τῷ αὐτῷ τρόπῳ . . τῷ ἑτέρῳ in the same way over again, Id. 2.127 ; ἄλλα τε τοιαῦθ' ἕτερα μυρία Ar. Pol. 1294a25 , cf. 1286b21 . other than should be, euphem. for κακός, παθεῖν μὲν εὖ, παθεῖν δὲ θάτερα S. Ph. 503 ; ἀγάθ' ἢ θάτερα, ἵνα μηδὲν εἴπω φλαῦρον D. 22.12 : abs., δαίμων ἕ. Pi. P. 3.34 ; λέκτρα, συμφοραί, E. Med. 639 (lyr.), HF 1238 ; ἐὰν τὰ ἕ. ψηφίσωνται οἱ δικασταί D. 48.30 ; πλέον θάτερον ἐποίησαν did more harm (than good), Isoc. 19.25 , cf. Pl. Phd. 114e , Euthd. 280e , Aristid. 2.117 J. Special Phrases: elliptical, mostly in dat. fem., τῇ ἑτέρᾳ (sc. χειρί), Ep. ἑτέρῃ or ἑτέρηφι, with one hand (v. sub init.); with the left hand, Od. 3.441 , Il. 22.80 , Theoc. 24.45 : hence prov., οὐ τῇ ἑτέρᾳ ληπτός not to be caught with one hand, Pl. Sph. 226a ; ἐκ δ' ἑτέρης A.R. 1.1115 , AP 9.650 ( Leont. ). θατέρᾳ (sc. ἡμέρᾳ) on the morrow, S. OT 782 , E. Rh. 449 ; τῆς ἑτέρας Pl. Cri. 44a ; but τῇ ἑτέρᾳ on the following (i.e. the third) day, X. Cyr. 4.6.10 . (sc. ὁδῷ) in another or a different way, καὶ τῇδε φῦναι χἀτέρᾳ S. OC 1444 ; another way, τρέπεσθαι Ar. Nu. 812 ; ἑτέρᾳ πῃ Id. Eq. 35 ; τότ' ἄλλοσ' . . , θατέρᾳ δὲ . . S. Tr. 272 ; θατέρᾳ . . , θατέρᾳ . . in one way . . , in the other . . , Henioch. 5.16 ; ἑτέρηφι Hes. Op. 216 : acc. ἑτέραν ἐκτρέπεσθαι Luc. Tim. 5 . adverb. with Preps.: ἐπὶ θάτερα to the one or the other side, one or the other way, ἐπὶ μὲν θάτερα . . , ἐπὶ θ. δὲ . . Hp. Art. 7 ; τότε μὲν ἐπὶ θάτερα, τότε δ' ἐπὶ θ. Pl. Prt. 314e : c. gen., ἐς τὰ ἐπὶ θ. τοῦ ποταμοῦ Th. 7.84 ; εἰς τἀπὶ θ. τῆς πόλεως X. HG 6.2.7 ; τὸ ἐπὶ θάτερον τῆς ῥινός Hp. Art. 35 . κατὰ θάτερα on the one or other side, κατὰ θ. ἀστός D. 57.30 ; ψόφου κατὰ θ. προσπεσόντος Plu. Brut. 51 , etc.; but καθ' ἕτερα at other points, Th. 7.42 . VA 3.39 . differently, rarely in Poetry, οὐχ ἑ. τις ἐρεῖ Theoc. Ep. 10.3 ; ἑ. ἔχειν to be different, Ar. Pl. 371 : freq. in Prose, ὡς ἑ. in the other way (cf. ὡς) , ἢν ἡ ἑτέρη γνάθος ἐκστῇ ὡς ἑ. χρὴ τὴν ἐπίδεσιν ἄγειν Hp. Art. 34 , cf. Pl. Sph. 266a , etc.; ἐάν τε καλῶς, ἐάν θ' ὡς ἑ. D. 18.85 , cf. 212 : c. gen., differently from, ἑ. πως τῶν εἰωθότων Pl. Plt. 295d ; ἑ. ἤπερ . . Ael. NA 12.28 . otherwise than should be, badly, wrongly, once in Hom. , ἑ. ἐβόλοντο Od. 1.234 ; εἰ καὶ ἑ. τοῦτο ἀπέβη SIG 851.10 (Marc.Aur.); εἴ τι ἑ. φρονεῖτε Ep.Phil. 3.15 .

english_sentence_A: Taking care, then, not to sew the tendons together along with them, having first stripped those away, I thus employed the sutures through a great depth, knowing that it is free of danger into the fleshy part itself of the muscles, whereas the danger arises from the tendons—and this too I had not seen any of my teachers doing.
english_sentence_B: Taking care, then, not to stitch the tendons together with them, I first stripped those away, and in this way I used the sutures through a great depth, knowing that there is no danger as regards the fleshy part itself of the muscles, but that the danger arises from the tendons; and I had not seen any of my teachers doing even this.

greek_sentence: τινὲς μὲν γὰρ αὐτῶν ἐν ταῖς τοιαύταις τρώσεσι τὰ τοῦ δέρματος χείλη μόνα συνέῤῥαπτον, ἔνιοι δὲ κατὰ τὰ σαρκώδη τοὺς μῦς αὐτοὺς τολμῶντες ῥάπτειν, ἐπιπολῆς αὐτῶν ἐποιοῦντο τὴν συναγωγὴν, ὥστε εἴ ποτε μέχρι βάθους συχνοῦ τὸ τραῦμα διῆκον ἐγεγόνει μὴ κατὰ τὸ μῆκος τοῦ κώλου, τὸ μὲν ἐπιπολῆς τοῦ μυὸς κολλᾶσθαι, τὸ δ’ ἄλλο πᾶν ἀκόλλητον μένειν.
english_sentence_A: For some of them, in wounds of this kind, used to sew together only the lips of the skin, while some, venturing to sew the muscles themselves in their fleshy parts, made the bringing-together of them at the surface, so that if ever the wound had come to extend to a considerable depth, not along the length of the limb, the surface of the muscle was agglutinated, while all the rest remained unagglutinated.
english_sentence_B: For some of them, in such woundings, sutured only the lips of the skin, while others, venturing to suture the muscles themselves at their fleshy parts, made the bringing-together superficially, so that if ever the wound had come about penetrating to a considerable depth, not along the length of the limb, the superficial part of the muscle would become agglutinated, but all the rest would remain unagglutinated.

english_sentence_A: At any rate, the best of the Empiricists of our time, who had read all the books of the anatomists, when a child at school had once made a stab with a stylus into the inner region of the upper arm, above its middle parts, applied one of the plaster drugs of which he had recently had experience as having cured a wound of a nerve, and seeing the child under it free of inflammation and free of pain, thought that it had been completely cured; but suddenly, on the seventh day, it died in convulsions.
english_sentence_B: At any rate the best of the Empiricists of our time, who had read all the books of the anatomists, once, when a child at a school had been pricked with a writing-stylus in the inner region of the arm, above its middle parts, applied one of the plaster drugs of which he had recently had experience, when it had treated a man wounded in a nerve. english_sentence_A: Some of the metallic substances do not even need to be pounded or sifted, since they are easily dissolved by the vinegar, as chalcitis and misy; but some require both to be pounded and sifted, like the scale of copper.

english_sentence_A: So then, as I said, let whatever drugs you are going to mix be triturated in the sun in the summer season for many [612] successive days, in the most acrid vinegar.

english_sentence_A: For the longer the time over which they are triturated, the more fine-particled they become and for this reason the more useful for narrow wounds, whereas in the case of exposed nerves at least one must guard against those that are excessively fine-particled and corrosive.

greek_sentence: σκεπασθέντος δὲ τοῦ γεγυμνωμένου νεύρου τοῖς μοτοῖς ἔξωθεν ἐπιβλητέον ἕν τι τῶν πρὸς τὰς στενὰς τρώσεις ἁρμοττόντων, ὧν ἐστι τέτταρα γένη, τουτὶ μὲν ἓν τὸ διὰ τῶν μεταλλικῶν, ὑπὲρ οὗ πρόκειται λέγειν, ἕτερον δὲ τὸ διὰ τῶν ὀπῶν, ἐν οἶς ἐστι καὶ τὸ δι’ εὐφορβίου, καὶ τρίτον τὸ διὰ τῆς κόπρου τῶν περιστερῶν, καὶ τέταρτον, ὃ καλῶ τὸ πρᾷον, ᾧ καὶ πρὸς τὰ τελέως γεγυμνωμένα νεῦρα τῶν [614] ἁπαλοσάρκων σωμάτων χρῶμαι.
english_sentence_A: Once the laid-bare nerve has been covered with the lint-plugs, one must apply on the outside one of the drugs suited to narrow wounds, of which there are four kinds: this one, the drug made of metallic substances, about which it is proposed to speak; another, the drug made of juices, among which is also the one made with euphorbium; a third, the drug made of pigeons' dung; and a fourth, which I call the mild one, which I use also for the completely laid-bare nerves of [614] soft-fleshed bodies.
english_sentence_B: When the exposed nerve has been covered with the pledgets, one must lay on from outside one of the remedies suited to narrow wounds. Of these there are four kinds: one is this one, the one made with metallic substances, about which it is proposed to speak; another is the one made with juices, among which is also the one with euphorbium; a third is the one made with pigeons' dung; and a fourth, which I call the mild one, which I also use for completely exposed nerves of [614] soft-fleshed bodies.

greek_sentence: τούτοις οὖν ὡς προείρηκα λειωθεῖσι μιγνύσθω κηροῦ κατὰ μὲν τὸ ἰσχυρότατον τὸ διπλάσιον, κατὰ δὲ τὸ ἀσθενέστατον δύο καὶ ἥμισυ μέρη, κατὰ δὲ τὸ μέσον ὃ μεταξὺ τούτων ἐστὶ μέρη δύο καὶ τέταρτον οἷον ἐπὶ τοῦ πρώτου γεγραμμένου τῶν τριῶν, ὅπερ ἰσχυρότατον ἔφην εἶναι, τὰ πάντα μέρη γίγνεται τὸν ἀριθμὸν ἐκ μίσυος καὶ χαλκίτεως καὶ λεπίδος ἀθροιζόμενα ἕξ.
english_sentence_A: To these, then, ground fine as I have said before, let wax be mixed: in the case of the strongest, double; in the case of the weakest, two and a half parts; and in the case of the middle one, which lies between these, two parts and a quarter. For example, in the case of the first of the three written down, which I said was the strongest, the total parts assembled from misy and chalcitis and scale come to six in number.
english_sentence_B: To these, then, ground fine as I said before, let wax be mixed: in the strongest, double the amount; in the weakest, two and a half parts; and in the middle one, which lies between these, two and a quarter parts. For instance, in the first written of the three, which I said was the strongest, all the parts, summed from misy, chalcitis and flake, come in number to six.

english_sentence_A: And in the case of the weakest, if there are six parts of the metallic substances, you would put in twelve parts of wax, and in the case of the middle one the amount between.

english_sentence_B: And so it is possible for you also to keep ready a drug of this kind, in which there is more [619] of the galbanum, for those who are sensitive, soft-fleshed and cacochymic.

lsj_entry_text: κατάντλ-ησις, εως, ἡ, = foreg., Hp. Medic. 3 , Antyll. ap. Orib. 9.23.1 , Gal. 10.237 .
greek_sentence: καὶ διὰ τοῦτο αὐτοῖς ἐπιτήδειός ἐστιν ἥ τε δι’ ἐλαίου κατάντλησις ἥ τε μίξις τῆς χαλβάνης ὁμοίως.
english_sentence_A: It is reasonable, then, that the drugs prepared from them appear rough and painful; and for this reason affusion with oil is suited to them, and likewise the admixture of galbanum.
english_sentence_B: And for this reason both the affusion of oil and, likewise, the admixture of galbanum are suitable for them.

lsj_entry_text: ὕαιν-α [υ], ἡ, prop. a fem. of ὗς: the striped hyena, a carnivorous animal with a bristly mane like a hog (whence the name), Hyaena striata, Hdt. 4.192 , Arist. HA 579b15 , Ael. NA 7.22 , Opp. C. 3.263 ; also called γλάνος, Arist. HA 594a31 ; cf. κροκόττας. a kind of antelope, Ael. NA 15.15 (s.v.l.). a sea-fish, Numen. ap. Ath. 7.326f , Ael. NA 13.27 ; also ὑαινίς, ίδος, ἡ, Epich. 65 ; v. ὗς 11 . in Porph. Abst. 4.16 ὑαίνας is most prob. an error for λεαίνας, as the corresponding masc. is λέοντες.
greek_sentence: ἐκλέγεσθαι δὲ καὶ τούτων ὅσα λεπτομερέστερα, τοιαῦτα δ’ ἐστὶ τά τε τῶν ἀγρίων ζώων καὶ μάλιστα λέοντός τε καὶ παρδάλεως καὶ ὑαίνης καὶ ἄρκτου, τά τε τῶν πτηνῶν καὶ μάλιστα τῶν χηνῶν.
english_sentence_A: Of these fats too one should select those that are finer in parts; such are those of wild animals, and especially of the lion, the leopard, the hyena and the bear, and those of birds, and especially of geese.
english_sentence_B: Of these too, select those that are finer-particled. Such are the fats of wild animals, especially of the lion, the leopard, the hyena and the bear, and those of birds, especially of geese.

Phdr. 260d . rustic, βίος Ar. Nu. 43 . of fruits, common, opp. γενναῖος, ὀπώρα Pl. Lg. 844d . (ἀγροῖκος dwelling in the country, ἄγροικος boorish, acc. to Ammon. greek_sentence: εἰ δὲ μὴ παρείη τοῦτο, τῶν ἀγροίκων ἀλεκτρυόνων τε καὶ ἀλεκτορίδων.
english_sentence_A: If this is not at hand, that of country cocks and hens.
english_sentence_B: If this is not available, use the fat of country cocks and hens.

english_sentence_B: If this is not available, use the fat of country cocks and hens.

english_sentence_A: In the same way one should also prefer the fat of country geese; for the fat of animals reared in cities, inasmuch as they are shut up in idleness, is moister and coarser in parts.
english_sentence_B: In the same way, prefer also the fat of country geese.

greek_sentence: τῶν γὰρ ἐν ταῖς πόλεσι τρεφομένων ζώων, ὡς ἂν ἀργῶν κατακεκλεισμένων, ὑγρότερόν τέ ἐστι καὶ παχυμερέστερον τὸ στέαρ.
english_sentence_A: In the same way one should also prefer the fat of country geese; for the fat of animals reared in cities, inasmuch as they are shut up in idleness, is moister and coarser in parts.
english_sentence_B: For in animals reared in the cities, being shut up idle, the fat is moister and thicker-particled.

english_sentence_A: But when the consistency of the drug is to be cerate-like, [620] let a third or a fourth part of wax be mixed in; or, if the fat should seem to you to be exceedingly moist, it is permissible to mix in even half as much wax, just as, if it should be dry, a fourth; and if it is in a middle state, a third.
english_sentence_B: When the consistency of the drug is to be something cerate-like, [620] let a third or a fourth part of wax be mixed in; or, if the fat should appear to you very moist, it is permissible to mix in even a half of wax, just as, if it should be dry, a fourth.

english_sentence_B: If, then, it is of the same year, it heats even more than the Cyrenaic juice, and especially more than that of the present day, ever since they have been making the plants grow by irrigation with water and preparing them for the production of a large quantity of juice. For after one year it is sufficiently hot, but already falls considerably short of the fresh.

greek_sentence: παρηγορηθέντος γὰρ οὕτως αὐτοῦ, πάλιν ἐπὶ τὴν ἀγωνιστικὴν ἀγωγὴν ἐπανελθεῖν ἔξεστιν, ἐγὼ γοῦν, ἐπιλυθέντος ποτὲ τοῦ νευροτρώτου μορίου, [633] θεασάμενος ἠρεθισμένον τὸ τραῦμα παρόντος κατὰ τύχην ὑγροῦ φαρμάκου, τοῦ διὰ τῶν στεάτων ὠτικοῦ, θερμήνας ἐπ’ ἀγγείου διπλοῦ, τοῦτο κατὰ τοῦ πεπονθότος ἐπιθεὶς μορίου, ταχίστην ὠφέλειαν ἐξ αὐτοῦ γενομένην εἶδον αὐτῇ τῇ τοῦ κάμνοντος αἰσθήσει, παραχρῆμα γὰρ ἀνώδυνος ἐγένετο καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα λυσάντων ἡμῶν αὐτὸ κατὰ φύσιν ἔχειν ἐφαίνετο.
english_sentence_A: For when it has been soothed in this way, it is possible to return again to the agonistic course of treatment. I, at any rate, when once a nerve-wounded part had been unbound, [633] seeing the wound irritated, and a liquid drug happening by chance to be at hand, the ear-remedy made with fats, warmed it in a double vessel and applied it to the affected part, and I saw a very swift benefit arising from it, by the very sensation of the patient; for he at once became free of pain, and afterwards, when we unbound it, it appeared to be in its natural condition.
english_sentence_B: For once it has been soothed in this way, it is possible to return again to the combative course of treatment. I at any rate, when on one occasion a nerve-wounded part had been unbandaged, [633] seeing the wound irritated, and there happening to be at hand a liquid drug, the ear-remedy made with fats, warmed it in a double vessel and applied it over the affected part, and I saw a very rapid benefit arise from it, by the very perception of the patient; for he at once became free of pain, and afterwards, when we unbandaged it, it appeared to be in its natural state.

greek_sentence: μὴ γοῦν μήτε τεχνικῶς αὐτῷ χρωμένου τοῦ προσφέροντος, ὡς ἤκουσεν ἐκ τίνων συνέκειτο, καὶ ἦν ἅπαντα εὔωνα, τοῦτο μὲν, ἔφη, τοῖς προσαίταις φύλαττε, τῶν πολυτελεστέρων δέ τι δίδαξόν με.
english_sentence_A: At any rate, not even (μὴ γοῦν μήτε) when the one who applied it did not use it skilfully, when he heard of what ingredients it was composed, and they were all cheap, 'this,' he said, 'keep for beggars; but teach me one of the more costly ones.'

greek_sentence: φάρμακα μέντοι τινὰς νευροτρωτοὺς θεραπεύειν ἐπαγγελλόμενα συνέθεσαν ἄνευ διορισμοῦ τε καὶ τρόπου χρήσεως ποικίλου [641] μήτε τὴν ἐπὶ τῶν στενῶν νυγμάτων ἀγωγὴν, ὁποία τις ἔσοιτο δηλώσαντες μήτε τὴν ἐπὶ τῶν εὐρυτέρων τρώσεων ἢ γεγυμνωμένου νεύρου ἢ τένοντος ἢ τεθλασμένου.
english_sentence_A: Drugs, however, that profess to treat certain persons with wounded nerves they did compose, but without distinction and without a varied mode of use, [641] indicating neither the treatment in the case of narrow punctures, of what sort it should be, nor that in the case of broader woundings, whether of a nerve or tendon laid bare or of one crushed; and much less, whether the affected part is already inflamed or has even come near to gangrene.
english_sentence_B: They did, however, compose drugs professing to cure certain patients wounded in a nerve, but without distinction and without a varied manner of use.

english_sentence_A: But since I learned that it was composed of a few of the naturally occurring substances, whereas the compound made from many I myself had at that time already prepared, I conceived the plan, by removing the greater number and composing another from a few, of examining afresh and testing through experience whether it appeared to fall short of the many-ingredient one by much or by little.
english_sentence_B: So I had in mind to remove most of the ingredients, compose another drug from a few, and then examine it again and test it by experience, to see whether it appeared to fall short of the many-ingredient drug by a great deal or by a little.

english_sentence_A: In this, then, the physician trained in the art is better than the one who treats an ulcer through experience alone, inasmuch as he knows that the ulcer is treated by drugs through no other power than that of rendering the part as dry as it was when it was in its natural state.

greek_sentence: ἡ τελειοτάτη δὲ μέθοδος πᾶσα γέγραπται διὰ τῆς θεραπευτικῆς πραγματείας, ἐν ᾗ προτετεχνῶσθαι χρὴ τὸν μέλλοντα τελέως ὑπὸ τῶν νῦν λεγομένων ὠφεληθήσεσθαι.

greek_sentence: ἐὰν δὲ μηδὲ ἑνὸς τούτων δεώμεθα, τὴν ποσότητα τῆς ὑγρότητος ἐπισκεπτέον ἅμα τῷ ῥύπῳ καὶ οὕτω ἐπὶ τὸ προσῆκον ἰτέον φάρμακον, ἀναμνησθέντας ἑκάστου τῶν ἁπλῶν ὅσα τε ξηραίνει μὲν, οὐ μὴν ἀποῤῥύπτει γε τὸν ῥύπον τοῦ ἕλκους, ὅσα τε ῥύπτει μὲν, οὐ μὴν ξηραίνει γενναίως.
english_sentence_A: But if we need none of these, one must examine the quantity of the moisture together with the filth, and so proceed to the appropriate drug, having recalled, among each of the simples, which ones dry but do not cleanse away the filth of the ulcer, which ones cleanse but do not dry vigorously, and which ones are of such a nature as to do both, considering in addition of what order each one is—a matter which is the most important of those that bear upon the treatment, yet has been neglected by those who wrote the books on materia medica.
