lsj_entry_text: φάρμακον [v. sub fin.], τό, drug, whether healing or noxious: in Hom. the sense is freq. determined by an epith., φάρμακα, πολλὰ μὲν ἐσθλὰ . . , πολλὰ δὲ λυγρά Od. 4.230 ; τόδε φ. ἐσθλόν 10.287 , cf. 292 ; φ. ἤπια, ὀδυνήφατα (v. infr. 2 ); κακὰ φ. ib. 213 ; φ. λυγρά ib. 236 ; φ. οὐλόμενον ib. 394 ; ἀνδροφόνον 1.261 ; θυμοφθόρα φ. 2.329 ; so, after Hom. , προσανέα φ. Pi. P. 3.52 ; παιώνια A. Ag. 848 ; χρήσιμον Pl. R. 382c ; θανάσιμα Ph. Bel. 103.31 ; ὀλέθριον Luc. Herm. 62 . healing remedy, medicine, in Hom. mostly of those applied outwardly, ἐπιθήσει φάρμαχ' ἅ κεν παύσῃσι μελαινάων ὀδυνάων Il. 4.191 ; ἐπ' ἄρ' ἤπια φάρμακα πάσσε ib. 218 ; ὀδυνήφατα φ. πάσσων 5.401 , 900 , cf. 11.515 , 830 , 15.394 ; προσάλειφεν ἑκάστῳ φ. Od. 10.392 ; φ. περιαλείφειν Ar. Eq. 906 ; also of potions, πιὼν φάρμακ' Od. 10.326 ; φ. πεπωκώς Hdt. 4.160 , cf. Pi. l. c.; παρὰ τοῦ ἰατροῦ Pl. R. 406d , cf. Grg. 467c ; φ. χριστόν E. Hipp. 516 ; ἔγχριστον Theoc. 11.1 ; ἐπίχριστον Str. 17.1.10 ; ἐπίπαστον Theoc. l. c.; καταπλαστόν Ar. Pl. 716 ; ποτόν E. Hipp. l.c.; freq. in Medic. writers, Sor. 1.4 , Gal. 6.265 , etc.; of medicines for cattle, PFlor. 222.11 (iii A. D.). c. gen. (v. infr. 11 ), φ. νόσου a medicine for it, remedy against it, A. Pr. 251 , 606 (lyr.); βηχός Phryn.Com. 60 : κεφαλῆς for a head-ache, Pl. Chrm. 155b ; στραγγουρίας Arist. HA 612b16 , cf. 624a16 ; μέθης Amphis 37 ; δίψης AP 6.170 ( Thyill. ); but ὑγιείας φ. a medicine to restore or maintain health, Aristid. Or. 37(2).11 . enchanted potion, philtre: hence, charm, spell, Od. 4.220 sq., Ar. Pl. 302 , Theoc. 2.15 , PSI 1.64.20 (i B. C.); φαρμάκοις τὸν ἄνδρ' ἔμηνεν Ar. Th. 561 ; τοιαῦτα ἔχω φ. such charms have I, Hdt. 3.85 , cf. Apoc. 9.21 . poison, S. Tr. 685 , E. Med. 385 ; πιεῖν τὸ φ. Antipho 6.15 , Pl. Phd. 57a , 115a ; φάρμακα ἐσβεβληκέναι ἐς τὰ φρέατα Th. 2.48 ; φ. δηλητήρια SIG 37 A 1 (Teos, v B. C.); τοξικὸν φ. BGU 21 ii 14 (iv A. D.). lye for laundering, Stud.Pal. 22.56.12 (iii A. D.). generally, remedy, cure, Hes. Op. 485 , Alc. 35 , etc.; μεῖζον . . τῆς νόσου τὸ φ. the cure too strong for, i. e. worse than, the disease, S. Fr. 589.4 , cf. Com.Adesp. 455 ; φ. πραΰ, of a bridle, Pi. O. 13.85 ; φ. τινι for a thing, Thgn. 1134 (pl.), Archil. 9 ; πρός τι Arist. Pol. 1321a16 ; ποττὸν ἔρωτα Theoc. 11.1 ; but most freq. φ. τινός remedy against . . χλαῖνα . . φ. ῥίγευς Hippon. 19 ; Ζεὺς πάντων φ. μοῦνος ἔχει Simon. 87 ; τὸ σιγᾶν φ. βλάβης ἔχω A. Ag. 548 ; φ. πόνων, λύπης, E. Ba. 283 , Fr. 1079 ; δόλοι . . χρείας ἀνάνδρου φ. ib. 288 ; φόβου Pl. Lg. 647e ; λήθης φάρμακα (of γράμματα) E. Fr. 578.1 ; v. εὐδιανός. c. gen. also, a means of producing something, φ. σωτηρίας Id. Ph. 893 ; μνήμης καὶ σοφίας φ. Pl. Phdr. 274e ; ὑπομνήσεως ib. 275a , cf. 230d ; ἀθανασίας Antiph. 86.6 ; ἡσυχίας Arist. Pol. 1273b23 ; φ. μανίας, of the oil applied to wrestlers, D.L. 1.104 . ἐπὶ θανάτῳ φ. ἑᾶς ἀρετᾶς εὑρέσθαι a remedy or consolation in his own virtue, Pi. P. 4.187 . dye, paint, colour, Emp. 23.3 , Hdt. 1.98 , A. Fr. 134 , Ar. Ec. 735 , Pl. R. 420c , Plt. 277c , PCair.Zen. 789.13 (iii B. english_sentence_A: It is best, then, to use drugs that have already given proof of themselves, in accordance with the method described.
english_sentence_B: Best, then, is to use drugs that have already given proof, in accordance with the method stated.

lsj_entry_text: μέθοδ-ος, ἡ, (μετά, ὁδός) following after, pursuit, νύμφης μέθοδον ποιεῖσθαι Anon. ap. Suid. s.v. ζεῦγος ἡμιονικόν ( EM 409.35 ):—hence, pursuit of knowledge, investigation, Pl. greek_sentence: εἰ δ’, ὡς ἔφην, ἀπορήσαιμέν ποτε τούτων, ἕξιν ἔχειν αὐτοὺς τοιαύτην, ὡς δύνασθαι συντιθέναι παραπλήσια τοῖς ἤδη δεδωκόσιν ἱκανὴν πεῖραν, ὥσπερ πολλάκις κᾀμὲ ὁρᾶτε πράττοντα [862] κατά γε τὰς ἀποδημίας καὶ ἄλλως.
english_sentence_A: But if, as I said, we should ever be at a loss for these, [it is best] that they themselves possess such a habit as to be able to compose drugs resembling those that have already given sufficient proof, just as you often see me too doing, [862] both on journeys abroad and otherwise.
english_sentence_B: But if, as I said, we should at some time lack these, [it is best] that we ourselves have such a trained disposition as to be able to compound drugs similar to those that have already given sufficient proof by experience, as you often see me doing too, [862] at least on journeys abroad, and in other circumstances as well.

greek_sentence: τὴν μὲν γὰρ πρώτην αὐτῶν σύνθεσιν ἐκ στοχασμοῦ τεχνικοῦ ποιούμεθα, μετὰ ταῦτα δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς πείρας, ἐνίων μὲν φανέντων δοκιμωτάτων, ἐνίων δ’ ἀπολειπομένων τοῦ σκοποῦ, δευτέρα πάλιν ἐπανόρθωσις γίνεται.

english_sentence_A: [863] [The plaster through herbs, of Crito.] The plaster through herbs, which I use, works against carcinomata and putrefactions; it brings scrofulous swellings (choirades) to suppuration and, pressing them out, removes leprai and dissolves boils (dothienes); it is suited to gouty patients and dissolves calluses (poroi); the same is a cephalic plaster, which without trepanation detaches scales of bone, brings up bones, and scrapes the bones to some extent; the same, for freshly inflicted wounds and for spreading sores (nomai), applied on lint, cleanses thoroughly and fills up, together with rose cerate, one part being mixed to two parts of cerate, and sometimes three or four; and with myrtle cerate, in two or three parts, it cicatrizes.
english_sentence_B: [863] [The plaster from herbs of Criton.] The plaster from herbs, which I use, is effective against carcinomas and putrefactions; bringing choirades to suppuration and squeezing them out, it removes lepras and dissolves boils; it is suitable for gouty patients; it dissolves calluses; the same, as a cephalic, removes scales of bone without trepanation, brings up bones, and scrapes the bones to some extent; the same is for freshly inflicted wounds; for spreading ulcers, applied on lint, it cleans them out; it fills in with rose cerate, one part being mixed to two parts of cerate, and sometimes to three or four.

greek_sentence: συνετοῦ μὲν τοίνυν ἐστὶ χρεία καὶ τετριμμένου περὶ τὴν τῶν [872] τοιούτων φαρμάκων χρῆσιν, ἐν ἀρχῇ μὲν εὐθέως ἐπινοοῦντος ποσαπλὰ δεῖται μίγνυσθαι τῇ κηρωτῇ, μετὰ δὲ τὴν πρώτην χρῆσιν ἔτι δριμυτέρου τοῦ φαρμάκου φανέντος ἢ ὥστε σαρκοῦν δύνασθαι, στοχάσασθαι πόσον ἔτι προσθεῖναι δεῖ τῆς κηρωτῆς, ὥσπερ ἐπὶ τῆς προκειμένης ὁ Κρίτων ἐποίησε.
english_sentence_A: There is need, therefore, of an intelligent man and one practised in the use of [872] such drugs, who at the very outset considers how many times over it needs to be mixed with the cerate, and who, after the first use, if the drug still appears sharper than to be able to produce flesh, conjectures how much more of the cerate must still be added, as Criton did in the case of the present one.
english_sentence_B: There is need, then, of an intelligent man, practised in the use of such [872] drugs, one who considers straightaway at the outset how many times its amount of cerate the drug needs to be mixed with, and who, if after the first application the drug still appears too pungent to be able to make flesh grow, estimates how much more of the cerate must still be added, just as Criton did with the plaster before us.

english_sentence_A: But since, as I said, in accordance with the amount of filth and the moistness of the ulcer, and the sensitivity or insensitivity of the parts that share in the affection, and further the softness and hardness of the bodily habit, the quantity of the cerate that is mixed in must be varied—which has been said many times—we must understand, keeping this in mind, that the quantity for use in such cases is written down with the road from there toward the other cases becoming easy for everyone in either direction [873] as far as the extremes.
english_sentence_B: Since, as I said, the quantity of cerate mixed in must be varied according to the amount of the filth and the moistness of the ulcer, the sensitivity or insensitivity of the parts that suffer along with it, and further the softness and the hardness of the habit of the body, as has been said many times, we must bear in mind and consider that in such recipes it is the quantity used that is written down, since for everyone the way from there towards the other cases in either [873] direction is easy, as far as the extremes.

greek_sentence: εἰκότως οὖν κατὰ τὸ προκείμενον φάρμακον, καίτοι σκοπὸν ἔχοντος θερμῆναί τε καὶ ξηρᾶναι καὶ διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ψύδρακας ποιεῖν, ἐμίχθη τι καὶ τῶν στυφόντων, ἀλλ’ οὐχ ἱκανά γε πρὸς πολλὰ θερμαίνοντα σφοδρῶς φάρμακα, δύο ταῦτα χάλκανθος καὶ ἅλες, ἀλλὰ καὶ λεπὶς χαλκοῦ κατὰ τὸν αὐτὸν [877] τὸν ἐμίχθη λογισμὸν ἥ τε στυπτηρία, διὰ τὸ σφοδρῶς στύφειν καὶ τοὔνομα λαβοῦσα τοῦτο.
english_sentence_A: Reasonably, then, in the case of the drug before us, although it has as its aim to heat and to dry, and for this reason also to produce psydrakes (pustules), something of the astringents too was mixed in — though not ones sufficient in relation to the many strongly heating drugs, these two, chalcanthum and salts; but scale of copper too was mixed in according to the same [877] reasoning, and alum, which has received this very name on account of its astringing strongly.
english_sentence_B: Reasonably, then, in the drug before us, although its aim is to heat and to dry and for this reason also to produce psydraces [pustules], something of the astringents too was mixed in. But since these two, chalcanthum and salt, are not sufficient against many violently heating drugs, copper flake too was mixed in by the same [877] reasoning, and so was alum, which also took this very name because it astringes violently.

greek_sentence: ἄλλην ἔμπλαστρον ἔγραψεν ὁ Κρίτων ἐνδοξοτάτην, ἣν ὀνομάζει Μεσιανὴν, ἕτερον ὕλης ἔχουσα γένος τῆς προγεγραμμένης καὶ τῆς μελλούσης ὑπ’ ἐμοῦ γραφήσεσθαι νῦν ἐφεξῆς, ἣν αὐτὸς ὁ Κρίτων ἀνίκητον ὀνομάζει, συγκειμένην ἐκ δριμέων τῶν πλείστων φαρμάκων, οὐκ οὔσης τῆς Μεσιανῆς τοιαύτης, ὡς μετὰ ταῦτα δειχθήσεται κατὰ τὸν οἰκεῖον αὐτῆς καιρόν.
english_sentence_A: Crito wrote another most renowned plaster, which he calls the Mesiane, having a different kind of material from the one written above and from the one about to be written by me now next in order, which Crito himself calls 'Invincible', being composed of drugs most of which are acrid, whereas the Mesiane is not of this sort, as will be shown after this at its own proper occasion.
english_sentence_B: Crito recorded another, very celebrated plaster, which he names the Mesian. Its material is of a different kind from that of the plaster written above, and from that of the one I am about to write next, which Crito himself names the invincible and which is composed mostly of acrid drugs.

II) ; Οὖτις ἐμοί γ' ὄ. 9.366 , cf. 18.5 , 19.183 , 247 ; Ἀρήτη δ' ὄνομ' ἐστὶν ἐπώνυμον 7.54 , cf. 19.409 , Hes. Th. 144 : in Prose ὄνομα is used abs., by name, πόλις ὄ. Καιναί X. An. 2.4.28 , etc. : also dat., πόλις Θάψακος ὀνόματι ib. 1.4.11 (v. l.) ; ὀνόματι λέγειν by name, Pl. Ap. 21c ; ἐπ' ὀνόματος δηλοῦσθαι Plb. 18.45.4 , etc. ; κατ' ὄνομα by name, Strato Com. 1.14 , Epigr.Gr. 983.4 (Philae) ; ἀσπάζου τοὺς φίλους κατ' ὄ. each by his name, 3 Ep.Jo. 14 . ὄ. τίθεσθαι or θέσθαι τινί give one a name, Od. 19.403 , 406 , 8.554 , A. Fr. 6 , Ar. Av. 810 :— Pass. , ὄ. κεῖταί τινι ib. 1291 ; ὄ. ἐστι or κεῖται ἐπί τινι, X. Mem. 3.14.2 , Cyr. 2.2.12 ; so ὄ. φέρειν or ἐπιφέρειν ἐπί τι, Arist. EN 1119a33 , HA 572a11 . ὄνομα καλεῖν τινα call one by name, εἴπ' ὄνομ', ὅττι σε κεῖθι κάλεον Od. 8.550 ; καλοῦσί με τοῦτο τὸ ὄ. X. Oec. 7.3 , cf. E. Ion 259 , 800 , Pl. Cra. 393e , etc. :—so in Pass. , ὄ. δ' ὠνομάζετο Ἕλενος S. Ph. 605 , cf. El. 694 ; ὄ. δημοκρατία κέκληται Th. 2.37 ; τὸ ἐναντίον ὄ. ἀφροσύνη μετωνόμασται Id. 1.122 ; ὄ. ἓν κεκλημένους Σικελιώτας Id. 4.64 ; λεγόμενοι τοὔνομα γεωργικοί Pl. Lg. 842e ; but also ὀνόματί τινα προσαγορεύειν Antipho 6.40 ; reversely, ὄνομα καλεῖν τινι give a name to, Pl. Plt. 279e , Cra. 385d ; ὄ. καλεῖν ἐπί τινι Id. Prm. 147d ; τύμβῳ δ' ὄ. σῷ κεκλήσεται . . Κυνὸς σῆμα E. Hec. 1271 ; τοὔνομα προσηγορεύθη Anaxil. 21.3 . name, fame, Ἰθάκης γε καὶ ἐς Τροίην ὄνομ' ἵκει Od. 13.248 ; οὐδὲ θανὼν ὄνομ' ὤλεσας 24.93 ; ὄ. ἔχειν or σχεῖν ἀπό τινος, Hdt. 1.71 , Pl. Hp.Ma. 282a ; τὸ μεγα ὄ. τῶν Ἀθηνῶν Th. 7.64 ; τῷ μέλλοντι χρόνῳ καταλιπεῖν ὄ. ὡς . . Id. 5.16 ; τοὔνομά τινος μεῖζον ἀφικνεῖται εἰς τὴν πόλιν X. An. 6.1.20 ; ὧν ὀνόματα μεγάλα λέγεται ἐπὶ σοφίᾳ Pl. Hp.Ma. 281c ; ὄ. μέγιστον ἔχειν Th. 2.64 ; ἐν ὀνόματι εἶναι to have a name, to be notable, Str. 9.1.23 ; οἱ ἐν πράγμασιν ἐπ' ὀνόματος γεγονότες Plb. 15.35.1 ; παράσιτοι δ' ἐπ' ὀνόματος ἐγένοντο notably, Ath. 6.240c ; τῶν δι' ὀνόματος παρασίτων ib. 241a . a name and nothing else, opp. the real person or thing, ἵνα μηδ' ὄνομ' αὐτοῦ ἐν ἀνθρώποισι λίπηται Od. 4.710 ; βοᾶς δ' ἔτι μηδ' ὄνομ' εἴη Theoc. 16.97 ; opp. ἔργον, E. Or. 454 , Hipp. 502 ; περὶ ὄ. μάχεσθαι Lys. 33.3 ; ἐκ τῶν ὀ. μᾶλλον ἢ τῶν πραγμάτων σκέψασθαι D. 9.15 ; ὀνόματι διαφέρεσθαι dispute about a word, Pl. Euthd. 285a , Lg. 644a . false name, pretence, pretext, ὀνόματι ἐννόμῳ ξυμμαχίας under the pretence . . , Th. 4.60 ; μετ' ὀνομάτων καλῶν Id. 5.89 ; χώρα καλῶν ὀ. καὶ προσχημάτων μεστή Pl. R. 495c , cf. Plb. 11.5.4 . in periphr. phrases, ὄ. τῆς σωτηρίας, = σωτηρία , E. IT 905 , cf. ὄνομ' ὁμιλίας ἐμῆς ( v. l. for ὄμμ' ) Id. Or. 1082 : with the names of persons, periphr. for the person, ὦ φίλτατον ὄ. Πολυνείκους Id. Ath. 6 , 10 (both pl.), Jahresh. 26 Beibl. 13 (Ephes., ii A. D., pl.) ; βαρέσαι τὸ ἐμὸν ὄ. charge my account, POxy. 126.8 (vi A. D.) ; τὸν τόκον τὸν ὀνόματί μου παραγραφέντα ib. 513.22 (ii A. D.) ; in registers of titledeeds, etc., οἰκίας οὐ κειμένης ἐν ὀνόματι τῆς ἀποδομένης not booked under the name of the seller, PLips. 3 ii 25 (iii A. Ath. 1.19 : generally, D. 19.187 . Gramm., word, opp. ῥῆμα (expression), Pl. Cra. 399b , cf. Ap. 17c , Smp. 198b , 199b , 221e , Isoc. 9.9 , 11 , Arist. Rh. 1404b5 , Aeschin. 3.72 , A.D. Synt. 12.25 , al., Demetr. Eloc. 23 , al. ; τὸ ἰλλαίνειν ὄ. the word ἰλλαίνειν, Gal. 17(1).679 . noun, opp. ῥῆμα (verb, predicate), Pl. Tht. 168b , Sph. 262a , 262b , cf. Arist. (along with ὀνομάζω, as 2.50 , 4.35 , al.), and sts. in other Ion. prose authors (v.l. in Hp. Prog. 25 , etc.), but is prob. not Ionic ; Ion. Inscrr. have only ὄνομα, IG 7.235.39 (Oropus), etc.: Hom. has οὔνομα Od. 6.194 , 9.355 , Il. 3.235 , οὐνόματ'ʽἀ 17.260 , ὄνομα Od. 9.16 , 364 , 366 , 19.183 , ὄνομ'ʽἀ 4.710 et saep. :—name of a person or thing, in Hom. always of a person, exc. ἐρέω δέ τοι οὔνομα λαῶν Od. 6.194 and in Od. 13.248 (v. infr. II) ; Οὖτις ἐμοί γ' ὄ. 9.366 , cf. 18.5 , 19.183 , 247 ; Ἀρήτη δ' ὄνομ' ἐστὶν ἐπώνυμον 7.54 , cf. 19.409 , Hes. Th. 144 : in Prose ὄνομα is used abs., by name, πόλις ὄ. Καιναί X. An. 2.4.28 , etc. : also dat., πόλις Θάψακος ὀνόματι ib. 1.4.11 (v. l.) ; ὀνόματι λέγειν by name, Pl. Ap. 21c ; ἐπ' ὀνόματος δηλοῦσθαι Plb. 18.45.4 , etc. ; κατ' ὄνομα by name, Strato Com. 1.14 , Epigr.Gr. 983.4 (Philae) ; ἀσπάζου τοὺς φίλους κατ' ὄ. each by his name, 3 Ep.Jo. 14 . ὄ. τίθεσθαι or θέσθαι τινί give one a name, Od. 19.403 , 406 , 8.554 , A. Cra. 393e , etc. :—so in Pass. , ὄ. δ' ὠνομάζετο Ἕλενος S. Ph. 605 , cf. El. 694 ; ὄ. δημοκρατία κέκληται Th. 2.37 ; τὸ ἐναντίον ὄ. ἀφροσύνη μετωνόμασται Id. 1.122 ; ὄ. ἓν κεκλημένους Σικελιώτας Id. 4.64 ; λεγόμενοι τοὔνομα γεωργικοί Pl. Κυνὸς σῆμα E. Hec. 1271 ; τοὔνομα προσηγορεύθη Anaxil. 21.3 . name, fame, Ἰθάκης γε καὶ ἐς Τροίην ὄνομ' ἵκει Od. 13.248 ; οὐδὲ θανὼν ὄνομ' ὤλεσας 24.93 ; ὄ. ἔχειν or σχεῖν ἀπό τινος, Hdt. 1.71 , Pl. Hp.Ma. 282a ; τὸ μεγα ὄ. τῶν Ἀθηνῶν Th. 7.64 ; τῷ μέλλοντι χρόνῳ καταλιπεῖν ὄ. ὡς . . Id. 5.16 ; τοὔνομά τινος μεῖζον ἀφικνεῖται εἰς τὴν πόλιν X. An. 6.1.20 ; ὧν ὀνόματα μεγάλα λέγεται ἐπὶ σοφίᾳ Pl. Hp.Ma. 281c ; ὄ. μέγιστον ἔχειν Th. 2.64 ; ἐν ὀνόματι εἶναι to have a name, to be notable, Str. 9.1.23 ; οἱ ἐν πράγμασιν ἐπ' ὀνόματος γεγονότες Plb. 15.35.1 ; παράσιτοι δ' ἐπ' ὀνόματος ἐγένοντο notably, Ath. 6.240c ; τῶν δι' ὀνόματος παρασίτων ib. 241a . a name and nothing else, opp. the real person or thing, ἵνα μηδ' ὄνομ' αὐτοῦ ἐν ἀνθρώποισι λίπηται Od. 4.710 ; βοᾶς δ' ἔτι μηδ' ὄνομ' εἴη Theoc. 16.97 ; opp. ἔργον, E. Or. 454 , Hipp. 502 ; περὶ ὄ. μάχεσθαι Lys. 33.3 ; ἐκ τῶν ὀ. μᾶλλον ἢ τῶν πραγμάτων σκέψασθαι D. 9.15 ; ὀνόματι διαφέρεσθαι dispute about a word, Pl. Euthd. 285a , Lg. 644a . false name, pretence, pretext, ὀνόματι ἐννόμῳ ξυμμαχίας under the pretence . . , Th. 4.60 ; μετ' ὀνομάτων καλῶν Id. 5.89 ; χώρα καλῶν ὀ. καὶ προσχημάτων μεστή Pl. Or. 1082 : with the names of persons, periphr. for the person, ὦ φίλτατον ὄ. Πολυνείκους Id. Ph. 1702 . of persons, ὄχλος ὀνομάτων Act.Ap. 1.15 ; ἕτερα ὀ. ἀντ' αὐτοῦ . . πέμψαι Wilcken Chr. 28.19 (ii A. D.) ; in Accountancy, both of persons and things (cf. Lat. nomen), Hyp. english_sentence_A: For indeed this was shown to be necessary for a ready supply of remedies, and not only so that you yourselves too may be able, without prepared drugs, in situations of want to be well supplied with remedies—as Erasistratus once found a supply of the juice of herbs when he did not have a stomatic drug with him in that place on his journey—but also so that, even if you lose the written recipes of those who compounded them, you yourselves may nevertheless be able [889] to compound ones closely similar to those that were lost.
english_sentence_B: For it was shown that this is necessary for a ready supply of remedies, and not only so that you yourselves may be able, without prepared drugs, to be well supplied with remedies in situations of want, as Erasistratus once supplied himself with the juice of herbs when his mouth-drug was not at hand in that place on his journey, but also so that, even if you lose the written recipes of what you yourselves have compounded, you may nevertheless be able yourselves to [889] compound drugs closely similar to those that were lost.

lsj_entry_text: οἷος, οἵα, Ion. οἵη, οἷον, ʽὅσʼ such as, of what sort, relat. and indirect interrog. Pron., correl. to direct interrog. ποῖος, indef. ποιός, demonstr. τοῖος : ὅσσος ἔην οἷός τε Il. 24.630 ; ὁσσάτιόν τε καὶ οἷον 5.758 : c. acc., οἶδ' ἀρετὴν οἷός ἐσσι what a man for valour, 13.275 : freq. to be rendered by an Adv., οἷος πόλεμόνδε μέτεισι as he rushes into war, ib. 298 , etc. :—Usage: οἷος in an independent sentence as an exclam. of astonishment, ὢ πόποι . . , οἷον ἔειπες Il. 7.455 ; οἷ. τὸ πῦρ what a fire is this ! A. Ag. 1256 , cf. Pers. 733 , al. ; οἷ. εἰργάσασθε Pl. R. 450a ; οἷ. ἄνδρα λέγεις ἐν κινδύνῳ εἶναι Id. Tht. 142b ; οἷα ποιεῖς Id. Euthphr. 15e , etc. : so in neut. as Adv., v. infr. v. 1 . in indirect sentences, S. OT 624 , 1402 , 1488 , etc. ; ὁρᾶτε δὴ ἐν οἵῳ ἐστέ X. Cyr. 3.2.12 ; ὁρῶν ἐν οἵοις ἐσμέν Id. An. 3.1.15 . more freq. as relat. to a demonstr. τοῖος, τοιόσδε, τοιοῦτος, or to ὁ , ὅδε, as τῷ ἴκελον, οἷόν ποτε Δαίδαλος ἤσκησεν Il. 18.591 ; θέαμα τοιοῦτον οἷ. καὶ στυγοῦντ' ἐποικτίσαι S. OT 1296 : but the demonstr. Pron. is freq. omitted, οὐ γὰρ ἐμὴ ἲς ἔσθ' οἵη πάρος ἔσκεν Il. 11.669 , etc. ; οἷ. καὶ Πάρις . . ᾔσχυνε like as Paris also . . , A. Ag. 399 (lyr.), cf. Pers. 21 , al. : with δή added, τοιόνδ', οἷ. δὴ σύ such as you surely are, Il. 24.376 , v. infr. v. 2 : with περ added, οἵη περ φύλλων γενεή, τοίη δὲ καὶ ἀνδρῶν just such as . . , 6.146 , cf. A. Ag. 607 , 1046 , X. Cyr. 1.6.19 : very freq. with τε added (this οἷός τε must be distd. from οἷός τε c. inf., v. infr. 111.2 ), οἷός τε πελώριος ἔρχεται Ἄρης Il. 7.208 , cf. 17.157 , Od. 7.106 , etc. ; οἷός που 20.35 : οἷός τις, οἷόν τι generalizes a Comparison, the sort of person who . . , thing which . . , Il. 5.638 , Od. 9.348 ; οἶσθα εἰς οἷόν τινα κίνδυνον ἔρχει . . ; Pl. Prt. 313a ; with attraction of οἷος to the case of its antecedent (which may follow instead of preceding), οἵοις περ σὺ χρώμενοι συμβούλοις D. 24.185 ; and with further attraction of the subject of the relat. clause, οὐ γάρ πω τοίους ἴδον ἀνέρας . . , οἷον Πειρίθοον (for οἷος Πειρίθοος) Il. 1.263 ; πρὸς ἄνδρας τολμηρούς, οἵους καὶ Ἀθηναίους Th. 7.21 , cf. X. Mem. 2.9.3 ; περὶ τοῦ τοιούτου . . , οἵου τοῦ ἑνός Pl. Prm. 161b . οἷος, οἵα, οἷον freq. introduce an 'indirect exclamation', giving the reason for what precedes, ἄνακτα χόλος λάβεν, οἷον ἄκουσε because of what he heard, Il. 6.166 , cf. Od. 17.479 ; ἐμακάριζον τὴν μητέρα οἵων τέκνων ἐκύρησε Hdt. 1.31 ; ἀγανάκτησιν ἔχει ὑφ' οἵων κακοπαθεῖ Th. 2.41 ; τὴν ἐμαυτοῦ τύχην [ἀπέκλαον], οἵου ἀνδρὸς . . ἐστερημένος εἴην Pl. Phd. 117c , cf. S. OT 701 . sts. in Hom. οἷος introduces the reason for saying what is said, ὠκύμορος . . ἔσσεαι, οἷ' ἀγορεύεις Il. 18.95 , cf. Od. 4.611 ; αἲ γάρ με θυμὸς ἀνείη ὤμ' ἀποταμνόμενον κρέα ἔδμεναι, οἷα ἔοργας Il. 22.347 . οἷα δὴ εἴπας saying so and so, Hdt. 1.86 (cf. ὅσος 111.2 ) : later with other Particles, v. infr. VI. οὐδὲν οἷον . . there's nothing like . . , ἀλλ' οὐδὲν οἷ. ἐστ' ἀκοῦσαι τῶν ἐπῶν there's nothing like hearing the verses, Ar. Av. 966 , cf. Lys. 135 ; οὐδὲν γὰρ οἷ. ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ τοῦ νόμου D. 21.46 , cf. Pl. Grg. 447c , 481b , X. Oec. 3.14 . never used like Adv. οἷον (infr. V. I) with an Adj. = how, for in Il. 11.653 , οἶσθα . . οἷ. ἐκεῖνος δεινὸς ἀνήρ = what manner of man, namely dread, cf. 15.94 , 21.108 , Od. 19.493 , etc. as indef., a sort or kind of . . , ὁ δ' ἕτερος οἷός ἐστιν οἰκουρὸς μόνον only a kind of watch-dog, Ar. V. 970 ; so with Adj., ἀφόρητος οἷος . . κρυμός of an intolerable kind, Hdt. 4.28 ; θαυμαστὸς οἷος of a wonderful nature, Luc. Zeux. 6 ; οἷος ἔμπειρος πολέμου rather skilled in war, D. 2.18 ; οἷον τετανότριχα rather straight-haired, Pl. Euthphr. 2b ; freq. with Sup. , χωρίον οἷον χαλεπώτατον country of a very difficult kind, X. An. 4.8.2 , cf. Ar. Eq. 978 , Ach. 384 , Pl. Ap. 23a ; ἀνὴρ οἷος κράτιστος Arist. EN 1165b27 ; κόλπος οἷος βαθύτατος Ael. NA 14.26 : in some of these passages with Sup. it is possible to take οἷος as relat., supplying δυνατόν, cf. ξύμμαχος ἔσομαι οἷος ἂν δύνωμαι ἄριστος IG 12.39.28 . οἷος c. inf. implies fitness or ability for a thing, οὐ γὰρ ἦν ὥρα οἵα τὸ πεδίον ἄρδειν fit for watering, X. An. 2.3.13 , cf. Pl. Grg. 487d ; οἷοι φιλεῖν, μισεῖν, etc., D. 25.2 , etc. : freq. with τοιοῦτος expressed, τοιοῦτός τις οἷ. διαπονεῖσθαι Pl. Cra. 395a , cf. R. 415e ; τὸ πρᾶγμα μέγα . . καὶ μὴ οἷ. νεωτέρῳ βουλεύσασθαι not proper for a young man to advise upon, Th. 6.12 : without inf., λόγους οἵους εἰς τὰ δικαστήρια Pl. Euthd. 272a . οἷός εἰμι I intend, ἐβιάζετο . . καὶ οἷος ἦν ἐξευρεῖν τὴν θύραν Lys. Fr. 159 S. , cf. D. 4.9 , al., Is. 8.21 ; οἷος ἦν κατεσθίειν was on the point of eating, Antig. Car. ap. Ath. 7.345d . more freq. οἷός τε c. inf., fit or able to do, λιποίμην οἷός τ' . . ἀέθλια κάλ' ἀνελέσθαι Od. 21.117 (preceded by τοῖον ib. 173 ), Hdt. 1.29 , 67 , 91 ; λέγειν οἷός τε κἀγώ Ar. Eq. 343 , cf. Th. 3.16 , Isoc. 8.69 , etc. ; inclined to . . , Plb. 3.90.5 , J. AJ 4.6.3 : most freq. in neut. sg. and pl., οἷόν τε [ἐστί] it is possible to . . , Th. 1.80 , etc. ; οἷά τε [ἐστί] Hdt. 1.194 , etc. ; a dat. is sts. added, μὴ οἷόν τε εἶναι ἐμοὶ κωλῦσαι Th. 7.14 . without inf., πάνυ προθύμως ὡς οἷός τ' ἦν ἐπήραξεν Pl. Im. 3 . sts. twice in the same clause, οἷ' ἔργα δράσας οἷα λαγχάνει κακά after what deeds what sufferings are his ! S. El. 751 ; ἱερῶν οἵαν οἵων χάριν ἠνύσω what thanks for what offerings ! Id. greek_sentence: ἡ μὲν γὰρ καθόλου μέθοδος οὔτε μετὰ διορισμῶν ἀκριβῶς οὔτ’ ἄνευ διορισμῶν ἐλλιπῶς ἐγράφη τινὶ τῶν πρόσθεν, ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ φάρμακον ἐπαγγελλόμενον ἰᾶσθαι τοὺς νυγέντας νεῦρον ὑπό τινος ὀξέος, οἷαί πέρ εἰσιν αἱ βελόναι καὶ τὰ γραφεῖα τῶν παιδίων, ἔγραψέ τις αὐτὸ τοῦτο μόνον ἄριστα ποιεῖν δυνάμενον, ἐμοῦ πλῆθος οὐκ εὐαρίθμητον ἐν τῷ προειρημένῳ γράμματι διελθόντος αὐτῶν.
english_sentence_A: For the general method was written by none of my predecessors, neither accurately with distinctions nor deficiently without distinctions; but neither did anyone write down a drug professing to cure those who have been pricked in a nerve by some sharp object—such as needles and children's styluses are—a drug able to do this one thing alone excellently, whereas I went through a not easily counted multitude of them in the aforementioned book.
english_sentence_B: For the general method was written by none of my predecessors, neither precisely, with distinctions, nor even defectively, without distinctions. Nor did anyone so much as write down a drug professing to heal those pricked in a nerve by something sharp, such as needles and children's styluses, a drug able to do excellently this one thing alone, whereas I went through a number of them not easily counted in the aforementioned book.

english_sentence_A: Some of them, however, who wrote down notable drugs of many uses (polychrēsta) — those at least who were more careful — added, in addition to the other things they profess these drugs [890] to do, sometimes that they are beneficial also for those wounded in the nerves, at other times for severings of nerves and muscles, and there are times when they said that they also help punctures or contusions of them.
english_sentence_B: Some of them, however, having written up noteworthy polychrest drugs (those, at least, who were more careful), added, besides the other things which they profess [890] these do, sometimes that they are also beneficial to the nerve-wounded, at other times that they are so for severances of the nerves and muscles, and there are times when they said that they also help punctures or contusions of these.

english_sentence_A: Now if, having first stated the power of each of the simple drugs, as we did in eleven books, and having also written some general method of the composition of drugs, as I did in the book preceding this one, he had proposed such recipes to the others then living for the sake of exercise, so that they might answer for which affections it can be useful, we would truly have praised his teaching.
english_sentence_B: Now if, after first stating the potency of each of the simple drugs, as we have done in eleven treatises, and after writing some general method for the composition of drugs, as I have done in the book before this one, he had then set such prescriptions before others still living for the sake of exercise, so that they might answer for what affections the drug can be useful, we would truly have praised his teaching.

lsj_entry_text: χίλιοι [χι], αι , α: gen. pl. fem. χιλιῶν, irreg. in Att. acc. to Hdn. Gr. 1.426 (prob. only when χίλιαι was used as a fem. Subst. (v. infr. 3 )); dat. pl. fem. (orig. loc.) χιλίασιν IG 12.10.18 ; χιλίαισι ib. 76.20 , 94.10 ; later χιλίαις: dialect forms, Locr. χίλιοι (as in Att. , v. supr.) IG 9(1).334.39 (Oeanthea, v B. C.); Dor. χήλιοι (written χέλ-) ib. 5(1).1.23 (Sparta, v B. C.), Lesb., Thess. χέλλιοι EM 817.1 (cf. χελληστύς), IG 9(2).1229.29 (Phalanna, ii B. C.); Ion. χείλιοι Schwyzer 688 C 15 (Chios, v B. C.), which shd. prob. be restored in Hom. , cf. δεκάχʽἐιλοι :—a thousand, Hom. only in neut., χ. μέτρα, πυρά, Il. 7.471 , 8.562 ; πρῶθ' ἑκατὸν βοῦς δῶκεν, ἔπειτα δὲ χίλι' ὑπέστη (sc. πρόβατα) , αἶγας ὁμοῦ καὶ ὄϊς 11.244 : usu. agreeing with its Subst., Hes. Th. 364 , etc.; but sts. as Subst. folld. by gen., χίλιοι Μακεδόνων Th. 2.80 : to express the addition of a smaller number, that number may either precede or follow, διακόσιοι καὶ χ. Isoc. 4.87 , 93 , Pl. Criti. 119b : but χ. καὶ πεντακόσιοι Aeschin. 2.77 ; later καί is freq. omitted, Plb. 3.33.10 , LXX Da. 12.11 , Apoc. 11.3 ; with Preps. χ. ἐπὶ μυρίοις Pl. Lg. 895a ; τέτταρας πρὸς τοῖς χ. Luc. Cat. 4 ; οἱ χ. λογάδες (at Argos) the Thousand, Th. 5.67 , cf. D.S. 12.80 . sg. with collect. nouns, χιλίη ἵππος a thousand horse, Hdt. 5.63 , 7.41 ; τὴν ἵππον τὴν χιλίην Id. 8.113 ; so ἵππον ἔχω εἰς χιλίαν X. Cyr. 4.6.2 ; also χιλία ὁλοκαύτωσις burnt-offering of 1000 cattle, LXX 3 Ki. 3.4 . χίλιαι (sc. δραχμαί) as Subst., a thousand drachmae, περὶ χιλιῶν κινδυνεύειν D. 22.21 ; ἐν χιλίαις ὁ κίνδυνος ib. 26 (χ. δραχμαί in full, Pl. Ap. 36b ). (Cf. Skt. sahásram 'a thousand' (with prefix sa- = sṃ-); I.- E. ĝheslo-, ĝheslio-.)
greek_sentence: ἐν γὰρ τοῖς χιλίοις εἷς τις δοκεῖ τὸ τέλος ἔχειν τῆς τέχνης, οἱ δ’ ἄλλοι [892] τοῖς ἰδιώταις ὡσαύτως ἀγαπῶσιν, ἐὰν τοῖς σαφῶς γεγραμμένοις φαρμάκοις ὀρθῶς χρῆσθαι δύνωνται.
english_sentence_A: For among a thousand, some one person seems to possess the perfection of the art, while the rest, [892] just like laymen, are content if they are able to use correctly the drugs that have been clearly written up.
english_sentence_B: For among a thousand, some one person seems to possess the end of the art, while the others [892], just like laymen, are content if they are able to use correctly the drugs that have been clearly written down.

lsj_entry_text: φάρμακον [v. sub fin.], τό, drug, whether healing or noxious: in Hom. the sense is freq. determined by an epith., φάρμακα, πολλὰ μὲν ἐσθλὰ . . , πολλὰ δὲ λυγρά Od. 4.230 ; τόδε φ. ἐσθλόν 10.287 , cf. 292 ; φ. ἤπια, ὀδυνήφατα (v. infr. 2 ); κακὰ φ. ib. 213 ; φ. λυγρά ib. 236 ; φ. οὐλόμενον ib. 394 ; ἀνδροφόνον 1.261 ; θυμοφθόρα φ. 2.329 ; so, after Hom. , προσανέα φ. Pi. P. 3.52 ; παιώνια A. Ag. 848 ; χρήσιμον Pl. R. 382c ; θανάσιμα Ph. Bel. 103.31 ; ὀλέθριον Luc. Herm. 62 . healing remedy, medicine, in Hom. mostly of those applied outwardly, ἐπιθήσει φάρμαχ' ἅ κεν παύσῃσι μελαινάων ὀδυνάων Il. 4.191 ; ἐπ' ἄρ' ἤπια φάρμακα πάσσε ib. 218 ; ὀδυνήφατα φ. πάσσων 5.401 , 900 , cf. 11.515 , 830 , 15.394 ; προσάλειφεν ἑκάστῳ φ. Od. 10.392 ; φ. περιαλείφειν Ar. Eq. 906 ; also of potions, πιὼν φάρμακ' Od. 10.326 ; φ. πεπωκώς Hdt. 4.160 , cf. Pi. l. c.; παρὰ τοῦ ἰατροῦ Pl. R. 406d , cf. Grg. 467c ; φ. χριστόν E. Hipp. 516 ; ἔγχριστον Theoc. 11.1 ; ἐπίχριστον Str. 17.1.10 ; ἐπίπαστον Theoc. l. c.; καταπλαστόν Ar. Pl. 716 ; ποτόν E. Hipp. l.c.; freq. in Medic. writers, Sor. 1.4 , Gal. 6.265 , etc.; of medicines for cattle, PFlor. 222.11 (iii A. D.). c. gen. (v. infr. 11 ), φ. νόσου a medicine for it, remedy against it, A. Pr. 251 , 606 (lyr.); βηχός Phryn.Com. 60 : κεφαλῆς for a head-ache, Pl. Chrm. 155b ; στραγγουρίας Arist. HA 612b16 , cf. 624a16 ; μέθης Amphis 37 ; δίψης AP 6.170 ( Thyill. ); but ὑγιείας φ. a medicine to restore or maintain health, Aristid. Or. 37(2).11 . enchanted potion, philtre: hence, charm, spell, Od. 4.220 sq., Ar. Pl. 302 , Theoc. 2.15 , PSI 1.64.20 (i B. C.); φαρμάκοις τὸν ἄνδρ' ἔμηνεν Ar. Th. 561 ; τοιαῦτα ἔχω φ. such charms have I, Hdt. 3.85 , cf. Apoc. 9.21 . poison, S. Tr. 685 , E. Med. 385 ; πιεῖν τὸ φ. Antipho 6.15 , Pl. Phd. 57a , 115a ; φάρμακα ἐσβεβληκέναι ἐς τὰ φρέατα Th. 2.48 ; φ. δηλητήρια SIG 37 A 1 (Teos, v B. C.); τοξικὸν φ. BGU 21 ii 14 (iv A. D.). lye for laundering, Stud.Pal. 22.56.12 (iii A. D.). generally, remedy, cure, Hes. Op. 485 , Alc. 35 , etc.; μεῖζον . . τῆς νόσου τὸ φ. the cure too strong for, i. e. worse than, the disease, S. Fr. 589.4 , cf. Com.Adesp. 455 ; φ. πραΰ, of a bridle, Pi. O. 13.85 ; φ. τινι for a thing, Thgn. 1134 (pl.), Archil. 9 ; πρός τι Arist. Pol. 1321a16 ; ποττὸν ἔρωτα Theoc. 11.1 ; but most freq. φ. τινός remedy against . . χλαῖνα . . φ. ῥίγευς Hippon. 19 ; Ζεὺς πάντων φ. μοῦνος ἔχει Simon. 87 ; τὸ σιγᾶν φ. βλάβης ἔχω A. Ag. 548 ; φ. πόνων, λύπης, E. Ba. 283 , Fr. 1079 ; δόλοι . . χρείας ἀνάνδρου φ. ib. 288 ; φόβου Pl. Lg. 647e ; λήθης φάρμακα (of γράμματα) E. Fr. 578.1 ; v. εὐδιανός. c. gen. also, a means of producing something, φ. σωτηρίας Id. Ph. 893 ; μνήμης καὶ σοφίας φ. Pl. Phdr. 274e ; ὑπομνήσεως ib. 275a , cf. 230d ; ἀθανασίας Antiph. 86.6 ; ἡσυχίας Arist. Pol. 1273b23 ; φ. μανίας, of the oil applied to wrestlers, D.L. 1.104 . ἐπὶ θανάτῳ φ. ἑᾶς ἀρετᾶς εὑρέσθαι a remedy or consolation in his own virtue, Pi. P. 4.187 . dye, paint, colour, Emp. 23.3 , Hdt. 1.98 , A. Fr. 134 , Ar. Ec. 735 , Pl. R. 420c , Plt. 277c , PCair.Zen. 789.13 (iii B. C.), etc. chemical reagent, PLeid.X. 25 , PHolm. 13.46 , 22.10 , Ps.-Democr. ap. Zos.Alch. p.160 B. ; used by tanners, Sch. Ar. Eq. 44 , 368 .—Cf. φαρμάσσω. [μα; but μα in φαρμακός.]

lsj_entry_text: ἐμπειρ-ικός, ή, όν, experienced, ἁλιεῖς Arist. HA 532b20 . Adv. -κῶς, ἔχειν τινός Id. GA 742a17 , cf. Alex. 243 , etc. οἱ ἐμπειρικοί the Empiric school of physicians, Cels. 1 Praef., Gal. Sect.Intr. 1 , al., S.E. M. 8.327 , al.; ἡ -κή their doctrine,= Lat. empirice, Plin. HN 29.5 ; in full, ἐ. αἵρεσις Gal. l.c.; so ἐ. ἱστορία Phld. Rh. 1.93S. Adv. -κῶς empirically, ἰατρεύειν S.E. M. 8.204 , cf. Gal. 15.8 .
greek_sentence: ὅπου δὲ καὶ τῶν ἐμπειρικῶν ὀνομαζομένων ἔνιοι καίτοι ἀξιόλογοι διὰ τῶν τῆς τέχνης ἔργων ὀφθέντες, ὅμως ἀγνοεῖν φασιν ᾧτινι λογισμῷ τῶν συνθέτων φαρμάκων ἕκαστον εὕρηται, καὶ τί λέγω λογισμῷ;
english_sentence_A: And why need one speak of such physicians, when even some of those called Empiricists, although they have shown themselves noteworthy through the works of the art, nevertheless say that they do not know by what reasoning each of the compound drugs was discovered—and why do I say 'by what reasoning'?
english_sentence_B: Where even some of those called Empiricists, although they have been seen to be noteworthy through the works of the art, nevertheless say that they do not know by what reasoning each of the compound drugs has been discovered. And why do I say 'by reasoning'?

lsj_entry_text: συντίθημι, used by Hom. only in Med. , v. infr.:— Pass. (v. infr.), but σύγκειμαι is more freq. as Pass. :— place or put together, τὴν οὐρὴν καὶ τὸν σπλῆνα . . συνθεὶς ὁμοῦ Hdt. 2.47 , cf. 4.67 ; ὅπλα ἐν τῷ ναῷ X. HG 2.3.20 ; ἅπαντα εἰς ἕν E. IT 1016 ; ἐν ὀλίγῳ πάντα Id. Supp. 1126 (lyr.); ὁ πρῶτος συνθεὶς εἰς ταὐτὸν τὰ δύο ταῦτα βιβλίδια Gal. 15.109 ; ς. ἱμάτια, opp. ἀνασείειν, fold them together, X. Oec. 10.11 ; ς. σκέλη, opp. ἐκτείνειν, Id. Cyn. 5.10 ; opp. διαιρεῖσθαι, Pl. Sph. 252b ; ς. ἄρθρα στόματος close the lips, E. Cyc. 625 ; εἰς τὸ οὖλον (αυλον cod.) ς. τὴν κόμην, = calamistrat, Gloss. :— Pass. , τὸ συντίθεσθαι καθ' ὁντινοῦν τρόπον ῥῖγος οὐκ ἀγαθόν ἐστι any sort of combination of shivering (with other symptoms), Gal. 16.746 . technical uses, Math., add together, of numbers, Hdt. 3.95 ( Pass. ); τό τε ἀρχαῖον καὶ τὸ ἔργον principal and interest, D. 27.17 , cf. 29.30 : Geom., of lines and figures, Archim. Spir.Praef. , Papp. 70.4 . Math. also, of the transformation of a ratio componendo, Arist. EN 1131b8 ( Pass. ), Euc. 5.18 , 24 ( Pass. ). Logic, combine the terms of a proposition, Arist. Metaph. 1012a4 , 1024b19 ( Pass. ); also, use the fallacy of composition (cf. σύνθεσις 1.2e ), Id. Rh. 1401a24 . Rhet., accumulate, joined with ἐποικοδομεῖν (to form a climax), ib. 1365a16 . ς. λόγον make up an account, PHib. 1.48.15 (iii B.C.). put together constructively, so as to make a whole, πεντηκοντέρους καὶ τριήρεας (as a bridge) Hdt. 7.36 ; λίθους, of builders, Th. 4.4 , IG 42(1).103.59 (Epid., iv B.C.); πλίνθους, ξύλα, X. Mem. 3.1.7 , etc.; τὰ ὄστρακα IG 42(1).121.82 (Epid., iv B.C.); τὰ κομισθέντα Sor. 2.64 ; ἐκ τούτων τὰ μέγιστα . . συνθεὶς τοῦτον . . τὸν λόγον ποιήσομαι Hippias Eleus 6 D. ; συλλαβάς Pl. Cra. 424e . construct, frame, τὸ θνητὸν γένος Pl. Ti. 69d ; ὁ συνθείς the creator, ib. 33d :— Pass. , to be constructed, of the material universe, opp. διαλύεσθαι, Arist. Cael. 304b30 . ς. τι ἀπό τινος compose or make one thing of or from another, Hdt. 4.23 ; τὸ ἐκ τῶν νεῶν καὶ τοῦ πεζοῦ πλῆθος συντιθέμενον Id. 7.184 ; ἐξ ὧν [συλλαβῶν] τὰ ὀνόματα συντίθενται Pl. Cra. 425a , cf. 434a ; συνθεὶς πρᾶγμα πράξει δι' ὀνόματος καὶ ῥήματος Id. Sph. 262e ; εἴδωλον οὐρανοῦ ξυνθεῖσ' ἄπο (Reiske for ὕπο) E. Hel. 34 : metaph., συντιθεὶς γέλων πολύν S. Aj. 303 ; δυοῖν ἅμιλλαν ξ. strive for two things at once, E. El. 95 . construct or frame a story, συνθέντες λόγον Id. Ba. 297 , cf. Ar. Ra. 1052 (anap.), Pl. Phdr. 260b ; οἱ τὰς τέχνας τῶν λόγων συντιθέντες Arist. Rh. 1354a12 ; narrate in writing, τὰ Ἑλληνικά Th. 1.97 , cf. 21 ; compose, ς. μύθους, ποίησιν, μελῳδίαν, ὄρχησιν, Pl. R. 377d , Phdr. 278c , Lg. 812d , 816c ; αἴνιγμα Id. Ap. 27a ; ὁ τὴν ἐνθάδε συνθεὶς ἀνατομήν Gal. 15.147 :— Pass. , pf. συντέθειται ib. 797 ; περὶ ὀλίγας οἰκίας αἱ . . τραγῳδίαι συντίθενται Arist. Po. 1453a19 . Math., of the synthesis of a geometrical problem, opp. ἀναλύω, Id. SE 175a28 , Papp. 648.13 ; συντεθήσεται τὸ πρόβλημα οὕτως the synthesis of the problem will proceed thus, Archim. Sph.Cyl. 2.1 , cf. Apollon. Perg. Con. 1 Praef., 2.44 , al. frame, devise, contrive, ὁ συνθεὶς τάδε the framer of this plot, S. OT 401 , cf. Th. 8.68 ; ἐξ ἐπιβουλῆς ς. ταῦτα Antipho 5.25 ; ς. λόγους ψευδεῖς Id. 6.9 ; ψευδεῖς αἰτίας D. 25.28 ; τὴν κατηγορίαν And. 1.6 , etc.; rarely in good sense, εὖ πρᾶγμα συντεθὲν ὄψεσθε D. 18.144 . put together, take in, comprehend, παιδὸς μόρον A. Supp. 65 (lyr.); ὄμνυ . . θεῶν συντιθεὶς ἅπαν γένος E. Med. 747 ; πάσας συντιθεὶς ψέγει γυναῖκας Id. Fr. 657 , cf. Hec. 1184 : ἐν βραχεῖ ξυνθεὶς λέγω putting things shortly together, speaking briefly, S. El. 673 . commit to a person's care, deliver to him for his own use or that of others, PMich.Zen. 2.3 , 14 (iii B.C.), PCair.Zen. 4.23 , 6.11 , 64 , 299.9 , al. (iii B.C.); γνώριζε οὐχ ὑπάρχον παρ' ἡμῖν ἀργύριον τοσοῦτο ὥστε ἱκανὸν συνθεῖναι Πυρρίχῳ PMich.Zen. 28.18 , cf. 32.7 , PSI 4.392.7 , 5.524.3 , 6.613.8 , 7.862.1 , PLille 15.3 (all iii B.C.); τινὶ ὀστᾶ, ἐπιστολάς, πλῆθος χρυσίου, etc., Plb. 5.10.4 , 8.17.4 , 15.25.16 , cf. 27.7.1 , 28.22.3 , IG 12(5).590.12 (Ceos, ii B.C.), 11(4).1056.4 (Delos, ii B.C., cf. Jahresh. 24.171 ), OGI 345.11 (Delph., i B.C.). αὐτοὶ δ' ἔνοχοι εἴημεν τῷ ὅρκῳ ὁπηνίκ' ἂν εὖ συνθῶμεν perh. as soon as we have duly delivered (or executed) this declaration, BGU 1738.32 (i B.C.); συνθεὶς τούτους μου τοὺς λιβέλλους ἐπιδίδωμι τῇ σῇ λαμπρότητι PLond. 3.1000.7 (vi A.D.). collect, conclude, infer, Plb. 28.17.14 , Arr. Ind. 34 . Med. συντίθεμαι, used by Hom. only in aor. 2 and in signf. 1 : put together for oneself, i.e. observe, give heed to, σύνθετο θυμῷ βουλήν Il. 7.44 ; φρεσὶ σύνθετο θέσπιν ἀοιδήν Od. 1.328 ; ἐμεῖο δὲ σύνθεο μῦθον 17.153 ; συνθέμενος ῥῆμα Pi. greek_sentence: ὅπου δὲ καὶ τῶν ἐμπειρικῶν ὀνομαζομένων ἔνιοι καίτοι ἀξιόλογοι διὰ τῶν τῆς τέχνης ἔργων ὀφθέντες, ὅμως ἀγνοεῖν φασιν ᾧτινι λογισμῷ τῶν συνθέτων φαρμάκων ἕκαστον εὕρηται, καὶ τί λέγω λογισμῷ;
english_sentence_A: And why need one speak of such physicians, when even some of those called Empiricists, although they have shown themselves noteworthy through the works of the art, nevertheless say that they do not know by what reasoning each of the compound drugs was discovered—and why do I say 'by what reasoning'?
english_sentence_B: Where even some of those called Empiricists, although they have been seen to be noteworthy through the works of the art, nevertheless say that they do not know by what reasoning each of the compound drugs has been discovered. And why do I say 'by reasoning'?

lsj_entry_text: ἔμ-πλαστρος, ἡ, salve or plaster, Dsc. 1.32 ; said to be later form of ἔμπλαστος, Gal. 13.372 ; also ἔμπλαστρον, τό, Hierocl. Facet. 221 , PSI 3.297 (V A. D. ).
greek_sentence: ἄχρηστος οὖν αὐτοῖς ἐστιν ἡ τῆς φαιᾶς ταύτης ἐμπλάστρου γραφὴ, τὸ χρῶμα μόνον ἐν τῷ προγράμματι διδασκούσης χωρὶς τῆς κατὰ δύναμιν ἐπαγγελίας, ἣν ἄμεινον ἦν γεγράφθαι πρὸ τοῦ χρώματος.
english_sentence_A: Useless to them, therefore, is the prescription of this grey plaster, which in its heading teaches only the colour, without the professed virtue in respect of its power, which it would have been better to have written before the colour.
english_sentence_B: To them, then, the recipe of this grey plaster is useless, since in its heading it conveys only the colour, without the claim regarding its power, which would better have been written before the colour.

greek_sentence: καὶ μέντοι καὶ τὴν χρείαν αὐτῆς εἰς τὰς ἐμπλάστρους ἔγνωτε διττὴν ὑπάρχουσαν, εἰ μὲν ἄτηκτος μείνειεν, ὡς ὕλης μόνον, εἰ δὲ τακείη καὶ ὡς ξηραίνειν δυναμένης [893] καὶ μᾶλλον εἰ ἐπὶ πλέον ἑψηθείη.
english_sentence_A: And indeed you also know that its use in plasters is twofold: if it remains unmelted, as material only; but if it is melted, also as something able to dry, [893] and the more so if it is boiled for longer.
english_sentence_B: And indeed you also learned that its use in plasters is twofold: if it remains unmelted, it serves only as material; but if it is melted, it serves also as something able to dry, [893] and the more so if it is boiled longer.

lsj_entry_text: κίκινος, η, ον, made from the κίκι-tree, ἔλαιον Dsc. 1.32 , Gal. 11.870 .
greek_sentence: γράψαντος τοῦ Ἀνδρομάχου μίγνυσθαι χρῆναι τοῦ κίκεως, ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἐλαίου κικίνου.
english_sentence_A: Now, however, there is a question as to how far it will be boiled, since Andromachus has written that six cotylae of kiki, which is castor oil, must be mixed in.
english_sentence_B: For he did not make clear of how many ounces of the Roman litra he means the kotyle to be.

lsj_entry_text: οὐγγία or οὐγκία, ἡ, Lat. uncia, as adopted by the Sicil. Greeks, Arist. Fr. 510 , Gal. 13.789 , Alex.Aphr. in Top. 210.7 :—written ὀγκία in Epich. 203 , Sophr. 151 : hence Adj. οὐγκιαῖος, α, ον, of one uncia, prob. in SIG 1042.23 (Sunium, ii/iii A. greek_sentence: πόσων γὰρ οὐγγιῶν τὴν ἐκ τῆς Ῥωμαϊκῆς λίτρας εἶναι βούλεται κοτύλην, οὐκ ἐδήλωσε· καίτοι βέλτιον ἦν ἐν Ῥώμῃ βεβιωκότα λιτρῶν μὲν καὶ ξεστῶν καὶ οὐγγιῶν μεμνῆσθαι, παραλιπεῖν δὲ τὸ τῆς κοτύλης ὄνομα ταῖς ἔξω τῆς Ἰταλίας πόλεσιν Ἑλληνικαῖς ὑπάρχον ἐν χρήσει.
english_sentence_A: For he did not make clear of how many ounces, reckoned from the Roman litra, he wants the cotyle to be; and yet it would have been better for one who had lived in Rome to speak of litrai and xestai and ounces, and to leave aside the name of the cotyle, which is in use in the Greek cities outside Italy.
english_sentence_B: And yet it would have been better for one who had lived in Rome to mention litrai, xestai and ounces, and to leave aside the name of the kotyle, which is in use in the Greek cities outside Italy.

greek_sentence: τὸ τοίνυν προκείμενον φάρμακον εὕρηται μὲν διαφορητικὸν ἰσχυρῶς, ὡς καὶ πῦον ἤδη τό γε μὴ πάνυ πολὺ, χωρὶς τοῦ διατρῆσαι τὸ δέρμα, διαφορεῖν δύνασθαι, μαλακτικὸν δὲ τῶν σκιῤῥουμένων τε καὶ ὁπωσοῦν σκληρυνομένων, κολλητικὸν δὲ μεγάλων τραυμάτων, ὥσπερ γε καὶ τῶν ἤδη κακοηθευομένων ἑλκῶν ἐπουλωτικὸν [901] ἁπάντων τε τῶν ἄλλων παθημάτων, ὅσα διαφορητικῆς τε ἅμα καὶ ἀποκρουστικῆς μετρεῖται δυνάμεως, ἐν οἷς ἐστι καὶ τὰ κατὰ τοῦ μετώπου ῥευματιζομένων ὀφθαλμῶν ἐπιτιθέμενα, καλούμενα δὲ ὑπὸ τῶν ἰατρῶν ἀνακολλήματα.
english_sentence_A: The drug under discussion, then, has been found to be strongly discutient, so that it is able to disperse even pus already present—at least when it is not very abundant—without perforating the skin; emollient for parts that are becoming scirrhous or hardened in any way whatever; agglutinative of large wounds, just as it is also cicatrizing of ulcers that are already becoming malignant, [901] and of all the other affections that are apportioned (μετρεῖται) a power at once discutient and repellent, among which are also the things applied to the forehead for eyes affected by flux, which are called by physicians anakollēmata.
english_sentence_B: The drug before us, then, has been found to be powerfully discutient, so that it is able to disperse even pus already formed, at least when it is not very much, without perforating the skin; and to be emollient of parts that are becoming scirrhous and of those hardened in any way whatever; and agglutinative of large wounds, just as it is also cicatrizing of ulcers that have already turned malignant, [901] and of all the other affections that are measured by (? μετρεῖται) a faculty at once discutient and repellent. Among these are also the applications placed on the forehead for eyes suffering from flux, which physicians call anakollēmata.

greek_sentence: καὶ ἄλλας δὲ πολλὰς ἔγραψεν ἅμα ταύταις ὁ Ἀνδρόμαχος ἐμπλάστρους, οὐδὲν ἄλλο προσθεὶς αὐταῖς ἢ τὸ τοῦ χρώματος ὄνομα, συγκειμένας ἐκ τῶν ἐναντίων ταῖς δυνάμεσι φαρμάκων, ἀλλὰ τινὲς μὲν αὐτῶν ἐπικρατοῦν ἔχουσι τὸ χαλαστικόν τε καὶ ἀνώδυνον, τινὲς δὲ διαφορητικόν τε καὶ ῥυπτικὸν, τινὲς δὲ τὴν στύψιν· ὥστε καὶ ἡμᾶς χρὴ πάσαις [908] αὐταῖς θαῤῥοῦντας ἐπιτηδείως ἑκάστῃ χρῆσθαι, πρὸς μὲν τὰ δυσεπούλωτα καὶ κακοήθη τῶν ἑλκῶν ταῖς στυπτικὸν ἐχούσαις πλέον· ἔνθα δὲ παρηγορῆσαί τε καὶ χαλάσαι πρόκειται· ταῖς τὸ χαλαστικόν· ἔνθα δὲ ἑλκύσαι τε καὶ διαφορῆσαι, ταῖς τὰ θερμαίνοντα καὶ πρὸς ἑαυτὰς τὰς ἐν βάθει διαθέσεων ἐπισπώμενα μοχθηρὰς ὑγρότητας.

lsj_entry_text: σύν-θεσις, εως, ἡ, putting together, composition, combination, Pl. Phd. 93a , R. 611b ; τῶν λίθων Arist. EN 1174a23 , cf. IG 42(1).103.56 (Epid., iv B.C.), 7.3073.92 (Lebad., ii B.C.); τῶν σπονδύλων Sor. 1.102 ; storage, τῶν μήλων (quinces in a ῥίσκος) Phylarch. 10 J. ; but ἐλαιῶν ς. a preserve of olives, Gp. 9.28.2 . in concrete sense, junction, ὀστῶν Arist. PA 658b19 ; συνθέσεις (λέγω τὰς γωνίας) Id. Pr. 910b14 . in various technical senses: in Grammar, composition, γραμμάτων τε συνθέσεις, i.e. syllables and words, A. Pr. 460 , cf. Arist. Metaph. 1092a26 ; ς. ἔκ τε ῥημάτων γιγνομένη καὶ ὀνομάτων, i.e. sentences, Pl. Sph. 263d , cf. Cra. 431c , Arist. Po. 1458a28 , Gal. 15.487 ; περὶ συνθέσεως ὀνομάτων, title of work by D.H. ; also, the juxtaposition of letters in a word, Arist. Rh.Al. 1434b34 ; of an author's composition, Isoc. 10.11 ; so ἡ τῶν μέτρων ς. metrical composition, Arist. Po. 1449b35 ; ἡ τῶν ἐπῶν ς. D.S. 5.74 ; ἡ τοῦ παίωνος ξ. the way the paeon is made up, Plu. 2.1143d ; the constitution of things, Hp. Virg. 1 . Math., synthesis of a problem (opp. ἀνάλυσις), Archim. Sph.Cyl. 2.7 , explained in Papp. 634 ; ἡ κατὰ ς. ἀγωγή synthetic procedure, Id. 412.2 . Math., ς. λόγου transformation of a ratio known as componendo, Euc. 5 Def. 14 ; κατὰ -σιν, = componendo, Archim. Aequil. 2.9 . Math., addition, Ph. 1.11 , Plu. 2.1018c , Dioph. 1 Intr.; καθ' ἁντινοῦν -σιν however many times added, i.e. whatever number of times taken (multiplied), Archim. Spir. 1 :—also as Pythag. name for 2 , Anatol. ap. Theol.Ar. 8 . in Logic, union of noun and verb or of two objects of thought in a statement, Arist. Int. 16a12 , de An. 430a27 ; also ὁ παρὰ τὴν ς. [λόγος] the fallacy of composition, opp. διαίρεσις, Id. SE 177a33 . in Physics, composition of substances, parts of organisms, from their elementary constituents, Id. PA 646a12 , Top. 151a23 ; opp μίξις (combination), Id. GC 328a6 . in Medicine, compounding of essences and drugs, τῶν μύρων Thphr. Od. 14 , al., cf. D.S. 4.45 , Aglaïas 8 . combination of parts so as to form a whole, γενέσεις καὶ ς. Pl. R. 533b ; ἡ τῶν στρωμάτων ς. Id. Plt. 280b , cf. Arist. PA 645a35 , Metaph. 1014b37 ; in plants, Thphr. HP 5.5.2 . in concrete sense, a social or political combination, Arist. Pol. 1276b7 ; a military formation, Ael. Tact. 18.5 . agreement, treaty, Pi. P. 4.168 , Fr. 205 ; πὸς τὰς συνθέσις in accordance with the agreements, IG 5(2).343.41 , 60 (Orchom. Arc. , iv B.C.); ἐκ συνθέσεως by arrangement, D.S. 13.112 , etc.; συνθέσεις περὶ γάμων Plu. Sull. 35 . ς. λόγων making up accounts, Stud.Pal. 4.70.391 (i A.D.); so ς. alone, εἰς σύνθεσιν τῷ βασιλεῖ PTeb. 714.6 (ii B.C.). set, service (most freq. in Lat. synthesis): collection of clothes, wardrobe, Dig. 34.2.38.1 ; also, dress, gown, costume, suit, ς. τελείας λευκὰς δεκατρεῖς, γυναικείας ς. Aj. 1331 ; φίλοι οἱ ἐγγυτάτω, οἱ ἔγγιστα, Lys. 1.41 codd., Plb. 9.24.2 ; after Hom. freq. with a gen., ὁ Διὸς φίλος A. Pr. 306 ; τοὺς ἐμαυτοῦ φ., τοὺς τούτων φ., Aeschin. 1.47 ; φ. ἐμός S. Ph. 421 ; τῶν ἐμε ͂ν φ. ib. 509 ; τοὺς σφετέρους φ. X. HG 4.8.25 : prov., ἔστιν ὁ φ. ἄλλος αὐτός a friend is another self, Arist. EN 1166a31 ; κοινὰ τὰ τῶν φ. Pl. Phdr. 279c , cf. Arist. EN 1159b31 ; οὐθεὶς φ. ᾧ πολλοὶ φ. Id. EE 1245b20 ; also of friends or allies, opp. πολέμιοι, X. HG 6.5.48 ; φ. καὶ σύμμαχος D. 9.12 , etc.; of a lover, X. Mem. 3.11.4 (in bad sense, Lac. 2.13 ); φίλε my friend, as a form of courteous address, Ev.Luc. 14.10 , etc.; in relation to things, οἱ μουσικῆς φ. E. Fr. 580.3 ; ἀληθείας Pl. R. 487a ; τῶν εἰδῶν Id. Sph. 248a ; Χίους φ. ποιῆσαι Lys. 14.36 , etc.; ποιεῖσθαι Luc. Pisc. 38 ; κτᾶσθαι Isoc. 2.27 , cf. Th. 2.40 ; φίλους τιθέντες τούς γε πολεμιωτάτους E. Hec. 848 ; φίλῳ χρῆσθαί τινι Antipho 5.63 ; ἡμᾶς ἔχειν φίλους And. 1.40 ; for Hdt. 3.49 , v. φίλιος. φίλη, ἡ, dear one, friend, κλῦτε, φίλαι Od. 4.722 ; λόγοις ἐγὼ φιλοῦσαν οὐ στέργω φίλην S. Ant. 543 ; of a wife, φίλην τινὰ ἄγεσθαι take as one's wife, Il. 9.146 , 288 ; ἡ Ξέρξου φ., of his mother, A. Pers. 832 ; of a mistress, X. Mem. 2.1.23 , 3.11.16 ; φίλην ποιήσασθαί τινα Antipho 1.14 . φίλον, τό, an object of love, τὸ φ. σέβεσθαι to reverence what the city loves, S. OC 187 (lyr.): addressed to persons, darling, φ. ἐμόν Ar. Ec. 952 (lyr.); so φίλτατον ib. 970 ; τὰ φίλτατα one's nearest and dearest, dear ones, such as wife and children, A. Pers. 851 , Eu. 216 , S. OT 366 , OC 1110 , E. Med. 16 : v. φίλτατος; τἀμὰ φίλα, τὰ σὰ φ. , Id. Ion 523 (troch.), 613 . οἱ πρῶτοι φίλοι, a title at the Ptolemaic court, OGI 99.3 , PTeb. 11.4 (ii B. C.), etc.; or simply οἱ φ. τοῦ βασιλέως OGI 100.1 ; or οἱ φ. alone, ib. 115.4 ; τῶν φ. και διοικητοῦ one of the king's friends and dioecetes, PTeb. 79.56 (ii B. C.). of things, pleasant, welcome, δόσις ὀλίγη τε φ. τε Od. 6.208 , cf. Il. 1.167 : c. dat. pers., αἰεὶ γάρ τοι ἔρις τε φίλη 5.891 , cf. Od. 8.248 , 13.295 ; οὐ φίλα τοι ἐρέω Hdt. 7.104 ; δαίμοσιν πράσσειν φίλα their pleasure, A. Pr. 660 , cf. infr. 11 . freq. as predic., φίλον ἐστί or γίγνεταί μοι pleases me, it is after my own heart, εἴ πού τοι φίλον ἐστί Od. 7.320 ; μὴ φ. Διὶ πατρὶ γένοιτο ib. 316 , cf. Il. 7.387 ; εἰ τόδε πᾶσι φ. καὶ ἡδὺ γένοιτο 4.17 ; καί τοι φ. ἔπλετο θυμῷ Od. 13.145 , etc.; τοῦτο μὲν ἴτω ὅπῃ τῷ θεῷ φίλον Pl. Ap. 19a : less freq. c. inf., οὐ μὲν Τυδέϊ γ' ὧδε φίλον πτωσκαζέμεν Il. 4.372 ; πεφιδέσθαι ἐνὶ φρεσὶ φίλτερον ἦεν Τρώων 21.101 , cf. 24.334 , Od. 14.378 ; so ταῦτα δαίμονί κοω φίλον ἦν οὕτω γενέσθαι Hdt. 1.87 , cf. 108 , 4.97 : rarely c. part., εἰ τόδ' αὐτῷ φιλον κεκλημένῳ if it please him to be so called, A. Ag. 161 (lyr.): agreeing with pl., αἰεί τοι τὰ κάκ' ἐστὶ φίλα φρεσὶ μαντεύεσθαι Il. 1.107 , cf. Od. 17.15 ; ἔνθα φίλ' ὀπταλέα κρέα ἔδμεναι Il. 4.345 ; σοὶ δ' ἔργα φίλ' ἔστω μέτρια κοσμεῖν Hes. Op. 306 . in Hom. and early Poets, one's own; freq. of limbs, life, etc., φίλον δ' ἐξαίνυτο θυμόν he took away dear life, Il. 5.155 , cf. 22.58 ; κατεπλήγη φίλον ἦτορ 3.31 ; εἰς ὅ κε . . μοι φίλα γούνατ' ὀρώρῃ 9.610 ; φίλον κατὰ λαιμόν 19.209 ; esp. of one's nearest kin, πατὴρ φ. 22.408 , Sapph. Supp. 20 a. 11 ; ἄλοχος φ. Il. 5.480 : cf. φίλτατος: as a standing epith. when no affection is implied, μητρὶ φίλῃ Ἀλθαίῃ χωόμενος κῆρ angry with his own mother, Il. 9.555 : simply to denote possession, φίλα εἵματα 2.261 ; φ. πόνος their wonted labour, Theoc. 21.20 . applied to the numbers 284 and 220 , Iamb. in Nic. p.35P. less freq. (chiefly poet.) in act. sense, loving, friendly, Od. 1.313 , cf. Il. 24.775 : c. gen., φίλαν ξένων ἄρουραν friendly to strangers, Pi. N. 5.8 , cf. P. 3.5 : of things, kindly, pleasing, φίλα φρεσὶ μήδεα εἰδώς Il. 17.325 ; φίλα φρονέειν τινί feel kindly, Il. 4.219 ; φ. ἐργάζεσθαί τινι Od. 24.210 ; φ. εἰδέναι τινί 3.277 ; φ. ποιέεσθαί τινι deal with one in friendly fashion, do one a pleasure, Hdt. 2.152 , 5.37 . fond of a thing, attached to, ἄλλων νόμων Arist. Fr. 543 ; δειλίας φίλον Pl. R. 604d . Adv. φίλως, once in Hom. , φίλως χ' ὁρόῳτε ye would fain see it, Il. 4.347 , cf. Hes. Sc. 45 , A. Ag. 247 (lyr.), [1591] , etc.; φ. ἐμοί in a manner dear or pleasing to me, ib. 1581 . in a friendly, kindly spirit, τήνδε τὴν πόλιν φ. εἰπών S. OC 758 ; φ. δέχεσθαί τινα X. HG 4.8.5 , cf. Pl. Epin. 988c . φίλος has several forms of comparison: Comp. φιλίων [λι], ον, gen. ονος, Od. 19.351 , 24.268 : Sup. φίλιστος, η, ον, interpol. in S. Aj. 842 . Comp. φίλτερος, Sup. φίλτατος, v. sub voce. Ph. 886 ; φ. μᾶλλον Thphr. CP 6.1.4 ; Sup. , μάλιστα φ. X. Cyr. 8.1.17 .

greek_sentence: Καίειν δ’ ἔφασκεν αὐτὰ τοῦτον τὸν τρόπον, Εἰς λοπάδα καινὴν ἢ χύτραν πλατύστομον Ἐνθέντα ἔριον οἰσυπηρὸν δαψιλὲς, Τὸ σῶμα προχρίσαντ’ ἢ γύψῳ ἢ κόνει, Ἢ γῇ κεραμικῇ, μεθ’ ὕδατος μεμιγμένη Ἐν πυρὶ λάβρῳ καίοντα, ὅταν ᾖ ῥάδιον, [921] Κόψαντα σῆσαι.
english_sentence_A: And he said to burn them in this manner: putting into a new dish or a wide-mouthed pot an abundance of greasy wool, having first smeared the body (of the vessel) with gypsum or with ash, or with potter's earth mixed with water, burning it in a fierce fire, and when it is easy (to do so), [921] pounding it and sifting it—at least as far as it seems to be well; and to burn them likewise also in baking-ovens, and in furnaces that have been very strongly fired, and grinding them fine in this way, take the weight that is required.
english_sentence_B: He said that they are to be burnt in this manner: placing a plentiful quantity of greasy wool in a new dish or a wide-mouthed pot, having first smeared its body with gypsum or with dust, or with potter's earth mixed with water, and burning it on a fierce fire, when it is easy to do so, [921] pound it and sift it.

lsj_entry_text: ἔμ-πλαστρος, ἡ, salve or plaster, Dsc. 1.32 ; said to be later form of ἔμπλαστος, Gal. 13.372 ; also ἔμπλαστρον, τό, Hierocl. Facet. 221 , PSI 3.297 (V A. D. ).
greek_sentence: ἵνα δὲ ἔμπλαστρος γένηται, καθάπερ ἐν τοῖς ἔμπροσθεν ἐῤῥέθη, τῷ μὲν γὰρ λιθαργύρου μίγνυται, τῷ δὲ ῥητίνης, τῷ δὲ κηροῦ, τῷ δὲ ἐλαίου, τῷ δὲ πίττης, οὔτε διαφορητικὴν δύναμιν ἀξιόλογον οὔθ’ ἑλκτικὴν ἐχόντων τῶν τοιούτων, ὥσπερ ἢ πρόπολις ἢ τίτανος ἢ μυελὸς ἢ χαλβάνη ἢ τὸ τῆς Ἀσίας πέτρας ἄνθος ἢ ἀφρὸς νίτρου ἢ ἀφρόνιτρον ἢ ὄξος ἢ κονία στακτὴ, πέπερί τε καὶ νᾶπυ καὶ στρουθίον, οἵ τ’ ἐδώδιμοι τῶν ἁλῶν, οἵ τε ἀμμωνιακοὶ καὶ πρὸς τούτοις ἄλλα πολλὰ, περὶ ὧν τῆς δυνάμεως ἐν τῇ τῶν ἁπλῶν φαρμάκων πραγματείᾳ λέλεκται.
english_sentence_A: But in order that a plaster may result, as was said in what precedes, with one of them litharge is mixed, with another resin, with another wax, with another oil, with another pitch—such things having neither a noteworthy discutient power nor an attractive one, as do propolis or lime or marrow or galbanum or the flower of the Asian stone or foam of nitron or aphronitron or vinegar or dripped lye, pepper and mustard and soapwort, and both the edible kinds of salts and the ammoniac ones, and in addition to these many others, concerning whose power it has been stated in the treatise on simple drugs.
english_sentence_B: But in order that a plaster may result, as was said in the earlier sections, there is mixed in, for one, some litharge, for another resin, for another wax, for another oil, for another pitch, such substances having no noteworthy power either dispersive or drawing, as propolis has, or 'lime' (titanos), or marrow, or galbanum, or the 'flower' of the Asian (Assian?) stone, or foam of nitre, or aphronitre, or vinegar, or strained lye, and pepper and mustard and strouthion, and the edible salts and the ammoniac ones, and besides these many others, concerning whose power I have spoken in the treatise on simple drugs.

english_sentence_A: Exceedingly good, dispersing scrofulous swellings, reducing every oedema and healing the watery conditions of the liver or of the spleen, bringing on abundant excretions of urine, and it resolves chronic sciatic affections.

greek_sentence: Ἔλεγε δ’ ὁ Κράτιστος καὶ πατὴρ τοῦ φαρμάκου, Καὶ πρὸς νόσων τε τῶν μακρῶν ἀπαλλαγὰς, Εὔχρηστον εἶναι καὶ καλὸν τὸ φάρμακον, Ἐφ’ ὧν τε χρόνιος φλεγμονὴ σπλάγχνων τινὸς Ὑποχόνδριον πεποίηκε σκληρὸν ἢ μέγα Σφόδρ’ ὠφελεῖν, ἱδρῶτας γὰρ ἐπιφέρει Καὶ τὰς σκληρίας λύει τῶν ὑποχονδρίων, Ἀπαλλαγάς τε τῶν νόσων ποιεῖ ταχὺ, Καὶ τὰς ἐποχὰς δὲ τῶν φυσικῶν καταμηνίων Ἄγει βραχείαις ἡμέραις ἐπικείμενον.
english_sentence_A: And the most excellent man and father of the drug used to say that the drug is serviceable and good also for deliverance from long diseases, and that in those cases where a chronic inflammation of some viscus has made the hypochondrium hard or large it helps greatly; for it brings on sweats and dissolves the hardnesses of the hypochondria, and quickly effects deliverance from the diseases, and it also brings down retentions of the natural menses when applied for a few days.
english_sentence_B: The most excellent man, the father of the drug, said that the drug is also serviceable and good for the riddance of long diseases, and that in those in whom a chronic inflammation of one of the viscera has made the hypochondrium hard or large it helps greatly; for it brings on sweats and dissolves the hardnesses of the hypochondria, and quickly effects the riddance of the diseases; and the suppressions of the natural menses it brings on when it has lain applied for a few days.

english_sentence_B: The most excellent man, the father of the drug, said that the drug is also serviceable and good for the riddance of long diseases, and that in those in whom a chronic inflammation of one of the viscera has made the hypochondrium hard or large it helps greatly; for it brings on sweats and dissolves the hardnesses of the hypochondria, and quickly effects the riddance of the diseases; and the suppressions of the natural menses it brings on when it has lain applied for a few days.

english_sentence_A: It is quite evident that in the mixture either the softening ingredients are more than the discutient ones, or the reverse, and the degree of more and less among them is no small matter.

greek_sentence: εὔδηλον δὲ ὅτι πολλάκις ἴσα ταῖς δυνάμεσι μίγνυνται, καὶ χρὴ καθάπερ ἐπὶ τῶν ἄλλων φαρμάκων, οὕτως κᾀπὶ τούτων παρασκευάσασθαι τῷ βουλομένῳ καλῶς ἰατρεύειν πλείω φάρμακα τῶν ὁμογενῶν, ἢ πάντως γε δύο μίγνυσθαι, τό τε ἰσχυρότατον ἐν τῷ γένει καὶ τὸ μετριώτατον, ἵνα ἐκ τῆς διαφόρου μίξεως αὐτῶν ἐπικαίρου γενομένης ἐργάζηται τὰ μεταξὺ τῶν ἄκρων πάμπολλα φάρμακα.
english_sentence_A: It is quite evident too that often they are mixed in equal proportions as regards their powers; and it is necessary, just as in the case of the other drugs, so also in the case of these, for one who wishes to practise medicine well to prepare for himself several drugs of the same kind, or at any rate to have two to mix, the strongest in the kind and the most moderate, in order that from their varied mixture, made in a manner suited to the occasion, he may produce the very many drugs that lie between the extremes.
english_sentence_B: It is quite clear too that they are often mixed in equal potencies. Just as with the other drugs, so with these, the one who wishes to treat well must have prepared several drugs of the same kind, or at any rate two to be mixed, the strongest in the kind and the most moderate, so that from their differing mixture, made at the opportune moment, he may produce a great many drugs between the extremes.

greek_sentence: κατὰ γὰρ τὴν κρᾶσιν τοῦ ζώου καὶ τὸ στέαρ ἐστι, τῶν μὲν θερμοτέρων θερμαντικώτερον, τῶν δὲ ξηροτέρων ξηραντικώτερον, καὶ γινώσκουσί γε οἱ πολλοὶ τῶν ἰατρῶν ἰσχυρότατον μὲν εἶναι κατ’ ἄμφω, λέγω δὴ τὸ θερμαίνειν τε καὶ διαφορεῖν, τὸ τοῦ λέοντος στέαρ.
english_sentence_A: For the fat too is in accordance with the temperament of the animal: that of the hotter animals is more heating, that of the drier more drying; and most physicians know that the strongest in both respects, I mean in heating and in dispersing, is the fat of the lion.
english_sentence_B: For the fat too is according to the temperament (krasis) of the animal: that of the hotter animals is more heating, that of the drier more drying. And indeed most physicians know that the strongest in both respects, I mean heating and dispersing, is the fat of the lion.

lsj_entry_text: μαλακ-τικός, ή, όν, emollient, χρίσματα Hp. Vict. 2.66 ; δύναμις Plu. 2.659c ; μ. οἶκος, of the outer chamber in a bath, Alex. Trall. Febr. 5 .
greek_sentence: ἐγγὺς δὲ αὐτῷ τὸ τῶν παρδάλεων, ὡς ὀλίγον ἔχειν τὸ μαλακτικόν.
english_sentence_A: Close to it is that of leopards, so that it has little of the emollient.
english_sentence_B: Close to it is that of leopards, so that it has little emollient quality.

greek_sentence: ἀνάλογον δὲ ἀφέστηκε τοῦδε καὶ τὸ τῶν ἀλεκτορίδων.
english_sentence_A: And that of hens stands at a proportionate distance from this one.
english_sentence_B: And that of hens stands at a proportionate remove from this one.

english_sentence_A: To all of these, moreover, belongs also being finer-parted than those in four-footed animals.
english_sentence_B: Now all of these also have the property of being finer-particled than those in four-footed animals.

greek_sentence: διαφορὰ δὲ πάλιν ἐν ἐκείνοις ἐστὶ παμπόλλη, τοῦ μὲν ὑείου μαλακωτάτου τε καὶ ὑγροτάτου καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἀσθενεστάτου τῶν ἄλλων ὄντος, ὡς ἁρμόττειν ἐπὶ σωμάτων μὲν ἁπαλῶν, οἷα τὰ τῶν γυναικῶν ἐστι καὶ παίδων καὶ εὐνούχων καὶ τῶν ἁβροδιαίτων ἀνδρῶν ἐν σκιατροφίᾳ καὶ ἀγυμνασίᾳ καὶ λουτροῖς πλείοσι ποτίμων ὑδάτων ἐκτεθηλυσμένα.
english_sentence_A: But again among those there is a very great difference, pig's fat being the softest and moistest and for this reason the weakest of the others, so that it suits tender bodies, such as those of women and children and eunuchs and of delicately-living men, bodies made effeminate by rearing in the shade, by lack of exercise, and by rather frequent baths of fresh waters.
english_sentence_B: Among those, in turn, there is a very great difference: pig's fat is the softest and moistest and for this reason the weakest of the others, so that it suits soft bodies, such as are those of women and children and eunuchs and of men of delicate living, made effeminate by rearing in the shade, lack of exercise, and frequent baths of drinkable water.

greek_sentence: ὥσπερ δὲ ἐν τοῖς ἄλλοις ἅπασιν ὅσα μεταπίπτειν εἰς ἄλληλα πέφυκεν, ἔνεστι μεθόριον ἀμφοτέρων ἠρέμα μέτοχον, οὕτως καὶ τῶν φλεγμονωδῶν ὄγκων πρὸς τοὺς ἄνευ φλεγμονῆς σκίῤῥους, οἷοί περ οἱ τῶν ἐσκληρυσμένων εἰσὶν, ὑπάρχει τις ἐν τῷ μεταξὺ διάθεσις, ἀνώδυνος μὲν, εἰ μὴ τοὺς δακτύλους ἐπερείδοις, ὀδυνωμένη δὲ τοῦτο πραττόντων, ἣν σαφοῦς τε καὶ συντόμου διδασκαλίας ἕνεκα ἤτοι φλεγμονὴν σκιῤῥώδη λεκτέον ἢ σκίῤῥον φλεγμονώδη, μὴ προσέχοντας ἐνταῦθα τῷ [951] κατὰ τὸν ὄγκον μεγέθει.
english_sentence_A: Just as in all other things that are naturally such as to change into one another there is a borderland partaking slightly of both, so too between the inflammatory swellings and the scirrhi without inflammation, such as those of indurated parts are, there exists a certain intermediate condition, painless, unless you press the fingers upon it, but painful when one does this; which, for the sake of clear and concise teaching, must be called either scirrhous inflammation or inflammatory scirrhus, not attending here to the [951] magnitude of the swelling.
english_sentence_B: Just as in all other things whose nature is to pass over into one another there is a borderland between the two that shares moderately in both, so also between phlegmonous swellings and the scirrhi without phlegmone, such as are those of parts that have become hardened, there exists a certain intermediate condition. It is painless unless you press the fingers on it, but painful when people do so.

english_sentence_A: [The differences and powers of the emollient drugs by kind.] Now the emollients that are thus weak also treat small inflammations; those weaker than these (ἀτονώτερα), the slight hardnesses without inflammation.

english_sentence_A: Those still stronger than these [treat] the greater [hardnesses], just as those that are curative of a hardness that has come near to scirrhus are the most effective, of which sort is the kind of the marrows, differing from one another in more and less, as I shall distinguish next, [954] and that of both bdelliums, the Arabian and the Scythian, and that of the storaxes.

Pi. P. 3.52 ; παιώνια A. Ag. 848 ; χρήσιμον Pl. R. 382c ; θανάσιμα Ph. Bel. 103.31 ; ὀλέθριον Luc. greek_sentence: σὺ δ’ ὅταν ἤτοι τι τῶν γεγραμμένων ἐν ταῖς φαρμακίτισι βίβλοις ἐξετάσῃς τε καὶ κρίνῃς ἢ συντιθῇς αὐτὸς, ἀκηκοὼς ἄρτι τὰς κατὰ τὸ μᾶλλόν τε καὶ ἧττον ἐν τοῖς φαρμάκοις διαφορὰς, ἀκηκοὼς δὲ καὶ τὰς τῶν σωμάτων τε καὶ παθῶν, τὰ μὲν ἰσχυρὰ τοῖς ἰσχυροῖς, τὰ δὲ ἀσθενῆ τοῖς ἀσθενέσι προσάξεις.
english_sentence_A: And you, whenever you either examine and judge one of the drugs recorded in the pharmacological books or compound one yourself, having just now heard the differences among drugs according to the more and the less, and having heard also those of bodies and of affections, will apply the strong ones to the strong and the weak ones to the weak.
english_sentence_B: And you, whenever you either examine and judge one of the remedies written in the pharmacological books, or compound one yourself, having just heard of the differences of more and less among drugs, and having heard also of the differences of bodies and of affections, will apply the strong ones to the strong and the weak ones to the weak.

english_sentence_B: And you, whenever you either examine and judge one of the remedies written in the pharmacological books, or compound one yourself, having just heard of the differences of more and less among drugs, and having heard also of the differences of bodies and of affections, will apply the strong ones to the strong and the weak ones to the weak.

english_sentence_A: [958] And in the interval, when one applies another after the one previously applied, it is fitting to pour simple, oily oil over the affected part.
english_sentence_B: [958] In the interval of applying another [drug] after the one applied before, it is fitting to pour simple oil over the affected part, and something oily suits it.

english_sentence_A: Of the drugs called adhesive (echekolla), none should be removed before it comes away of its own accord; rather, even if one bathes, it should be allowed to remain in place.
english_sentence_B: Of the drugs called echekolla ('adhesive'), none should be removed before it comes away of its own accord; rather, even if the patient bathes, one should let it stay in place.

lsj_entry_text: μαλακ-τικός, ή, όν, emollient, χρίσματα Hp. Vict. 2.66 ; δύναμις Plu. 2.659c ; μ. οἶκος, of the outer chamber in a bath, Alex. Trall. Febr. 5 .
greek_sentence: [Αἱ τῶν μαλακτικῶν φαρμάκων κατ’ εἴδη διαφοραὶ καὶ δυνάμεις.] Ἐπεὶ δὲ οὐ πάντες εἰσὶ τοιοῦτοι καὶ πρόκειται κατὰ τήνδε τὴν πραγματείαν, οὐχ ὥσπερ ἐν τῇ τῆς θεραπευτικῆς μεθόδου, μόνην εἰπεῖν τὴν μέθοδον, ἀλλ’ ἅμα παραδείγματι τῶν κατὰ μέρος ἑνί τε καὶ δευτέρῳ, προστεθῆναι δεῖ καὶ τὰ πείρᾳ προκείμενα φάρμακα, ἃ πρόσκειται τοῖς πρὸ ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ φαρμακευτικῷ μέρει τῆς τέχνης ἐνδόξοις, ἐπὶ τὰς κατ’ εἴδη διαφορὰς ἐπὶ τῶν μαλακτικῶν φαρμάκων ἀφίξομαι τὴν ἀρχὴν ἀπὸ τῶν μαλακωτάτων ποιησάμενος [959] αὐτοῖς, ἃ καὶ τὰς μικρὰς ἰᾶται φλεγμονάς.
english_sentence_A: [The differences and powers of emollient drugs according to kinds.] But since not all are such men, and since it is proposed in this treatise not, as in that of the Therapeutic Method, to state the method alone, but together with one or two examples of the particular cases, there must also be added the drugs that are established by experience, which are set down by those before us who are esteemed in the pharmaceutical part of the art;
english_sentence_B: [The differences by species, and the potencies, of emollient drugs.] But since not all are of this kind, and since what is proposed in this treatise is not, as in the Therapeutic Method, to state the method alone, but to state it together with an example of the particulars, one or a second, and the drugs established by experience must also be added, those set down by the men before us who were renowned in the pharmaceutical part of the art, I shall come to the differences by species among the emollient drugs, making my beginning from the mildest of them, which also cure small inflammations.

greek_sentence: [Αἱ τῶν μαλακτικῶν φαρμάκων κατ’ εἴδη διαφοραὶ καὶ δυνάμεις.] Ἐπεὶ δὲ οὐ πάντες εἰσὶ τοιοῦτοι καὶ πρόκειται κατὰ τήνδε τὴν πραγματείαν, οὐχ ὥσπερ ἐν τῇ τῆς θεραπευτικῆς μεθόδου, μόνην εἰπεῖν τὴν μέθοδον, ἀλλ’ ἅμα παραδείγματι τῶν κατὰ μέρος ἑνί τε καὶ δευτέρῳ, προστεθῆναι δεῖ καὶ τὰ πείρᾳ προκείμενα φάρμακα, ἃ πρόσκειται τοῖς πρὸ ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ φαρμακευτικῷ μέρει τῆς τέχνης ἐνδόξοις, ἐπὶ τὰς κατ’ εἴδη διαφορὰς ἐπὶ τῶν μαλακτικῶν φαρμάκων ἀφίξομαι τὴν ἀρχὴν ἀπὸ τῶν μαλακωτάτων ποιησάμενος [959] αὐτοῖς, ἃ καὶ τὰς μικρὰς ἰᾶται φλεγμονάς.
english_sentence_A: [The differences and powers of emollient drugs according to kinds.] But since not all are such men, and since it is proposed in this treatise not, as in that of the Therapeutic Method, to state the method alone, but together with one or two examples of the particular cases, there must also be added the drugs that are established by experience, which are set down by those before us who are esteemed in the pharmaceutical part of the art;
english_sentence_B: [The differences by species, and the potencies, of emollient drugs.] But since not all are of this kind, and since what is proposed in this treatise is not, as in the Therapeutic Method, to state the method alone, but to state it together with an example of the particulars, one or a second, and the drugs established by experience must also be added, those set down by the men before us who were renowned in the pharmaceutical part of the art, I shall come to the differences by species among the emollient drugs, making my beginning from the mildest of them, which also cure small inflammations.

english_sentence_A: I shall therefore proceed to the differences according to kinds among the emollient drugs, making my beginning from the softest [959] of them, which cure even small inflammations.
english_sentence_B: One should use, as has been said before, for slight indurations and for soft bodies those of the first order; for bodies and affections stronger than these, those of the second; and likewise those of the third and of the fourth in proportion.

greek_sentence: χρῆσθαι δὲ προσῆκεν, ὡς προείρηται, πρὸς μὲν τὰς βραχείας σκληρότητας καὶ τὰ μαλακὰ σώματα τοῖς τῆς πρώτης τάξεως.
english_sentence_A: It is fitting to use, as has been said before, against slight hardnesses and soft bodies those of the first order; against bodies and affections stronger than these, those of the second, just as also those of the third and the fourth proportionately.
english_sentence_B: [Emollient drugs of the first order.] Butter or Colophonian resin and white wax that is not old, the three in equal weight, melted together, are emollients of the first order.

english_sentence_A: [That different differences in respect of more and less arise in the emollient plaster of Mnaseas according to the differing quantity, age and boiling of the simples.] For indeed in the second rank of the emollients one would not least place the plaster composed by Mnaseas, since all who have mentioned it agree with one another that it is made from old oil, litharge and pig's fat, but differ both in the quantity of each of these and in that some compose it from fresh fat, others from old fat, which is now customarily called by everyone axoungion.
english_sentence_B: [That various differences in respect of the more and the less arise in the emollient plaster of Mnasaeus, according to the differing quantity, age and boiling of the simple ingredients.] For in the second order of emollients one might quite justifiably place the plaster composed by Mnasaeus. All who have recorded it agree with one another that it is made of old oil, litharge and pig's fat.

greek_sentence: ἤτοι γὰρ ἴσα τῷ σταθμῷ καὶ μέτρῳ μίγνυται τὰ τρία καὶ πολλοί φασι τὴν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Μνασαίου συντεθεῖσαν ἐκ τριῶν ἴσων συγκεῖσθαι ἢ τὰ δύο μὲν ἴσα, τὸ τρίτον δὲ οὐκ ἴσον ἀλλ’ ἔλαττον ἢ πλέον ἢ τῶν τριῶν ἀνίσων μιγνυμένων.
english_sentence_A: For either the three are mixed in equal amounts by weight and measure—and many say that the one compounded by Mnaseas himself is composed of three equal parts—or two are equal and the third not equal but less or more, or the three are mixed in unequal amounts.
english_sentence_B: For either the three are mixed in equal amounts by weight and measure (and many say that the plaster composed by Mnasaeus himself consists of three equal parts), or two are equal and the third not equal but less or more, or the three are mixed unequal.

english_sentence_A: For when more litharge is put in, the drug will become milder in its power, and when less, stronger.

lsj_entry_text: μαλακ-τικός, ή, όν, emollient, χρίσματα Hp. Vict. 2.66 ; δύναμις Plu. 2.659c ; μ. οἶκος, of the outer chamber in a bath, Alex. Trall. Febr. 5 .
greek_sentence: ὡς εἴ γε τούτου μὴ φροντίζοι τις, ἀλλὰ ἴσῳ χρόνῳ τό θ’ ἧσσον ἔχον ἐλαίου κατὰ τὸ πλέον ἑψήσει, πρόδηλον ὅτι μαλακτικώτερον ἔσται κατὰ τὴν δύναμιν, ᾧ πλέον ἔλαιον μέμικται, καθάπερ εἰ καὶ ὠμήν τις ἄκοπον τὴν λιθάργυρον ἐλαίῳ μίξας βούλοιτο χρῆσθαι.
english_sentence_A: For if someone were not to attend to this, but were to boil for an equal time both that which has less oil and that which has more (κατὰ τὸ πλέον), it is obvious that the one with which more oil has been mixed will be more emollient in its power, just as if someone, having mixed raw litharge with oil, should wish to use it as an akopon.
english_sentence_B: So if someone pays no attention to this, but boils the preparation having less oil and the one having more for an equal time, it is evident that the one in which more oil has been mixed will be more emollient in its power, just as if someone should wish to use the litharge raw and unground, mixed with oil.

greek_sentence: διό περ ὃ πολλάκις ἤδη μοι λέλεκται, μεμνῆσθαι διὰ παντὸς αὐτοῦ κελεύω, μὴ καθάπερ ἔνιοι τὰς ἀποφάσεις ἁπλῶς ὑπὲρ τῶν φαρμάκων ποιοῦνται καὶ ἡμᾶς οὕτω πράττειν, βελτίονα λέγοντας ἁπλῶς εἶναι τήνδε τὴν σύνθεσιν τοῦ φαρμάκου τῆσδε.
english_sentence_A: Wherefore I bid you always keep in mind what has already often been said by me: that we should not, as some make their pronouncements about drugs without qualification, act in the same way ourselves, saying without qualification that this composition of a drug is better than that one.
english_sentence_B: For this reason I bid you always remember what I have often said already: that we should not, as some make their pronouncements about drugs without qualification, act in this way ourselves, saying without qualification that this composition of the drug is better than that one.

english_sentence_A: Accordingly, anyone who has first heard all these things now said by me, being not only industrious or retentive in memory but also intelligent by nature, will read with profit what has been written and what will be written by me with distinctions.

lsj_entry_text: μαλακ-τικός, ή, όν, emollient, χρίσματα Hp. Vict. 2.66 ; δύναμις Plu. 2.659c ; μ. οἶκος, of the outer chamber in a bath, Alex. Trall. Febr. 5 .
greek_sentence: ὥσπερ αὖ πάλιν, εἴ τινα ἴσην ᾤετο δύναμιν ἔχειν, αὐτὸ τοῦτο προσγράψαι, ἢ εἴπερ εὐλαβοῖτο κινδυνεύειν ἔν γε ταῖς τοιαύταις ἀποφάσεσιν, ἀλλὰ τά γε ἁπλᾶ μαλακτικὰ φάρμακα προδιδάξαι, τὸ μᾶλλόν τε καὶ ἧττον ἐν αὐτοῖς διορισάμενον, ὅπως ὁ ἀναγινώσκων ἐφεξῆς τὰς ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένας μαλακτικὰς ἐμπλάστρους πολλὰς, ἰσχυροτέραν μὲν εἶναι γνωρίζῃ τὴν διὰ στύρακος, ἀμμωνιακοῦ τε καὶ βδελλίου καὶ προπόλεως καὶ χαλβάνης, στέατός τε [966] ταυρείου καὶ τραγείου καὶ τῶν μυελῶν συγκειμένην, ἀσθενῆ δὲ τὴν μηδὲν τούτων ἔχουσαν, ἀλλ’ ἤτοι πάντα ἀσθενῆ κατὰ τὴν δύναμιν, ἢ τούτων μὲν αὐτῶν ἰσχυρότερα, μέσα δὲ ταῖς κράσεσί τε καὶ δυνάμεσιν ἢ μετὰ τοῦ μεμίχθαι τοῖς ἀσθενέσιν ἕν τι τῶν ἰσχυρῶν ἢ δύο.
english_sentence_A: just as, again, if he thought that some had an equal power, he should have added this very thing; or, if he were wary of running a risk in such pronouncements, he should at least have taught beforehand the simple emollient drugs, distinguishing the more and the less among them, so that the reader of the many emollient plasters written by him in sequence might recognise that the one composed of storax, ammoniac, bdellium, propolis and galbanum, of bull's [966] and goat's fat and of the marrows is stronger, while the one that has none of these is weak—but either all its ingredients are weak in power, or they are stronger than these themselves yet intermediate in their mixtures and powers, or one or two of the strong ones have been mixed in with the weak ones.
english_sentence_B: just as, again, if he thought that some had equal potency, he should have added this very fact in writing; or, if he was wary of running a risk in such pronouncements, he should at least have taught beforehand the simple emollient drugs, distinguishing the more and the less among them, so that one reading in sequence the many emollient plasters he wrote might recognise as stronger the one compounded of storax, ammoniac, bdellium, propolis and galbanum, and of [966] bull's and goat's suet and the marrows, and as weak the one containing none of these, but either ingredients all weak in potency, or ingredients stronger than these themselves but intermediate in their temperaments and potencies, or with one or two of the strong ingredients mixed in with the weak ones.

Il. 13.95 ; ν. ἀνήρ 23.589 : alone, νέοι youths, 1.463 , Hes. Sc. 281 , etc.: later mostly with Art., οἱ νέοι Ar. Nu. 1059 , etc.: prov., ὁ ν. ἔσται ν. 'boys will be boys', Lib. Ep. 910.3 ; οἱ ν., corporately organized, SIG 831.8 (Pergam., ii A.D.), etc.; opp. ἔφηβοι, παῖδες, ib. 589.38 (Magn.Mae., ii B.C.): opp. γέρων, ἠμὲν νέοι ἠδὲ γέροντες Il. 2.789 , etc.; ἢ ν. ἠὲ παλαιός 14.108 , cf. Od. 1.395 , etc.; opp. γεραίτερος, 3.24 ; opp. προγενέστερος, 2.29 ; opp. γεραιός, X. Lac. 1.7 ; εὐθὺς ἐκ νέου ἐθίζειν from youth upwards, Pl. Grg. 510d , etc.; ἐκ νέων παίδων Id. Lg. 887d ; ἐκ νέων ἐθίζεσθαι Arist. EN 1103b24 ; ἐκ νέας (sc. ψυχῆς) Pl. R. 409a ; τὸ ν., = νεότης , youth (in the abstract), S. OC 1229 (lyr.), E. ND 20 ; also, of minors, νέου ὄντος ἔτι Th. 1.107 ; cf. νεώτερος. rarely of animals and plants, ὄρπηκες, ἔρνος, Il. 21.38 , Od. 6.163 ; οἱ ν. τῶν νεβρῶν X. Cyn. 9.8 . suited to a youth, youthful, ἄεθλοι Pi. O. 2.43 ; ν. θράσος A. Pers. 744 (troch.); ν. φροντίς youthful spirits, E. EN 1095a6 ). new, fresh, ν. θάλαμος Il. 17.36 ; ν. ἄλγος 6.462 ; νέῳ . . κόλλοπι Od. 21.407 (this sense elsewh. in Hom. only in Adv. νέον, v. infr.); λίνον Alc. 15 (dub.); πόνοι . . νέοι παλαιοῖσι συμμιγεῖς κακοῖς A. english_sentence_A: Those, however, in which there is sensation, but faint, are treated by means of drugs which do indeed disperse the thickened humour, yet do not do this strongly and all at once, [993] as the discutient drugs do.
english_sentence_B: But those in which sensation is present, though faint, are treated by means of drugs that do, clearly, disperse the thickened fluid, yet do not do this strongly and all at once [993], as the discutient drugs do.

english_sentence_B: Menecrates did this because it often happens that errors are made in the writings not only by people acting unintentionally but also by some acting deliberately out of envy: they make the letter ο into θ by drawing another, transverse line through the middle of the round line, and alter the letter iota by adding another, likewise transverse, line; just as, when one line is scraped off from the letter [gamma?] and from rho, the result is that the character of iota is left.
